Art4Mental: Art, Technology and Mental Health Project (Poland, Ukraine)
ART4MENTAL, a Creative Europe-funded initiative exploring how immersive art and Virtual Reality can support mental well-being across Europe and Ukraine, is looking for 20 artists from Ukraine, Czech Republic, Estonia, Sweden and Austria who are curious about what happens when creativity meets mental health, technology and real human need.
The works will be used in real therapy sessions with patients and community groups across partner countries.
The project is seeking to support 20 artists (10+ from Ukraine and at least 1 from each EU partner country) who:
Are curious about the intersection of art, technology and healing;
Want to transform their practice into evidence-based therapeutic tools;
Are open to collaboration with mental health professionals and social care specialists to effectively deliver immersive art-therapy practices;
Believe that art can be transformative for individuals and communities.
What selected artists receive:
A sub-grant of up to 5,000 EUR for each artist
Professional training in VR and immersive technologies
A residency programme in the Carpathian mountains, Ukraine
Mentorship from experts in art, mental health and immersive tech
Participation in an international exhibition in Poland
The chance to see their work used in real therapy sessions across Europe and Ukraine
Deadline: 11 November 2026

IZOLYATSIA Foundation (UA) and Malý Berlín (SK) together with Trans Europe Halles (SE) announce the rolling open call for cultural and arts organisations within the ZMINA:Resilience project, strand "Support for international showcasing of co-creation projects".
The objective of this call is to support projects that bring artistic and cultural works co-created by Ukrainian and other Creative Europe cultural organisations to wider audiences through public showcasing and presentation events in Ukraine and across other Creative Europe countries.
Funding will be provided to projects featuring co-creations made by partnerships involving at least one organisation from Ukraine and at least one organisation from another Creative Europe country. The projects should maximise the visibility, audience reach, sustainability, and future showcasing potential of these works.
Supported projects are expected to include active partner cooperation to adapt showcased works to new audiences, for example by contextualising works, providing translation, involving local artists, experts and communities, conducting parallel programmes, and similar approaches.
All creative and cultural sectors are eligible except audiovisual.
Project Objectives
Showcase and tour co-creations that explore the theme of resilience in any arts or cultural sector except audiovisual.
Hold a minimum of 6 public presentation events: at least 3 events in each of at least two countries, one of which must be Ukraine (see FAQ, question 14).
The presentation events cannot take place in the home city or town of any of the applicant organisations.
Overall Strand Budget
Total funding available: 950,000 €
Grant amount: up to 50,000 €, covering up to 90% of total project costs.
The remaining 10% must be covered by the applicants as their own contribution in monetary form (not in-kind) and reflected in their accounting statements.
Expected number of grants: 19–25.
Rolling Call — Selection Rounds
This is a rolling call, open for 16 months, with deadlines every three or four months (see indicative timeline). Applications are reviewed and selected after every round deadline.
The rolling structure allows applicants to submit proposals for showcasing projects that are ready to go immediately, as well as those requiring more preparation time — including projects that received co-creation funding through earlier ZMINA:Resilience calls.
Who Can Apply?
Organisations working in the arts and culture sectors, registered in Creative Europe countries (EU countries and non-EU countries).
For Ukraine — registered in territories under the effective control of the Ukrainian government.
While proposals are submitted by a single lead applicant, the project must include at least two partner organisations from at least two countries, one of which is Ukraine. All partners have equal rights and joint responsibility for the correctness of data submitted on the platform and in future reporting.
The partnership must reflect genuine balance and exchange — not a formality. Each partner should play an equally important role, bring equal value, and contribute to reaching audiences in all participating countries.
Eligible Activities
All activities necessary for the preparation and delivery of the presentation events, including:
Public presentation events (in Ukraine, hybrid or online formats are accepted due to the security situation)
Preparation, rehearsals, and production activities related to the presentations
Travel for organisational, rehearsal, and presentation purposes
All projects must include at least 3 presentation events in each of at least 2 countries, one of which must be Ukraine (see FAQ, question 14). Presentation events cannot take place in the home city or town of any of the applicant organisations.
Eligible Costs
All costs necessary for the implementation of the project
Costs of presenting artistic and cultural works in each partner's country
Travel related to organisational, rehearsal, creative, and presentation purposes
All costs must be incurred after the grant agreement is signed and during the implementation period.

Funding Conditions

Double funding within the EU budget is not permitted.

📄 Draft subgrant agreement template
Project Duration
The implementation period is up to 7 months. The earliest start of implementation is after signing the grant agreement.
Technical Eligibility Criteria
All required attachments are uploaded in separate files in the formats specified for this call.
All required attachments follow standard templates available for download on the platform.
All required attachments are readable, accessible, and printable.
All project partners meet the eligibility conditions for this call.
The applicant's registration meets the conditions specified for this call.
The application form is complete and contains all requested information.
The application is submitted by the eligible lead applicant.
The subgrant amount requested does not exceed the maximum set for this call.
The total partner contribution meets the co-financing requirements.
The project implementation period is within the limits set for this call.
The project start date meets the conditions specified for this call.
Applications are checked for technical eligibility by the ZMINA:Resilience team. Proposals found admissible and eligible are forwarded to evaluators (2 per application).
Evaluation Criteria
Relevance:
Relevance of the project to the objectives of this call.
Quality:
Quality of the partnership — equal importance of the roles played by each partner.
Extent to which cross-cutting issues (digital dimension, environmental sustainability, inclusion) and barrier-free access to project results are addressed.
Scale of engagement — expected audience size and number of presentation events.
Impact:
Sustainability of the project, including plans for future showcasing and presentations beyond the grant period.
Selection Procedure
Applications are first reviewed for technical eligibility by the ZMINA:Resilience team to confirm compliance with all formal requirements, including eligibility and admissibility criteria.
Proposals that pass this stage are forwarded to two independent experts for evaluation. Evaluators assign scores, after which applications are ranked by average score.
Final selection is made by the Selection Committee, taking into account geographical, sectoral, and thematic diversity within the available call budget.
The application budget is assessed for cost-effectiveness and justification and may be adjusted prior to signing the grant agreement. The final grant amount is determined based on a combination of lump-sum units and actually incurred costs.
Due to the volume of applications received, the ZMINA:Resilience project team will not be able to provide individual justification for selection decisions. All decisions are final.
How to Apply
Via the IZOLYATSIA online platform, no later than 23:59 (Kyiv time) on the last day of the corresponding selection round.
The application is submitted by ONE representative of the consortium (the lead applicant).
Language of application: English.
Required Documents
The application package includes:
Application form and budget (filled in directly on the platform).
Supporting documents on capacity, eligibility, and admissibility — uploaded in .pdf format separately for each partner:
Scanned copy of the guarantee letter, completed and signed by the head of the organisation (template available for download on the platform).
Registration documents:
For organisations from Creative Europe countries other than Ukraine — national registration documents with an English translation if the original is in another language.
For organisations from Ukraine — a full extract from the Unified State Register of Legal Entities, Individual Entrepreneurs and Public Organisations, dated after the announcement of this call — in the original language.
Current Statute or equivalent document (if required for the legal entity) — all pages:
For organisations from Creative Europe countries other than Ukraine — with an English translation if the original is in another language.
For organisations from Ukraine — in the original language.
Note: The application form, the budget, the guarantee letter, other supporting documents, and any information the applicant provides to ZMINA:Resilience team are not the mere formality. Where those or any parts thereof are untrue, factually inaccurate, misleading, unfounded, misrepresent the facts, lack factual basis, and the like, providing support to the projects can be terminated at any stage of their lifecycle.

Ortaklaşa: EU-Türkiye Cultural Partnership Programme
Read this call in: 
Turkish
The Ortaklaşa EU-Türkiye Cultural Partnership Call for Proposals under the Ortaklaşa: Culture, Dialogue and Support Programme is open. The call will help foster arts- and culture-based cooperation networks among cities in Türkiye and Europe.
The Ortaklaşa EU-Türkiye Cultural Partnership Call for Proposals will bring together the local knowledge and experience of arts and culture organisations and municipalities in Türkiye and Europe through equal partnerships. The aim is for these collaborations to move beyond one-off project partnerships and develop into lasting relationships grounded in mutual learning, co-production and shared responsibility.
Projects supported under the Ortaklaşa EU-Türkiye Cultural Partnership Call are expected to strengthen the local cultural ecosystem in Türkiye while establishing lasting ties between cultural actors in Türkiye and Europe and creating a field of fair and sustainable cultural cooperation.
The project duration will be 9–12 months and it must be implemented primarily in Türkiye. Activities can include:
Activities with Impact on Policy-Making Processes in Arts and Culture
Artistic Production and Participatory Cultural Events
Capacity Building and Experience Sharing Activities
Infrastructure and Organisational Strengthening
Outreach, Visibility and Communication Activities
Within the scope of this call, applications are expected to be submitted through a four-institution cooperation structure consisting of:
A culture-oriented CSO based in Türkiye as the lead applicant,
A culture-oriented CSO based in an EU member state or candidate country (Albania, Iceland, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Kosovo or Serbia) as the partner,
One municipality from Türkiye as associates, and
One municipality from an EU member state or candidate country (Albania, Iceland, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Kosovo or Serbia) as associates.
The grant amount per project is between 60,000 EUR and 120,000 EUR. Grant support may cover between 70% and 95% of the projects’ total eligible costs.

Kiruna 2029 European Capital of Culture: Artistic Projects and Early Ideas (Sweden) 
Kiruna, Ice Hotel. Photo by Asaf Kliger/Ice Hotel 
Kiruna 2029 European Capital of Culture is calling for applications for large and medium-sized projects that can be led by an external organisation as part of the official artistic programme of Kiruna2029.
There are two main areas:
Test an Idea
Artistic Project
The European Capital of Culture is an initiative intended to invite everyone who wishes to engage, broaden perspectives, discover new ways to develop, and allow creativity and curiosity to bring us closer together. It is an opportunity to present something out of the ordinary.
In selecting projects to be included in the official artistic programme for Kiruna 2029, there are five criteria: Homemaking, European Adventure, Perspectives, Finding New Ways, and Power of Culture. These criteria serve as guiding principles in shaping the official programme and interweave the artistic concept with the goals formulated for the European Capital of Culture initiative in Kiruna 2029. They act as a support for those who wish to collaborate through artistic projects, as well as in the selection process for the official artistic programme 2029.
A project’s size can be defined based on several factors. These may include the project’s duration, financial scope, audience reach, or its strategic importance in delivering projects and achieving the objectives outlined in the Kiruna2029 Bid book.
Under this open call, Kiruna2029 can contribute up to 50% of the total project budget. There are no specific requirements regarding which project costs may be covered by funding granted by Kiruna2029.

Welcome - Välkommen - Bures boahtin - Tervetuloa - Tervetulu
Kiruna is the European Capital of Culture 2029
Look forward to world class culture all over our northern region when Kiruna is the Cultural Capital of Europe 2029!
This is what it means to become a European Capital of Culture
The European Capital of Culture is an initiative of the European Commission, a title awarded to two cities in different countries each year. The selected cities use the year, and the time leading up to it, to organise a series of cultural events that develop the local culture activities and promote European cooperation. The aim of the European Capital of Culture year is to contribute to the well-being of citizens and the development of the city. By highlighting cultural diversity and similarities, one aim is to contribute to mutual understanding between Europeans.
We want to use our year as European Capital of Culture, and the time leading up to it, to organize interesting cultural activities that can help create new memories for everyone throughout Kiruna Municipality. We want to enrich the cultural landscape in the region through culture-driven community development and increase Kiruna's international collaborations. We have a lot to share with the world, and to learn from Europe. We want to build pride in who we are and what we offer: our stories, our traditions and our Arctic way of dealing with contemporary challenges.
Our Story
Every night at 1:30 a.m. you hear a muted explosion underneath the city in Kiruna. The walls slightly vibrate and the water at your bedside vaguely ripples. It is the big underground mine, detonating a blast. The city of Kiruna is built on the biggest underground iron-ore mine in the world. But now the city is literally cracking up. Roads are breaking, the infrastructure of pipes in the ground is deforming and buildings can’t withstand the stress of the constant explosions anymore.
So, the city must move. And it’s happening right now. Some buildings are picked up on huge trailers and relocated, but most of them are demolished. Roads and traditional reindeer herding trails are cut off. The claws of the machines are eating away at the memories and years of life of the people day by day. Traditional ways of life are facing extinction. The movement causes conflicts about the rights of land, about our sense of self as two thirds of our population are being uprooted and have to move. It is clear that Kiruna is facing a time of significant challenges and opportunities. The new cityscape with impressive buildings, hotels, cafés and cultural venues are taking shape and gives us possibilities to start anew. A chance to rebuild our city and shape our surroundings. Maybe even ourselves. Not as we were, but into the future. To something more inclusive where more stories, cultural expressions and voices are given room to grow.
Our home has through history been described by others as an uninhabited wilderness and is often still talked about as a widespread wasteland with endless resources up for grabs. Through ignorant rethorics we are reduced to a mining city far out in nowhere. Nothing could be more wrong. Our land is highly rich in culture and has been the home for indigenous people and cultural groups for centuries. Geographically we are located in the heart of the Arctic. Kiruna is situated in Sápmi, the traditional homeland of the Sámi people and we are also part of Tornedalen, home for several minorities; Tornedalian, Kven and Lantalaiset, speaking different languages. For us living here, regardless of cultural heritage, the bond to nature is strong, the connection to all living things and ancestors is vital, precious and rooted in our ground. But now the ground is moving beneath our feet.
How do we find our soul, our character, our culture amidst all this movement? Where do we find ourselves when the dust from the big trucks rebuilding our city has settled? We want to make sure we build a vibrant and culturally rich community. A city and municipality where culture leads the societal transformation. Like many places in Europe’s countryside, we are facing a decreasing population trend that we need to change. This requires a cultural shift. We now have an opportunity to build something bright and colourful through culture that will reverberate with the history and heritage of the people who came before us, resonate with the people living here now, and attract the people who don’t live here — yet.
This is our story, our movement.
Welcome - Välkommen - Bures boahtin - Tervetuloa – Tervetulu!
Our Concept and Artistic Vision
Movement - Below ground, On earth, In space is our concept and is something that defines us, that runs through the veins of everyone living here, both historically and currently, regardless of culture or traditions. Our artistic vision is to share our strong and captivating stories, indigenous traditions and our Arctic take on contemporary challenges that affect all of Europe.
Kiruna/Giron/Kieruna/Kiiruna is a city of contrast and layers, where movement is part of everyday life. We invite you to share our stories, our traditions and our arctic way of meeting contemporary challenges with art and culture at its core.
The core of our artistic vision is to always apply a female gaze, keeping our young community involved and integrating perspectives from the indigenous Sámi people and Tornedalian cultures on their own terms. Making sure the artistic vision becomes reality, our strategy is that whenever you visit Kiruna, there will be an event going on, a cultural site to enjoy or a sensorial experience to be had, regardless of the time of year.
By working with local, national and international professionals, organisations and associations, we’ll be able to highlight the specific contrasts of Kiruna. With our vision and programme, we will raise sensitive topics around the city transformation, the right of land and rural exclusion. Through creative methods and artistic outlets we want to touch upon issues that create cracks and conflicts within ourselves and in our society, alongside with the joy and compassion that we have for one another and care for future generations, history and nature. We see the cracks appearing everywhere and we will use the movement as an opportunity for something new, vibrant and colourful to take place.
Open call - Artistic projects and early ideas
In the work of European Capital of Culture, we will enable different ways to participate in the official programme for Kiruna 2029 – which we present continuously on our social media channels.
Further down you find two links to online forms for submitting project proposals. If you have the seed of a project you would like to explore, choose the form Test an Idea. If you already have a project proposal ready, choose the form Artistic Project. The questions within the differens forms serve as support for you to reflect on how your project connects to Kiruna 2029, and for us to understand what kind of support you may need in a potential collaboration.
The European Capital of Culture is an initiative intended to invite everyone who wishes to engage, broaden perspectives, discover new ways to develop, and allow creativity and curiosity to bring us closer together. It is an opportunity to present something out of the ordinary – something that challenges and inspires. In selecting projects to be included in the official artistic programme for Kiruna 2029, we use five criteria, which you can find below. These criteria interweave the artistic concept with the goals outlined in our bidbook, the bidbook is also available on this website.
The last day to submit an application for an Artistic Project is October 31, 2026. The selection of project proposals will take place after this. Dialogues will be conducted both individually and in groups with project owners whose projects are selected for inclusion in the official programme for Kiruna 2029. These dialogues aim to integrate the projects into a broader context and facilitate knowledge-sharing and information about ongoing and future work. You find the timeline under FAQ section.
The form Test an Idea will be available until December 31, 2026.
If you have questions about how we work with shaping the artistic content, the selection process, or anything else related to European Capital of Culture Kiruna 2029, you are welcome to contact us. We recommend first browsing our website, here you can find useful information in the published texts and under the FAQ section for Project proposal. For this call, we do not hold individual meetings about specific project.

Criteria for Artistic projects
As part of the development of the artistic programme for Kiruna 2029, five criteria have been established – Homemaking, European Adventure, Perspectives, Finding New Ways, and Power of Culture. These criteria serve as guiding principles in shaping the official programme and interweave the artistic concept with the goals formulated for the European Capital of Culture initiative in Kiruna 2029. They act as a support for those who wish to collaborate through artistic projects, as well as in the selection process for the official artistic programme 2029.
Homemaking
Homemaking is about exploring how relationships and contexts can contribute to a sense of safety, belonging, and a sense of home.
In times of major transitions and uncertainty it becomes essential to create campfires where we can gather and share our worries and our hopes. Through art and culture, safe spaces can emerge, enabling us to process the often intangible aspects of change - a movement that begins within and, in encounter with others, makes us stronger together. By celebrating what is unique, highlighting what we share, and addressing both challenges and collective joys, our cultural roots intertwine to guide the way forward.
European Adventure
European Adventure is about sharing knowledge, collaborating across borders, and building new relationships with partners in Europe and beyond.
By learning from and with each another, artistic perspectives broaden, contributing to exchanges between artistic practitioners and fostering new audience encounters. Achieving a European dimension requires collaboration between artists, producers, creators, or entrepreneurs across different countries. At the same time, we place particular focus on strengthening cooperation with our neighbours in the Arctic, exploring questions that shape how we live and work in this region.

Busan Metropolitan City: Land and Ecological Art (South Korea) 
Read this call in: 
Korean
Busan Metropolitan City invites individuals and teams from around the world to propose a site-responsive work of land and ecological art for Eulsukdo, an estuarine island at the mouth of the Nakdong River, South Korea’s longest river.
Situated within a brackish estuary where the river meets the sea, Eulsukdo is an important stopover for migratory birds travelling along the East Asian–Australasian Flyway. The island was once heavily altered by agriculture, landfill and urban development, but it has since been restored as wetlands and migratory bird habitats. This layered history invites reflection on coexistence between human and more-than-human life.
The Open Call seeks original proposals that respond to Eulsukdo’s ecology, landscape, history and changing environment, while minimising ecological disturbance and demonstrating environmental responsibility throughout the work’s lifecycle.
The project will be completed and opened to the public from May to June 2027. No on-site construction or artwork installation is permitted during the peak migratory bird arrival period (November through February).
Individuals or teams who are professionally active in art, landscape architecture, architecture, design or related fields can apply. Interdisciplinary teams are welcome.
Support
Artwork Support: 380,000,000 KRW (Support covering all aspects of artwork production, implementation, installation, stays, etc.)
Artist fee: 20,000,000 KRW
Additionally, each artist/team invited to the second-round presentation review will receive a presentation honorarium of 1,000,000 KRW.

Open Call Theme
01
A Place Where Disappearance and Emergence Intersect
Brackish estuaries, where rivers meet the sea, support diverse forms of life and are among the environments most vulnerable to climate change. Their waterways, landforms, vegetation and living beings are in constant flux, while the landscapes we see today face the possibility of disappearance.
02
Fleeting Time and Deep Time
The theme begins with the contrast between the brevity of human time—which nevertheless leaves profound and lasting marks on the land—and the land’s deep ecological time, which has sustained life from the distant past to the present. “The Earth Endures” expresses a shared hope that the habitats we must protect, and the relationships they sustain, will endure intact for generations to come.
03
Site-Specific Land-Ecological Art
We invite site-specific works of land and ecological art that move beyond anthropocentric perspectives, reconsider human roles and responsibilities through ecological perspectives and timescales, and explore, through the language of art, the planetary interconnections between humans and non-human beings, nature and cities, and past and future.

About
Background & Aims
Eulsukdo lies in a brackish estuary where fresh water meets the sea. One of Korea’s major migratory bird habitats, it supports diverse forms of life. Although industrialisation, urban development and the Nakdong River Estuary Barrage significantly altered its environment, wetland and habitat restoration has helped revive its ecological vitality.
Now facing sea-level rise and biodiversity loss, Eulsukdo prompts renewed reflection on coexistence between humans and nature. Building on its ecological and historical context, this project uses art to foster environmental awareness and action, and to establish Eulsukdo as a hub for environmental art.
 Today View of Eulsukdo
Aim 01
Reinterpreting Coexistence between Humans and Nature
Moving beyond anthropocentric perspectives, the project considers ecosystems from more-than-human viewpoints and reinterprets the value of coexistence through land and ecological art.
Aim 02
Site-Specific Environmental Art
Reflecting Eulsukdo’s geographical and historical context, the project seeks creative, ecologically responsible works that explore sustainability in an age of climate crisis.
Aim 03
Art that Responds to Nature
Through installation projects that evolve and circulate with nature over time, the project proposes new possibilities for environmental art.
Aim 04
Establishing an Environmental Art Platform
The project strengthens the case for the Nakdong River Estuary’s designation as a National Urban Park and develops Eulsukdo as an international public cultural platform, promoting its ecological identity in Korea and beyond.
Aim 05
Revitalising Culture and Tourism in Western Busan
By creating a distinctive cultural destination that brings together the ecology and art of the Nakdong River Estuary, the project aims to foster local pride and broaden access to cultural experiences.
Eulsukdo
Nakdong estuary · Saha-gu, Busan
1966S
Eulsuldo, An Ecological Haven
Eulsukdo first appeared as an island on a cadastral map in 1916. Recognised for its international importance as a migratory bird habitat, it was designated Natural Monument No. 179 in 1966.
1970s — 1997
Ecological Degradation
From the 1970s onwards, the island’s ecosystem was degraded by the introduction of night-soil treatment, waste disposal and sewage treatment facilities. In particular, large-scale landfilling took place between 1993 and 1997.
1999 — 현재
Restoring the habitat
Eulsukdo was designated a Wetland Protection Area in 1999 and included in the Busan Coastal Special Management Area in 2000. As ecological restoration progressed, parks, visitor trails and cultural facilities were established, including the Nakdong Estuary Eco Center and the Museum of Contemporary Art Busan.
Ongoing
Pursuing Designation as a National Urban Park
Designation of the Nakdong River Estuary as Korea’s first National Urban Park is now being pursued to support its systematic conservation and restoration. Building on sustained efforts by Busan’s civil society since 1999, the National Urban Park system was established in 2016.

Slovenian
Artists, designers and researchers are invited to respond to the public call for participation in the Textile Art Biennial BIEN 2027, which will take place between 29 May and 14 August 2027 in Slovenian cities Kranj, Tržič, Škofja Loka, and Jesenice.
Artists and artist collectives from around the world may participate by submitting three works that are no more than three years old. Only online submissions will be considered.
Submitted works should be thematically aligned with the central theme, ‘Traces of Grace’, and should be primarily created in the medium of textiles or in a medium that references textiles through material, technique, or concept.
Textile Art Biennial BIEN bears the costs incurred in presenting the Exhibition, including insurance, promotion, publicity, previews, unpacking and repacking the artwork, additional installation costs.
Textile Art Biennial BIEN will award a residency in Kranj of up to 4 weeks in 2028 or 2029 to one selected artist (or an artist collective of up to two members), including coverage of travel expenses, accommodation, per diem, and production costs. The recipient of the award will be announced at the opening of BIEN 2027 in Kranj (29 May 2027). If the same person receives both the main award and the international ETA Award, the two awards will be combined.
The ETA Award is intended for young people under the age of 29 who demonstrate an exceptional use of textile craft techniques. The international award winner receives a two-week residency in Kranj, while the national award winner receives a one-week residency at the Lottozero textile laboratory in Prato, Italy.
Students and artists at risk are provided with a fee waiver.

Residency at BUDA with a premiere at NEXT Festival: Three weeks in October/November 2027
Furthering our commitment to provide conditions for new works to emerge and meet their audiences, we are continuing our partnership with Kunstencentrum BUDA and NEXT Festival in Belgium to offer a three-week residency for a performing artist from the Arab world. Using BUDA’s facilities and artistic support, the artist would finalize a new production and premiere their work at NEXT Festival at the conclusion of the residency. The partners will provide the selected artist (working with a maximum of three collaborators, i.e. up to four individuals in total) with their travel, visa costs, and per diem, a contribution to their project’s production costs, and the presentation fee for the performance.
Kunstencentrum BUDA in Kortrijk is a space for performing arts, an art house cinema, and one of the largest workspaces for performing arts in Belgium. Founded in 2006, BUDA constructs an artistic context in which the artist’s desire to create and learn is central. It offers time and space, customized support (logistic, technical, feedback), a network of artistic and professional contacts, and the possibility of an informal presentation for a test audience. BUDA co-organizes NEXT Festival.
NEXT Festival is a yearly, international cross-border dance, theatre, and performance festival founded in 2008 featuring works by renowned and young artists in more than 20 locations in and around Lille-Kortrijk-Tournai-Valenciennes cities. It is co-organized by five French and Belgian artistic houses and 18 associated partners. It is a collaborative endeavour and a landmark event for cultural and international artistic professionals. It brings together disciplines, communities, and cultures, encourages and facilitates intercultural dialogue amongst programmers, artists, festival organizers, students, and the broad public.
Previous artists invited to be part of NEXT festival through this partnership are Amina Aboulghar, Bint Mbareh, Nermin Habib, Nadim Bahsoun, Nagham Othman and Stephanie Kayal.
SPECIFIC ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA
In addition to complying with the general eligibility criteria that you can read here, please note the following:
Applicants must have developed and presented previous works.
Applicants must be working on a new and original project.
Applicants must be working with contemporary forms of performance (classical theatre, community theatre, and classical western dance such as ballet and so forth are not eligible).
Proposals for concerts are not eligible for this call.
Unconventional projects dealing with experimental forms and/or concerned with progressive discourses are encouraged to apply.
Unsuccessful applicants to previous editions are eligible to re-apply.
Applicants must have advanced and be in the final development phase of their projects by September 2027 and have confirmed co-producers and/or a financing plan, as this residency only partially contributes to the production costs.
PROCESS
The applications will be assessed by Mophradat and the final selection will be made in collaboration with BUDA and NEXT.
Preselected applicants will be contacted for a conversation sometime in February 2027.
All applicants, whether selected or not, receive a response to their applications by March 1, 2027.
Only one application can be selected.
Due to a high volume of applications and the confidentiality of the selection process, Mophradat cannot provide individual feedback explaining the reason an application was not selected.
Upon selection, the resident will sign separate agreements with Mophradat, BUDA, and NEXT.
The partners will support the selected applicant through the necessary visa applications; and if the artists are unable to travel due to visa refusals, the project will be compensated.
The partner covers travel and visa costs as well as residency per diems, in addition to coproduction costs, and a presentation fee for the performance at NEXT Festival for an overall amount of 10,000 euros, all included.
A short-written report of the resident’s experience must be submitted to Mophradat within two weeks of the residency’s end.
APPLICATION
Please note that the application form online, can neither be saved nor revisited. It may only be filled out and submitted at once. To help you prepare for your application, you may check out the expected questions here.
Any material sent by email will not be considered.
If you are interested in being considered for this residency, please fill out the form here and make sure you answer all parts of the questions. Please be aware that we want to get to know you through this application process and don’t evaluate applications based on writing ability, so we are not interested in reading any AI generated answers.

Greek
The International Mute Photo Festival (IMPhF) 2027 is calling for submissions made on children’s thermal printer camera in the theme ‘Nature ate the pixels’. The exhibition will be held in Karlovasi, Samos, Greece, in July 2027.
In an era dominated by digital mediation, IMPhF 2027 invites photographers to rekindle a silent dialogue between Humanity and Nature. The festival seeks images that capture a resilient coexistence, moments where human presence embeds within the landscape, or where nature triumphantly reclaims its space.
The exclusive capturing medium for this open call is children’s thermal printer camera. The open call redefines an accessible toy into a powerful tool for contemporary artistic creation, embracing imperfection, organic forms, and low-resolution intimacy.
Thematic categories are:
Landscape
Symbiosis
Rebirth
Future
It is open to photographers of all levels (6–9 images), as well as children and youth under 18 years old (5 images). The jury will select the top 15 photographic series from the Adult Category and the top 5 photographic series from the Children & Youth Category.
For selected projects, the festival will fully cover all production and printing costs to produce enlarged prints of the submitted digital scans. The festival will cover travel and accommodation expenses for the artist who submits the most complete photographic series, enabling them to attend the exhibition opening.
Deadline: 30 April 2027

Read this call in: 
French, German
The Fondation François Schneider announces the launch of the call for applications for the 16th edition of its Talents Contemporains competition on the theme of Water.
Initiated in 2011, the competition aims to explore European and international art scenes and build a collection of unique works centred on the theme of water. Today, the art centre’s collection brings together artists from diverse backgrounds, whether graduates of recognised art schools or self-taught.
For the winners, the financial grant is accompanied by concrete support. The competition acts as a career springboard, offering artists institutional recognition, targeted promotional support, and broad exposure for their work through exhibitions and events at the regional, national, and international levels.
There will be an exhibition of the works in winter 2028 at the Fondation François Schneider’s art centre in Wattwiller.
The competition is for artists (of legal age) of any nationality. Eligible artistic disciplines are: painting, drawing, sculpture, textiles, installation, photography, video, and other visual and fine arts. he work must be a unique piece. Exception for photography and video only: if the work is an editioned/multiple piece, the prize money varies.
Artists working in sculpture or installation have the specific option to apply either with an existing artwork or with a project proposal to be produced. In this second case only, a detailed production budget may be allocated, up to a maximum of 50,000 EUR.
Grant
15,000 EUR per winner for the acquisition of their work by the Fondation (or 8,000 EUR if the photographic or video work exists in multiple editions)
Inclusion in a group exhibition at the art centre in Wattwiller
Bilingual booklet
Video portrait
All travel costs are also covered for attending the exhibition (as well as accommodation, etc.)

Water
Inaugurated in 2013 in the former bottling plant of the Wattwiller springs, the François Schneider Foundation’s Art Centre is a unique venue entirely dedicated to the theme of water. Every year, through temporary exhibitions and cultural projects, this vital element is explored across all its facets: artistic, poetic, aesthetic, geographic, political, and scientific.
Since its launch in 2011, the Talents Contemporains competition dedicated to the theme of water has honored numerous international artists, thereby building a singular and highly original institutional collection of contemporary art.
View the collection
Guidelines and eligibility
The competition is open to visual artists of all nationalities who are of legal age.
Profile: Applicants must demonstrate a solid professional artistic background and/or hold a degree from an art school. To be eligible, candidates must provide evidence of a recent and continuous track record over the past five years through several exhibitions (solo and/or group), publications (monographs, catalogues), or artist residencies.
Eligible Disciplines: Painting, drawing, sculpture, installation, photography, video, textile art, or any other form of fine and visual arts. Note: Performing arts and music are not accepted.
Artwork Specifications: The submitted artwork (whether it consists of a single piece or a body of work) must focus exclusively on the theme of water. Each candidate may submit only one artwork or project per year.
Existing Artwork / Project to be Produced:
Existing Artworks (All disciplines): For painting, drawing, photography, video, textile art, as well as completed sculptures and installations (unique pieces), only the existing artwork can be submitted. No additional production budget will be allocated for these proposals.
Creative Projects (Sculpture and Installation only): Artists working in sculpture or installation have the specific option to apply either with an existing artwork or with a project proposal to be produced. In this second case only, a detailed production budget may be allocated, up to a maximum of €50,000.
Multiple Artworks (Editions): The submitted artwork may be part of a limited edition series for video and photography. If the proposed artwork includes multiple editions, the final grant structure differs and is reduced to €8,000.
Competition Process
Artists are invited to submit their proposals based on the theme of water—whether realistic or utopian, figurative or abstract—by bringing a unique and sensitive perspective to this subject.
Selection of Artworks and Projects
Four Expert Committees and an International Grand Jury will convene successively:
The Expert Committees
Four expert committees, composed of gallerists, art critics, curators, and past competition winners, form pairs to review 200 applications each and shortlist the finalists. The roughly thirty finalist applications are then presented to the Grand Jury.
The International Grand Jury
Chaired by Jean-Noël Jeanneney, this Jury will select 4 to 7 Talents Contemporains laureates from among the thirty finalists. Their artworks will be acquired by the Foundation.
Jean-Noël Jeanneney, Former President of Radio France, former Secretary of State, and former President of the Bibliothèque nationale de France – Paris (France)
Constance de Monbrison, Head of the Insulinde Collections, Musée du Quai Branly – Jacques Chirac – Paris (France)
Alfred Pacquement, Honorary General Curator of Heritage – Paris (France)
Ernest Pignon-Ernest, Artist – Paris (France)
Roland Wetzel, Director of the Museum Tinguely – Basel (Switzerland)
Rosa Maria Malet, Director of the Fundació Joan Miró from 1980 to 2017, Member of the Board of Directors of the Fundació Miró – Barcelona (Spain)
Chiara Parisi, Director of Centre Pompidou-Metz (France)
NB: The composition of the expert committees and the Grand Jury is subject to change based on member availability.
Timeline
September to November: Online call for applications period.
December to February: Review of applications and shortlisting of approximately thirty finalists by the Expert Committees.
March: Official announcement of the finalist artists.
May/June: Deliberations of the International Grand Jury and announcement of the winners.
Autumn (Year N+1): Major group exhibition of the winners at the Wattwiller Art Centre, featuring video portraits of the laureates.
The Prize Grant
For each edition, the International Grand Jury designates a maximum of 7 laureates.
Each winner receives a grant of €15,000 as a merit-based prize and for the official acquisition of their artwork, which then joins the collection of the François Schneider Foundation. (In the case of photographic or video works involving multiple editions, the grant is fixed at €8,000).
The Foundation covers all costs related to the production of the winners’ exhibition at the Wattwiller Art Centre (see rules and regulations).
How to Apply?
Participation in the competition can only be done electronically after registering on the François Schneider Foundation website by clicking the Individual registration or Collective registration buttons at the top of this page.
Applications must be written in French for French-speaking candidates and in English for all other candidates.
Applications must strictly include:
Administrative Section
Registration form and signed, approved Rules and Regulations (PDF format).
A copy of your valid ID (recto/verso ID card or passport) (PDF format).
Artistic Section (Completed artwork or project to be produced, sculpture or installation)
Your CV and/or a presentation of the artists’ collective, demonstrating a professional artistic background (work recently exhibited in institutions, galleries, festivals, etc., or participation in artist residencies) (PDF format, maximum 2 pages).
Your portfolio/artistic dossier presenting an overview of your work (PDF format, maximum 20 A4 pages, maximum 30 MB).
A statement of intent presenting the artwork or project and the artist’s conceptual and creative approach for the competition (PDF format, maximum 2 pages).
A detailed technical specification sheet of the existing artwork or project (sculptures, installations), indicating title, materials, technique, dimensions, weight, constraints, and technical means required for exhibition, installation, or transport (PDF format, maximum 1 page).
A detailed production budget up to a maximum of €50,000 for artworks submitted as project proposals for sculptures and installations (PDF format).
3 to 5 color visuals (photo, drawing, diagram, 3D modeling, floor plan, etc.) (JPG format, maximum 5 MB per visual).
A video excerpt for video works. Video footage may also be attached for other types of artwork (painting, sculpture, etc.) to contextualize them (MOV/MP4 format, maximum 4 GB).
NB: The jury will particularly appreciate clear, concise applications and proposals that align cohesively with the collection of the François Schneider Foundation.
Incomplete applications or those failing to comply with the above instructions will not be submitted to the Expert Committees or the International Grand Jury.
In the event of technical difficulties related to the internet connection, candidates should contact the Organizer as soon as possible. We strongly encourage you to submit your application well in advance to avoid server slowdowns that could prevent your submission from reaching us on time.
IMPORTANT: Under no circumstances should the submitted artworks be designed with the intention of being permanently installed at the Foundation.

About 200 works, selected from the competition, will be exhibited at Ceramics Park MINO in Tajimi City, Gifu Prefecture from 8 October to 7 November 2027.

Works cannot have selected in other public competitions
The size, weight, and shape of the work must not interfere with its transportation or indoor exhibition (the guideline is a floor space of 4 ㎡ or less, a height of 4m or less, and a weight of 100kg or less)

Gold Award: 2,000,000 JPY (1 work)

Artist Residencies
Rencontres de la jeune photographie internationale 
From 02 September 
 To 15 November
The Encounters of Young International Photography Artist Residency takes place in Niort, in the Nouvelle-Aquitaine region (France). Niort is located on the edge of the Marais Poitevin, near the Atlantic coast, between Nantes and Bordeaux.
Every year, the Artist Residency welcomes emerging international photographers with a wide variety of approaches, selected based on their portfolios. This year, they will be mentored throughout their stay by the duo Simon Brodbeck and Lucie de Barbuat.
They receive technical support from the team at La Villa Pérochon—a center for contemporary photographic art managed by the association Pour l’Instant—as well as from two printers at the Picto lab (through a skills-based sponsorship). A technical facility, equipped with professional gear including a black-and-white film darkroom and a digital workshop, is reserved exclusively for them. With this support, the photographers are invited to create and experiment. This is a true carte blanche, fueled by encounters, exchanges, and the sharing of experiences drawn from each participant’s very different backgrounds. It is a unique artistic experience! 
Artist Residency dates: March 26 through April 12, 2027 (inclusive)
The selection jury will be chaired by Simon Brodbeck and Lucie de Barbuat and will include prominent figures from various fields of contemporary photography (documentary, fine art, etc.). The Artist Residency is open to six emerging international photographers, regardless of age or background, and across all artistic styles. For logistical reasons, only individual applications will be accepted.
Practical information
Artist Residency from March 26 to April 12, 2027.
Application deadline: November 15, 2026 (inclusive).
Apply using the form below. Applications submitted by any other means (email, mail, etc.) will not be considered. 
Artist Residency Requirements
Expenses covered: round-trip travel from home, supplies needed for the creative process, lodging, breakfast, and dinner.
Compensation: a 400-euro Artist Residency grant + 400 euros in exhibition fees for the exhibition at the end of the Artist Residency.
During the Artist Residency, the artists-in-residence agree to produce works that will make up the exhibition marking the end of the Artist Residency, to be held from April 10 to May 31, 2027, at the Bernard d’Agesci Museum in Niort.
Simon Brodbeck and Lucie de Barbuat
Brodbeck & de Barbuat (Simon Brodbeck and Lucie de Barbuat) are an artist duo who work with photography and video. Since 2005, their work has explored the concepts of landscape, memory, and perception, blending a conceptual approach with a poetic dimension. Playing with space-time and light, they create images in which reality constantly engages with the imagination. Attentive to the history of photography and the evolution of technology, they regularly incorporate experimental or hybrid practices to explore how these innovations transform our relationship with images and our daily lives.
Residents at the Villa Medici from 2016 to 2017, they are graduates of the École nationale supérieure de la Photographie in Arles and the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales. They are recipients of the national photography commission Image 3.0 (Jeu de Paume / CNAP), the Prix Jeune Création, the HSBC Prize for Photography, and the Images Vevey Festival.
Their work has been featured in solo exhibitions at the Fotomuseum in Antwerp, the Maison Européenne de la Photographie, the Villa Medici, and the Institut français du Japon, as well as in group exhibitions including the Rencontres d’Arles, the Arsenale in Venice, the Cairo Biennale, the Thessaloniki Museum of Photography, and the Mucem in Marseille, among others. 
Both are guests of honor at the 2027 Encounters of Young International Photography.
SUBMIT YOUR APPLICATION
The application package must include:
A biography and a resume
A portfolio showcasing the two most representative series of your previous work
A statement of intent explaining what you would like to do during the Artist Residency or, at the very least, what you expect from it. The project does not need to be very detailed, but it must demonstrate that it is feasible within the allotted time (about ten days). 
Application deadline: November 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m.

When sending your files, please follow the naming convention below:
Portfolio: RJPI27_NAME_PORTFOLIO.pdf
Resume: RJPI27_NAME_CV.pdf
Statement of Intent: RJPI27_NAME_NOTE.pdf
Your files must be submitted exclusively in PDF format, and their names must be written in all capital letters, without accents.

Kuldīga invites Europe to reimagine democracy: applications open for the international Democracy Residency “European Dream”
 15. October, 2026
Copy Link
The Democracy Foundation, based in Kuldīga, Latvia, invites applications for the international Democracy Residency “European Dream”, organised as part of the Liepāja – European Capital of Culture 2027 programme. The residency will take place in Kuldīga in August 2027.
Six participants from different fields and European countries will be selected to bring together diverse experiences, knowledge and skills, and to explore new, unexpected and meaningful ways not only to talk about democracy, but to experience it.
“Democracy can sometimes feel like something that belongs in parliamentary chambers and official documents. During the residency, it will move beyond these formal settings and into the city, becoming part of people’s everyday lives. We are interested in one central question: how can democracy be made tangible? How can we explore participation, power, trust, difference and the challenges of living together in ways that speak not only to the mind, but also to emotions, imagination and the body? We are not looking for ready-made solutions to the challenges facing democracy today. What matters most is curiosity, a willingness to experiment and collaborate, and the ability to turn personal experience into something others can take part in,” emphasise the organisers.
Over the course of three weeks, residents will develop activities to be included in the programme of the Kuldīga Democracy Festival. These might take the form of a game, workshop, performance, a new format for conversation or participation, or something that does not yet have a name. We are looking for ideas that invite festival visitors to become active participants rather than simply spectators. The festival will take place at the end of the residency, on 20–21 August 2027.
People from a wide range of fields, places and backgrounds are invited to apply – civic activists, artists, researchers, journalists, educators, designers, architects, athletes, entrepreneurs, social workers, chefs, programmers, marketing and communication professionals, and people from many other walks of life. Residents will be encouraged to develop activities together, although individual work will also be possible. Local people will be involved in the planning and development process, creating opportunities for experiences from across Europe to meet local perspectives from Kuldīga.
Each of the six participants will receive accommodation in Kuldīga’s Old Town and a EUR 1,000 stipend to cover everyday expenses during the residency. In addition, each participant will have access to a separate budget of up to EUR 1,000 for developing and implementing their activity.
The selection process will take place in two stages. Applications will first be reviewed, and shortlisted applicants will be invited to an online interview.
Following the interviews, six residents will be selected. When forming the group, we will consider not only the quality of the applications and the potential of the ideas, but also the diversity of the participants – including their professional backgrounds, countries, ages, genders and other aspects. Democracy depends on hearing different voices, and the residency therefore aims to bring together people with a broad range of experiences and perspectives.

Applications open until November 15, 2026

Residency dates: 3–23 August 2027
Location: Kuldīga, Latvia

Who can apply: Residents of European countries (not limited to EU Member States)

Budget for activity development and implementation: Up to EUR 1,000 per participant

Description
Lauched in 2024 to support young emerging artists, the Sixi International Artist-in-Residence Project is committed to facilitating exchanges between artists from different backgrounds and helping them achieve creative breakthroughs and personal growth in their creative work. 
The Sixi AiR Project will provide living and working space, as well as financial support and other necessary assistance. By the end of the residency period, artists will also have the opportunity to showcase their outcomes in exhibitions. 
Nanjing is a distinctive Chinese city that combines traditional and contemporary culture, where contemporary art is vibrant in the midst of its rich history. As one of the few local art residency programmes, the Sixi AiR Project hopes to provide artists with the opportunity to engage in dialogue with the city, and to make its contributions to the international cultural exchanges in Nanjing and the diversified development of the art ecology in contemporary China.

TRACES: Residency at Laboratory for Energy Materials for Visual Artists 2027 (Switzerland)
Read this call in: 
French
TRACES (Transdisciplinary Research in Arts, Creation & Sciences) is a new international Art & Science residency programme based on the Energypolis campus in Sion, Switzerland.
For its pilot edition, TRACES invites an international visual artist to spend three months in dialogue with the Laboratory for Energy Materials of Prof. Sascha Feldmann (EPFL) from 11 January to 18 April 2027, with a public presentation on 15 April 2027.
The lab explores how light and matter interact to design the next generation of ‘soft’ semiconductors, used in flexible solar cells, energy-efficient displays and quantum technologies. The residency is run by the FDDM in partnership with EPFL-Valais, Energypolis SA, the City of Sion and the Canton of Valais.
The residency is open to established, professional international visual artists. Applicants must have specialised training or equivalent experience, as well as recognition in their field demonstrated by public presentations of their artistic work. A minimum of two years of professional practice is required. Applicants must be at least 25 years old and have completed their studies at least two years ago.
Support:
A stipend of CHF 2,000 per month
Accommodation in Sion
Travel costs (up to 1,500 CHF)
A production budget
Access to the lab and to scientific mentoring
Deadline: 22 November 2026

Call for international artistic project
Résidence Art & Science 
For its pilot phase, TRACES invites an international visual artist
 to engage in dialogue with the Laboratory for Energy Materials of Prof. Sascha Feldmann
(EPFL), on the Energypolis campus in Sion (Valais, Switzerland).
This residency offers the selected artist privileged access to a
cutting-edge research environment on the energy materials of tomorrow,

TRACES_OPENCALL_FR
TRACES_OPENCALL_UK
TRACES 
Transdisciplinary Research in Arts, Creation & Science
"Art and
science are two branches of the same tree." 
Albert Einstein
TRACES is an Art&Science residency program supported by the Foundation
for the sustainable development of mountain regions (FDDM) in Switzerland, in
partnership with EPFL-Valais,
Energypolis SA, the City of Sion, and the Canton of Valais.
TRACES aims to strengthen the links between
arts, sciences, and society in the context of the development of the Energypolis Campus in Sion, Switzerland. 
The program seeks to
promote collaborations between artists and researchers through
residencies, cultural and scientific events, as well as mediation actions. The project explores new forms of interdisciplinary creations
and makes scientific issues accessible to the public.
TRACES ART & SCIENCE @ ENERGYPOLIS
At a Glance
Application
Terms and Conditions
Duration of the residency: 3 months 11.01.2027 - 18.04.2027
Location: Sion, Valais, Switzerland
Artistic grant: 2,000 CHF per month
Housing and travel expenses covered
Qualifications
Confirmed and professional international visual artist
At least 25 years old 
Minimum 2 years of professional practice 
International 
Main working language: English
Selection criteria
Quality and uniqueness of the artistic approach.
Relevance and originality of the proposed dialogue with the laboratory’s research.
Feasibility of the proposal within the allotted time and space.
The artist’s ability to engage in a collaborative process with a scientific team. process with a scientific team.
The proposal’s value for public outreach and engagement.
The Scientific Partner
The partnership with the Laboratory for Energy Materials of theEPFL Valais-Wallis anchors this pilot edition
in the themes of energy transition, sustainability and future
materials. The laboratory's research explores the interactions between light and matter to design the
next generation of "soft" semiconductors — materials at the heart
of flexible solar cells, highly energy-efficient
screens, and emerging quantum technologies.
Since 2024, the laboratory has been led by Professor Sascha Feldmann, who studied chemistry at Heidelberg University and then physics at the University of Cambridge. He earned a highly acclaimed Ph.D. on hybrid perovskites. He then became a Rowland Fellow at Harvard University, where he developed ultrafast spectroscopy techniques to study light-matter interactions. His work has earned him several international honors, including an ERC Starting Grant, the Wiley Young Innovator Award, and a spot on the “C&EN Talented 12” list.
The thematic framework
The laboratory's research opens a rich imagination between chemistry and physics. The very title
of the program — TRACES — invites us to think about what materials, light, or energy leave
as traces, memories, or futures.
Candidates are invited to formulate
a proposal resonating with one or more of these open questions:
How to make sensitive what escapes
perception — the transformation of light into
energy, phenomena at the scale of
materials?
What forms, what narratives, or
what experiences can arise from the dialogue between visual creation and
energy materials science?
All disciplines of visual arts are
welcome (installation, sculpture, digital media,
visual performance, photography, etc.). The proposal does not
need to be finalized at the application stage: the jury will assess the relevance
of the dialogue with the scientific laboratory and the originality of the overall
approach of the artist.
The partners
The FDDM
Since 1999, The FDDM has contributed to making Valais an exemplary and sustainable territory. Born from the joint will of the State of Valais and the City of Sion, the foundation supports, assists, and raises awareness among the Canton, municipalities, schools, businesses, and citizens who wish to have a positive and concrete impact on Valais, now and for future generations.
ENERGYPOLIS SA
Rooted in a creative and inspiring Valais, Energypolis brings together research, training, and innovation within the same ecosystem, designed to foster impactful solutions.
EPFL Valais-Wallis
With its 19 active laboratories in the key areas of energy, environment, and health, managed by researchers and doctoral students from 40 nationalities, the Valais campus, solidly integrated into the Energypolis project, fully plays its role in favor of research and innovation in the heart of the Alps.

Culture Moves Europe: Call for Individual Mobility 2026–2027
Culture Moves Europe promotes cultural and artistic mobility by supporting individual mobility and residency projects across all Creative Europe countries. The project is funded by the Creative Europe programme of the European Union and implemented by the Goethe-Institut. The Individual Mobility supports artists and cultural professionals to carry out a project with a partner of their choice in a Creative Europe country which is not their country of residence. The partner can be an individual or an organisation. It is possible to apply either as an individual or as a group of up to five people.
The project must follow two of the following objectives: to learn, to create, to explore, or to connect. The project must be between 7 and 60 days in length (for individuals) or between 7 and 21 days (for groups). Applicants must be active in one of the following sectors: Architecture, Cultural Heritage, Design and Fashion Design, Literature, Music, Performing Arts, and Visual Arts.
Applicants can only receive one individual mobility grant between October 2025 and July 2028.
It is open to artists and cultural professionals, who are:
legally residing in one of the Creative Europe countries, including the overseas countries and territories and outermost regions
18 years of age or older
active in one of the following sectors: architecture, cultural heritage, design and fashion design, literature, music, performing arts, and visual arts; No specific level of experience is required
The grant provides:
A daily allowance of 85 EUR per day
Travel allowance (400 EUR for distances under 5,000 km, 800 EUR for greater distances)
Top-ups such as green mobility (400 EUR), overseas or outermost region top-up (175 EUR), family top-up (200 EUR per child), visa top-up (120 EUR)
Accessibility support is offered at 30 EUR per day (for personal assistance or sign-language interpretation)
The Call for Individual Mobility 2025-2026 is a rolling call with monthly deadlines. Applicants will be notified of the result up to 8 weeks after the monthly deadline.

Create an account

Complete the application form

Evaluation and selection

It will consider the evaluator’s score, the project’s duration, as well as other criteria such as geographical and sectoral balance, and other inclusion aspects.

Hordaland Kunstsenter is currently accepting applications from artists based in the Nordic and Baltic countries to participate in their residency programme for 2027/ 2028.
Hordaland Kunstsenter supports a wide range of artistic practices, and they do not privilege any single medium or way of working. Since their founding, they have hosted and supported projects spanning exhibition-making, performance, sound, publishing, moving image, socially engaged and participatory practice, as well as research-based and discursive formats that unfold over time. Residency period is for two months (four separate residency periods are available: Spring 2027 / Fall 2027 / Winter 2027 / Spring 2028).
It is expected that the resident artist shares their research and offers insights into their practice through a public presentation / talk at Hordaland Kunstsenter during their stay. The format of this is not a fixed one, and is made in dialogue with the residency coordinator.
The residency is open to artists with a permanent address in the Nordic region (Sápmi, Denmark, Finland, Faroe Islands, Greenland, Iceland, Sweden, Åland) or the Baltic countries (Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania), with the exception of Norway. It is not open to full-time students or artists currently enrolled in an artistic PhD programme.

Connections to relevant studios/production networks in Bergen based on the artist’s needs

European Hybrid Intelligence Network: Dirtly Lab Residencies 2027 (Belgium, Croatia, Germany, Serbia, Slovenia, Spain)
EHIN (the European Hybrid Intelligence Network) has announced its Open Call for Artists’ Residencies. This programme brings together artists, scientists and field practitioners to explore hybrid intelligence, embedded between different species and in living systems, and biocomputing as a creative and ecological alternative to energy-intensive, silicon-based technologies.
EHIN is a programme designed to support six artists through a two-phase, cross-institutional residency, running for approximately 12 months per artist, starting from February 2027.
Through six Dirtly Lab residencies, hosted by six partner institutions across Europe, EHIN offers artists the opportunity to develop a new artwork in direct collaboration with scientists in the field of hybrid intelligence and bio-computation and a local field practitioner (such as a herbalist, farmer, or ecologist), supported by dedicated production teams and access to specialised infrastructure.
Each residency pairs 1 artist + 1 scientist/expert + 1 field practitioner. The six host partners are: Kersnikova Institute (Slovenia), CPN (Serbia), GLUON (Belgium), LABoral (Spain), ZKM (Germany), and KONTEJNER (Croatia)
Each residency includes at least 2 Open Dirty Labs of public engagement activities, sharing the artistic and scientific process with local communities.
Support includes the following:
Up to 25,000 EUR budget per residency, covering artist fee and production costs

Open call
Exploring hybridintelligence through the shared agency of morethanhuman world.
Application deadline:
4 December 2026, 23:59 CET
European Hybrid Intelligence Network brings together artists, scientists, and environmental practitioners to study how living organisms generate, exchange, and respond to information within natural ecosystems.
Through biocomputing and collaborative inquiry, EHIN approaches biological processes not merely as technological alternatives to silicon computing, but as a way to understand ecological interdependence and interspecies communication. We invite you to step into real world environments, examine multi-species relationships, and develop new artistic narratives rooted in ecological knowledge.
We are offering six distinct residency partners, each providing a unique environment and framework for interdisciplinary collaboration, fieldwork, and experimentation.

Guide for applicants

Fellowship hosting institution
CPN
Center for the Promotion of Science (CPN)
Location city & country
Belgrade, Serbia
Residency characteristics /
info on the host institution:
The Center for the Promotion of Science (CPN) has broad experience in the art–science collaborations, public engagement and the design and development of interdisciplinary projects, with its art+science programme established in 2014 which encompasses annual festival since 2016.
The selected artist will have access to CPN’s makerspace and prototyping facilities, including a range of production and digital fabrication tools. The guidance will provide local Residency Expert Group, whose expertise spans bioinformatics, biological signal processing, neuroengineering and computational systems. Depending on the needs of the artistic project, CPN can involve additional research institutions and experts, including the Institute of Botany and Botanical Garden “Jevremovac”, the Institute of Molecular Genetics and Genetic Engineering, the Centre for Data Processing, etc.
These collaborations will be developed according to the research direction and practical needs of the selected project. We are particularly interested in artists working across disciplines, open for potential collaborations with local scientists, practitioners and communities; previous experience in community-based work is an advantage!
English is sufficient for the residency, while Serbian/BHS may be useful but it isn’t required.
The residency will support the development and production of a new, exhibition-ready artwork.
Biocomputing expert(s) involved
Andrej Savić
Andrej M. Savic is a Scientific Advisor at the University of Belgrade - School of Electrical Engineering, with sixteen years of research experience in neurosciences and neurotechnology. Collaboration with Andrej offers scientific mentorship grounded in direct experience with biological signal’s reading and interpretation, including how to think about interfaces between living systems, and how machine learning can be used to find structure in complex biological data.
Marko Mišić
Marko Mišić received his BSc degree in 2007, his MSc degree in 2010, and his PhD in 2017 in the field of computer engineering and informatics, all from the University of Belgrade. He is an Associate Professor at the University of Belgrade, School of Electrical Engineering. His main fields of interest include parallel programming, with an emphasis on GPU computing, bioinformatics, image processing, machine learning, social and complex network analysis, as well as educational tools and applications. His recent research interests also include spatial transcriptomics, which combines gene-expression profiling with spatial information to investigate how molecular states are organized across cells and tissues. By revealing spatial relationships between cellular states, spatial transcriptomics provides new possibilities for studying cellular interactions, communication, and the emergence of collective patterns in living systems.

Location city & country
Brussels, Belgium
Residency characteristics /
info on the host institution:
Gluon offers an artistic research environment through its network of cultural and scientific partners in Brussels and beyond. This residency will focus on artistic research into bioprinting and biofabrication: technologies in which living cells, bioinks and hydrogels are 3D-printed into precise living shapes that can grow, remodel and self-organise over time into tissues and organoids. The scientific host is the Malda Lab, the Biofabrication in Translational Regenerative Medicine group led by Prof. Jos Malda at Utrecht University and UMC Utrecht, part of the Regenerative Medicine Center Utrecht. The lab works across bioink and biomaterials design, 3D bioprinting, bioreactors, organ-on-chip models and the regeneration of cartilage and bone, including a comparative collection of joint tissue from horses and dogs to whales and giraffes. The network of expertise also includes the Levato Lab of Dr. Riccardo Levato, which pioneers volumetric, light-based bioprinting and AI-guided bioprinters that observe and steer tissue development in real time, and the Utrecht Biofabrication Facility.
Gluon provides network, scientific expertise, production, exhibition and public-presentation support.
The artist will work closely with Gluon's Art&Research team that will give organisational and curatorial support throughout the residency. The artist should be present in Utrecht and Brussels for key research and production periods, and in Brussels for the public presentation and a knowledge-sharing event. We are looking for experienced candidates with a strong interest in, or background with, living and biological materials. They should bring curiosity about self-organising biological systems, cells and organoids as co-designers, human–AI–biology collaboration, and questions of control, agency, hybridity and authorship in biofabrication.
Expected result: an art installation developed and completed on time, with documented research and a public knowledge-sharing event.
Working language: English is the main language, but Dutch and/or French is a plus to engage with local communities in and around Brussels.
Biocomputing expert(s) involved
Prof. dr. ir. Jos Malda
Jos Malda is Professor of Biofabrication in Translational Regenerative Medicine at Utrecht University (Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, Equine Sciences) and UMC Utrecht, where he is Head of Research in the Department of Orthopaedics. He also directs the Utrecht Biofabrication Facility. Trained in bioprocess engineering at Wageningen University, he earned his PhD in cartilage tissue engineering at the University of Twente and was a research fellow at Queensland University of Technology in Brisbane. His lab works on biofabrication and biomaterials design, with a particular focus on regenerating cartilage and bone using tissues made from patient-specific cells. He has received an ERC Consolidator Grant and an ERC Advanced Grant, the latter to decode and rebuild the arched architecture of cartilage. He has served as President of the International Society for Biofabrication and co-founded the first international master's programme in Biofabrication.
Dr. ir. Riccardo Levato
Riccardo Levato is Associate Professor of Translational Bioengineering and Biomaterials at Utrecht University and UMC Utrecht, where he leads a multidisciplinary team at the Regenerative Medicine Center Utrecht. He trained in biomedical engineering at Politecnico di Milano and earned his PhD at the Institute for Bioengineering of Catalonia (IBEC) in Barcelona. He is known for pioneering volumetric bioprinting, a light-based technique that creates centimetre-scale living structures in seconds rather than building them layer by layer. His current work on the GRACE and SMART-AGENT projects develops bioprinters with integrated imaging and artificial intelligence that can "see" cells and guide how tissue develops. His research has received ERC Starting, Proof of Concept and Consolidator Grants, as well as the 2023 Mid-Career Investigator Award of the International Society for Biofabrication. He sits on the board of that society.

Residency characteristics /
info on the host institution:
Kersnikova offers a hybrid art and science production environment combining BioTehna Lab, Rampa Lab, Vivarium and Kapelica Gallery. BioTehna provides wet-lab infrastructure for experimentation with living systems and biotechnology; Rampa supports electronics, mechatronics, sensing, prototyping and technical fabrication; Vivarium enables work with soil, plants, animals and technology in the field of bionics; and Kapelica provides production, installation, exhibition and public-presentation support. The Dirty Lab can therefore be configured around the selected project, combining indoor laboratory work, mobile/field setups, environmental monitoring and artistic production.
The artist will work closely with Kersnikova’s curatorial, production and technical team, scientists and field practitioners, and should be present in Ljubljana for key research, fieldwork and production periods, as well as a public Open Dirty Lab. We seek a research-based artist interested in biocomputation, interspecies communication, non-human cognition or ecosystemic intelligence, and some experience with wet-lab methods, sensing, electronics, data or computational approaches.
Our scientific network includes, but is not limited to the Departments of Biology and Microbiology at the Biotechnical Faculty, the National Institute of Biology, and the Bioinformatics Laboratory at the Faculty of Computer and Information Science.
Expected result: a completed artwork, documented research and a public knowledge-sharing activity.
Working language: English or Slovenian.
Biocomputing expert(s) involved
Dr Matej Butala
Dr Matej Butala is an Associate Professor at the Biotechnical Faculty, University of Ljubljana. His recent research includes DNA-based digital data storage, developing enzymatic approaches for encoding information in DNA. His broader research investigates bacteria and bacteriophages—viruses that infect bacteria—and how these biological systems process information, regulate genes and make molecular decisions. He studies genetic switches, gene regulation, protein–DNA interactions and phage–host interactions, including how phage proteins can alter bacterial gene expression and interactions between co-resident viruses. He also leads the Infrastructural Centre for Molecular Interactions Analysis at the University of Ljubljana. His expertise brings together molecular biology, biotechnology and biologically based approaches to storing and processing information.
