Performance Opportunity for Emerging Artists in New York City
The NYC performance open call for Dark Matters invites performers, sound artists, musicians, and interdisciplinary artists living in New York City’s five boroughs to present work responding to surveillance, anti-surveillance, countersurveillance, and sousveillance. Organized by Flux Factory at Flux IV in Hunters Point South, the program will feature two selected performances followed by a public discussion and artist Q&A. Selected artists receive a $500 stipend and access to Flux Factory resources.
If you regularly apply for artist opportunities, grants, residencies, and open calls, join the Contemporary Performance newsletter to receive new opportunities each week.
Join The Newsletter
Opportunity Snapshot
What: Dark Matters Performance Symposium Open Call
Who: Emerging performers, sound artists, musicians, and interdisciplinary artists residing in NYC
Where: Flux IV, Hunters Point South, Queens, New York City
Award / Support: $500 artist stipend, Flux Factory resources, Access to Materials for the Arts, Public presentation, Artist Q&A participation
Deadline: July 1, 2026, 11:59 PM EST
Official Link: Flux Factory
Strategy Coach Notes: https://www.patreon.com/pformart/posts/strategy-coach-161417234
Get The Application Strategy
This opportunity looks simple on the surface, but the application questions reveal a specific curatorial framework. Reviewers are not searching for the strongest performance in general. They are looking for artists whose work can engage directly with the themes established through Simone Browne’s Dark Matters: On the Surveillance of Blackness.
The Strategy Coach Notes break down how to frame your project, how reviewers are likely reading the application, how to approach the thematic questions, and how to position work samples so they reinforce the proposal. Join the Contemporary Performance Network to access the full Strategy Coach Notes.
Get The Strategy
About Dark Matters 
Dark Matters is a one-day symposium connected to the themes of surveillance and resistance. Flux Factory is inviting artists to consider how systems of observation shape identity, behavior, power, memory, and public life. The project takes inspiration from Simone Browne’s influential study of surveillance and Blackness, using performance and sound-based practices as a way to engage these ideas publicly.
The symposium format is intentionally focused. Two selected artists or collectives will present performances, followed by a moderated discussion led by artist and organizer Kamari Carter and curator and writer Kennedy Hollins Jones. The event places equal emphasis on artistic presentation and public dialogue. Applicants should understand that their broader practice will become part of the conversation alongside the specific project being proposed.
What Is Offered
$500 artist stipend
Public presentation opportunity
Curated symposium participation
Moderated artist discussion
Access to Flux Factory resources
Access to Materials for the Arts
Technical planning visit to the space
Light rehearsal opportunity before presentation
Who Should Apply to Dark Matters 
This opportunity is designed for emerging artists living in New York City. Flux Factory defines emerging broadly. Applicants may be early-career artists, self-trained practitioners, recent graduates, current students, or artists developing new directions within their practice.
The strongest applicants will likely demonstrate a clear relationship between their artistic methods and the themes of surveillance, anti-surveillance, countersurveillance, or sousveillance. Experimental approaches are encouraged. Work-in-progress projects are welcome. Existing works may also be submitted, although priority will be given to projects that have not been presented in New York City during the previous year.
Timeline
Application Deadline: July 1, 2026, 11:59 PM EST
Performance Date: August 16, 2026
Selected Artists: Two artists or collectives
Performance Length: 20–40 minutes
Why Dark Matters 
Many open calls focus primarily on production support. Dark Matters functions more like a curatorial selection process. Artists are being invited into a focused public conversation around surveillance, visibility, and power. The symposium structure creates a context where the performance itself and the discussion surrounding it carry equal weight.
For emerging artists working in performance, sound, interdisciplinary practice, media, or socially engaged work, the opportunity offers visibility, critical dialogue, and institutional support while remaining accessible through a relatively straightforward application process.

New Commission For Art Science Fellowship Amsterdam Emergence Festival 2027
The Emergence Art Science Fellowship Amsterdam opportunity invites artists, makers, and collectives to propose new commissions for the Emergence Festival 2027. The fellowship is part of Emergence at All Scales, a Dutch research consortium exploring how complex structures, patterns, materials, behaviors, and forms of collective life arise from simple ingredients, local interactions, or microscopic rules. Selected projects receive a production budget of up to €20,000 including VAT per project, research support, curatorial support, and a festival presentation in Amsterdam. The deadline is June 30, 2026.
Join the Contemporary Performance newsletter for weekly artist opportunities, grants, residencies, and fellowships.
Join The Newsletter
Opportunity Snapshot
What: Open Call for New Commissions for the Emergence Festival 2027
Who: Artists, makers, and collectives
Where: Amsterdam, Netherlands
Award / Support: Production budget of up to €20,000 including VAT per project; research support; curatorial support; development in dialogue with EAAS researchers; festival presentation
Residency Duration: New commission developed in dialogue with EAAS researchers, with premiere at Emergence Festival 2027
Deadline: June 30, 2026
Official Link: https://www.d-iep.org/artsciencefellowships
Strategy Coach Notes: https://www.patreon.com/pformart/posts/strategy-coach-161362479
Get The Application Strategy
Strategy Coach Notes for this opportunity focus on how to structure the three-page project proposal, one-page budget, curriculum, and portfolio as one coherent application system. The strongest applications will need to show a clear artistic concept, a defined relationship to emergence research, a feasible production plan, and a public-facing festival outcome. Join the network to access the Strategy Coach Notes and use them to organize your application before the deadline.
Get The Strategy
About The Art Science Fellowship Amsterdam
The Emergence Art+Science Fellowships are connected to Emergence at All Scales, a Dutch research consortium that brings together researchers across mathematics, physics, astronomy, chemistry, and related fields. The call asks applicants to propose new works inspired by emergence. The official page frames the central questions around how complexity arises, how simple ingredients or local interactions give rise to structures, patterns, materials, behaviors, and collective life, and how space and time emerged. Selected projects will be developed in dialogue with EAAS researchers and will premiere at the first Emergence Festival in June 2027.
The opportunity supports new commissions rather than general research time. Applicants should propose a work that can move from concept into public presentation within the fellowship structure. The call welcomes projects that connect to EAAS research, scientific ideas, methods, data, simulations, concepts, ambitions, or early findings. The final work should function as an artistic public experience for a broad audience. The program offers production support, research dialogue, curatorial guidance, and presentation through the festival context.
What Is Offered
Production budget of up to €20,000 including VAT per project
Research support
Curatorial support
Development in dialogue with EAAS researchers
Festival presentation
Premiere at the first Emergence Festival in June 2027
Inclusion in the EAAS research context
Potential visibility through festival and archive materials
Who Should Apply
This opportunity is for artists, makers, and collectives. It is especially relevant for applicants working across visual art, digital art, film, installation, performance, theatre, dance, music, sound, and interdisciplinary forms. Strong applicants should be able to connect artistic method to scientific inquiry. The proposal should show how the project engages emergence through a specific artistic form, production process, and public outcome. Applicants should avoid broad thematic framing and focus on a project that can be developed with researchers and presented in Amsterdam in June 2027.
Timeline
Deadline: June 30, 2026
Premiere: Emergence Festival 2027, June 2027
Why The Art Science Fellowship Amsterdam Matters
This fellowship offers substantial production support for artists working across art, science, research, and public presentation. The €20,000 production budget gives applicants room to propose a developed commission with material, technical, collaborative, and presentation needs. The research relationship with EAAS creates a strong framework for artists whose work already engages systems, complexity, collective behavior, matter, scale, data, public knowledge, or scientific imagination. For Contemporary Performance readers, this is a strong fit for performance, installation, sound, digital media, theatre, dance, and hybrid practices.
Apply
Apply through the official DIEP application page:
https://www.d-iep.org/artsciencefellowships

Create new work across rural Japan through one of the country’s largest site-responsive contemporary art festivals.
The Nakanojo Biennale 2027 Artist Open Call invites artists from around the world to develop and present work across the historic towns, schools, hot spring districts, and rural landscapes of Nakanojo, Japan. The biennale has built an international reputation for long-term site engagement and artist-led production. Participating artists receive production support and access to exhibition sites throughout the region. Applications are open through July 12, 2026.

Join The Newsletter
Opportunity Snapshot
What: Nakanojo Biennale 2027 Artist Open Call
Who: Individual artists and artist groups working in all genres including sculpture, painting, photography, video, installation, and performance
Where: Nakanojo Town, Gunma Prefecture, Japan
Award / Support: Production grant; no exhibition fee; no residency fee; insurance subsidy support available
Residency Duration: Production periods between April 15 and August 16, 2027 depending on location
Application Opens: May 8, 2026
Deadline: July 12, 2026, 23:59 JST (UTC+9)
Official Link: https://nakanojo-biennale.com/2027-open-call/english.html
Strategy Coach Notes: https://www.patreon.com/posts/strategy-coach-160022282
Get The Application Strategy
Nakanojo Biennale operates very differently from many residency and exhibition opportunities. The selection process is deeply connected to site, logistics, feasibility, and an artist’s ability to work within existing buildings and communities over an extended production period. Successful applications typically demonstrate a strong relationship between artistic method, proposed site use, installation requirements, and production planning. Strategy Coach Notes examine how the review process functions, how to approach the Image Sheet and concept proposal, how reviewers evaluate portfolios against site-responsive work, and how to construct an application that aligns artistic ambition with the realities of a distributed rural biennale.
Get The Strategy
About the Nakanojo Biennale 2027 Artist Open Call
Nakanojo Biennale takes place across multiple communities within Nakanojo Town in Gunma Prefecture, Japan. The festival transforms former schools, shopping districts, historic buildings, hot spring areas, and rural environments into exhibition spaces for contemporary art. Artists work across a decentralized network of locations rather than within a single exhibition venue.
The biennale emphasizes artistic engagement with place. Applicants propose projects for specific sites while considering the architectural, social, and environmental conditions of each location. Artists are responsible for production, installation, maintenance, and removal of their work. The festival provides a framework that supports artistic development while encouraging long-term engagement with local contexts.
What Is Offered
Production grant support
No exhibition fee
No residency fee
Opportunity to exhibit during a 37-day international biennale
Multiple exhibition sites throughout Nakanojo Town
Eligibility for individual artists and artist groups
Insurance subsidy support
Long-term production period beginning in April 2027
Potential residency accommodation in select areas beginning around April 2027
Who Should Apply to The Nakanojo Biennale 2027
This opportunity is well suited to artists who work with installation, performance, site-responsive practice, socially engaged work, environmental art, sculpture, photography, video, and interdisciplinary forms. Artists interested in developing work in direct dialogue with architecture, local histories, community contexts, and rural environments may find strong alignment with the structure of the biennale.
Applicants should be prepared to manage production logistics, travel planning, installation, maintenance, and deinstallation. The biennale rewards artists who can clearly connect artistic intent to a specific site and demonstrate realistic plans for realizing the work.
Nakanojo Biennale 2027 Timeline
Application Opens: May 8, 2026
Application Deadline: July 12, 2026, 23:59 JST
Artist Selection Notification: November 2026
Site Visits: January–March 2027
Production Period: April 15–August 16, 2027
Festival Dates: September 18–October 24, 2027
Why The Nakanojo Biennale 2027 Matters
Nakanojo Biennale has become one of Japan’s most distinctive contemporary art festivals because of its long production timeline and distributed site structure. Artists are given the opportunity to work within existing buildings and landscapes while engaging audiences across an entire region rather than a single exhibition venue. The biennale offers substantial visibility within the Japanese contemporary art ecosystem and encourages projects that emerge from direct encounters with place, architecture, and community.

Tanztage Berlin Open Call 2027 for Emerging Dance Artists
Support for premieres and revivals by Berlin-connected choreographers and performance makers
Tanztage Berlin Open Call is now accepting applications for its 2027 edition at Sophiensæle. Since 1996, the festival has supported emerging choreographers and performance artists working across contemporary dance, choreography, installation, video, and expanded performance formats. The 2027 edition, scheduled for January 7–23, 2027, will be the final edition under the artistic direction of Mateusz Szymanówka. The festival is seeking artists connected to Berlin who are developing new productions or proposing revivals of completed works. Premiere projects can receive between €10,000 and €18,000 in production support, while revival projects receive a €5,000 flat fee. The deadline to apply is July 5, 2026.
Tanztage Berlin Snapshot
What: Open call for premieres and revivals in contemporary dance, choreography, and performance
Who: Emerging artists connected to Berlin, including artists early in their careers, artists newly living in Berlin, and artists without prior Berlin project funding
Where: Sophiensæle, Berlin, Germany
Award / Support:
Premieres
€10,000–€18,000 production subsidy
€410 evening fee per person per performance
Approximately 2 weeks of rehearsal space
Technical, curatorial, dramaturgical, PR, and organizational support
Photo and video documentation
Revivals
€5,000 flat fee
€410 evening fee per person per performance
Technical, curatorial, PR, and organizational support
Photo and video documentation
Additional Support
Workshops on accessibility, intimacy coordination, and mental health
Administrative and budgeting support
Potential rehearsal access at Sophiensæle
Residency Duration / Structure: Festival runs January 7–23, 2027. Rehearsal periods begin November 2026.
Deadline: July 5, 2026
Official Link: Tanztage Berlin Open Call 2027
Strategy Coach Note: https://www.patreon.com/posts/strategy-coach-158260508
Want the Strategy Behind This Application
Tanztage Berlin is structured around choreographic clarity, production feasibility, and technical realism. Most applications weaken when proposals describe themes and aesthetics without clearly explaining how the work functions in rehearsal, staging, audience encounter, and festival presentation. Strategy Coach Notes break down how reviewers evaluate premieres versus revivals, how work samples are assessed alongside budgets and technical materials, and how to build an application where choreography, production planning, accessibility, and collaborator structure operate as one coherent system.
Application Strategy Notes
About Tanztage Berlin Open Call
Tanztage Berlin has long functioned as a major entry point into Berlin’s independent dance and performance ecosystem. The festival consistently focuses on artists whose practices challenge conventional choreographic structures and whose work engages expanded understandings of embodiment, social structures, image production, and live performance. The open call explicitly welcomes projects working across stage performance, online formats, installation, long-duration structures, and video. This creates room for choreographic work that exceeds traditional theatre presentation models.
The 2027 edition places strong emphasis on artists connected to Berlin’s independent dance field. The eligibility language is intentionally broad. Applicants are not required to provide formal residency registration, though the application must demonstrate a meaningful professional relationship to the city. The festival also states its interest in projects involving marginalized perspectives, intergenerational casts, disabled artists, and diverse working structures. The call openly acknowledges the institution’s ongoing internal work around accessibility, anti-discrimination, and power structures, which gives important context to how applications may be evaluated.
Operationally, the festival divides applications into two tracks: premieres and revivals. Premiere projects require a budget and production structure. Revival projects focus more heavily on feasibility, touring readiness, and technical execution. In both modules, the application functions as an organizational document as much as an artistic proposal. Reviewers are evaluating whether the project can realistically move through rehearsal, technical setup, scheduling, and public presentation within the framework of the festival.
The application materials reinforce this operational focus. Applicants must articulate the project clearly within strict character limits while also providing rehearsal planning, technical requirements, participant information, accessibility considerations, and work samples. The strongest applications will demonstrate structural clarity across all sections instead of relying on abstract thematic framing.
What Is Offered
€10,000–€18,000 production support for premieres
€5,000 flat support for revivals
€410 evening fee per person per performance
Approximately 2 weeks of rehearsal space for premieres
Technical rehearsals and stage setup support
Curatorial support throughout development
Junior dramaturg support for premieres
PR and marketing support
Photo and video documentation
Administrative and billing support
Accessibility workshop participation
Intimacy coordination workshop participation
Mental health workshop participation
Opportunity to present work within a major Berlin festival platform
Who Should Apply to Tanztage Berlin 
This opportunity is well suited for choreographers and performance makers developing work that already has a clear production structure. The festival supports experimentation, though the application still requires strong operational planning. Projects should demonstrate an understanding of rehearsal needs, technical setup, audience relationship, and team organization.
Artists proposing premieres should already have a concrete production direction and a realistic budget structure. Revival applicants should demonstrate why the project merits renewed presentation and how the work functions within the festival context. Since many performances are programmed as double bills, concise runtime planning and technical feasibility may influence selection decisions.
The call is especially relevant for artists building visibility within Berlin’s independent performance ecology. 
Artists newly connected to the city are encouraged to apply.
Timeline for Tanztage Berlin 
Applications are due July 5, 2026. Program decisions are expected by the end of September 2026, subject to funding confirmation. Selected artists will participate in workshops during October 2026. Rehearsal periods begin in November and December 2026, with additional technical rehearsals taking place between Christmas and New Year and during January 2027 leading into the festival presentation period.
Applicants may also participate in open Zoom office hours with curator Mateusz Szymanówka during May and June 2026, along with a public information session on June 29, 2026.
Why Tanztage Berlin Matters
Tanztage Berlin remains one of the most visible platforms for emerging choreography in Germany. The structure combines production support, institutional visibility, technical resources, and curatorial framing within a concentrated festival environment. The opportunity is particularly valuable for artists seeking stronger integration into Berlin’s independent dance ecosystem while developing ambitious new choreographic work.
The festival’s openness toward hybrid formats, installation, video, and expanded performance structures also makes this opportunity relevant for interdisciplinary artists working beyond traditional stage choreography. The inclusion of workshops focused on accessibility, intimacy, and mental health reflects a broader institutional shift toward sustainable artistic working conditions and contemporary production ethics.

Est-Nord-Est invites professional visual artists from Québec, Canada and internationally to undertake an eight-week residency focused on artistic research and experimentation. Four artists are hosted per season, with a dedicated studio-workshop, technical resources and opportunities for public engagement.
Who can apply:
 Professional visual artists at emerging or established stages, from Québec, Canada and internationally. Collectives are eligible. The Summer 2027 residency prioritises artists of African descent, while welcoming applicants whose practices resonate with its themes of osmosis, Black experience and relationships with the living world.
What you get:
 CAD $2,080 honorarium, studio-workshop accommodation, access to specialised equipment and documentation resources, technical and logistical support, local resources, and opportunities to share research publicly. A selected community workshop proposal receives an additional CAD $300 honorarium.

Call for applications | ENE artist residency
 Kyle Alden Martens, vue d'atelier, 2026. Crédit photo: ENE / Jean-Sébastien Veilleux photographe 
 Residencies program 
 REGULAR Artist Residency 
 Author residencies | REGULAR 
Artist residencies | REGULAR
This residency program is open to professional visual artists, whether established or emerging, from Québec, Canada, and other countries. The eight-week residencies host four artists per season. They include an honorarium, lodging, work spaces, logistical support, and access to the centre’s technical and documentary resources.
Call for application for artists | Regular
2027-2028
Submit an application
Duration of the residency:
8 weeks
Residency periods:
Spring: April 19 to June 11, 2027
Summer*: July 5 to August 27, 2027
Fall : September 27 to November 19, 2027
Winter: January 24 to March 18, 2028
*A residency curated by Cécilia Bracmort titled Corps céleste, corps terrestre (Celestial Body, Terrestrial Body) centered on the concept of osmosis, viewed as a process of gradual transformation through which beings, materials, and environments mutually influence one another.
Eligibility for the summer residency: Priority is given to artists of African descent, while welcoming anyone whose practice resonates with the themes explored.
Rooted in the curator’s reflections on the Black experience, the residency seeks to question and shift representations of the Black body beyond its strictly physical and social dimensions, particularly when it is reduced to a utilitarian function. It explores what can flourish when a being is no longer constrained by external representations: its presence, memory, energy, spirituality, and relationship to the living world.
This reflection will engage in dialogue with the landscape, the river, nature, and the sky of Saint-Jean-Port-Joli. The Perseid meteor shower will mark a highlight of the residency, offering participants the opportunity to share a spiritual moment in communion with nature and the stars, and to reflect on our place within a whole that is greater than ourselves.
The residency will be a space for sharing and exploration, giving artists the opportunity to question their own practices, experiment, and imagine new ways of creating, communicating, and connecting. Open to the visual arts, dance, music, poetry, science, and interdisciplinary practices, it gives priority to artists of African descent, while welcoming anyone whose practice resonates with the
questions raised.
To accompany this call for submissions, you are invited to listen to this short playlist curated by the curator as a source of inspiration.
Conditions
The eight-week residency includes:
 Residency honorarium of CAD $2,080 
 Access to an individual studio-workshop to be used for work and lodging 
 Access to specialized equipment (wood, metal, ceramics) 
 Access to a documentation centre (books, magazines) 
 Access to local resources 
 Technical, artistic and logistical support 
 Access to a bicycle in season/occasional local transportation in winter 
* Materials, travel fees and other living charges are at the residents’ expense.
ENE offers artists:
 Time and a place to devote themselves to research and experimentation 
 Privileged access to local resources and diverse areas of knowhow 
 An international art community 
Expectations towards the artists:
 To make full use of the residency period offered for his/her research 
 To be present during the entire residency period 
 To present his/her approach and research interests at the beginning of the residency at a public event organized by ENE 
 To present his/her research and experiments carried out during the residency at a public event organized by ENE at the end of the residency period 
 OPTIONAL : To propose a workshop for a youth or community organization in the region (an additional honorarium of $300 is offered to artists whose workshop proposal is selected) 
You application must include:
 A curriculum vitae (maximum two pages, PDF format) 
 A text including an artist’s statement and your research and experimentation intentions, including any specific needs in terms of technical resources, if applicable (maximum one page, PDF format) 
 A portfolio of 10 to 15 images in a single PDF document accompanied by a description list of the images. If video works are used, provide a link (Vimeo, YouTube) accompanied by the password, if applicable. Make sure that the videos will be accessible. 
The application must be submitted online. No application sent by mail, incomplete or received after the deadline will be accepted.
Artists are selected according to the following criteria:
 Consistency with the center's mandate, which focuses on experimentation and research rather than production and project completion; 
 The potential impact of the residency and its specific features (time, technical workshops, events, community, etc.) on the resident's career; 
 The rigor and clarity of the proposal; 
 Openness to participating in the center's community life. 
Est-Nord-Est recognizes the importance of bringing together a multiplicity of forms of artistic and cultural expression. In the selection process, emphasis will be placed on cultural, generational, sexual, and identity diversity. In this spirit of inclusion, we encourage artists from underrepresented, marginalized, and minority groups to apply.
Submit an application — Deadline: November 8, 2026 at 11:59. p.m.
Accessibility and application support :
Est-Nord-Est wishes to promote inclusion and accessibility for all artists and authors, particularly those from underrepresented and/or marginalized groups.
A virtual mentoring session can be offered, upon request, to help you prepare your application for this call for submissions. To request this service, please write to info@estnordest.org before November 1st, 2026.
If you wish to submit your application in a format other than written (audio, video, etc.), please contact us at info@estnordest.org or by phone at 418-598-6363.
Conditions for hosting residents with children:
If you wish to come to the residency with your child or children, please note that you must come during Fall 2027.
Each studio is furnished with one double bed and two single beds. Therefore, residents who are parents may come with one or two children and live at ENE. If the resident has three or more children, the centre will help find alternative lodging. However, the lodging costs will be at the resident’s expense.
Residents may come with an accompanying adult for the entire duration of the residency at no extra cost. If the accompanying adult also lives at the centre, this person must occupy the same studio as the resident. There are no extra bedrooms. If the accompanying adult is lodged outside the centre, the resident is responsible for that person’s lodging cost.
If you wish to have a babysitter for your child or children during yourworkdays, the centre will help you find a resource person. Please note that babysitting costs must be borne by the resident.
Despite these stated conditions, we remain flexible with regard to each resident’s reality, and if you are selected we will be happy to discuss your needs with you!
Conditions for hosting collectives:
Each member of the collective receives an honorarium.
The collective shares a studio. The studio is furnished with one double bed and two single beds. If the collective would like to find alternative lodging near the centre, the team can help with the search, but the lodging costs are at the collective’s expense.
If you have any questions, please refer to our FAQ. Otherwise, we invite you to join us for an online Q&A session with the center’s General and Artistic Director on Thursday, October 1, 2026, at 1 PM in French and 2 PM in English, via Zoom (Eastern Standard Time).
The session will not be recorded.

Tuwaiq Sculpture 2027 Open Call - Riyadh Art
Tuwaiq Sculpture 2027 Open Call
Where Roots Run Deep takes as a starting point the idea that a place is shaped not only by what appears on its surface, but by the layers of land, memory, culture, and lived experience that give it depth and continuity. Roots are understood not simply as a connection to the past, but as a source of resilience, growth, and the capacity to continually redefine a place.
Riyadh offers a compelling context for this exploration: a city deeply rooted in its land, history, culture, and people, while undergoing profound transformation. Here, the rooted and the emerging exist in dialogue; inherited knowledge meets new possibilities, and the past continues to inform the ways in which the future takes shape. Transformation, in this sense, is not a departure from what came before, but an extension of it.
The symposium invites artists to engage with these ideas through contemporary approaches to land, belonging, identity, memory, transformation, and imprint. The root is not treated as a literal image or fixed metaphor, but as an open and evolving concept that may emerge through material, trace, movement, relationship, experience, or a sense of place.
Through site-responsive making, artists are invited to engage with Riyadh’s physical and cultural landscape, allowing the site and its conditions to become part of the artwork. Material, ground, light, shadow, sound, movement, distance, and human presence may all contribute to how an artwork takes form and is encountered.
The symposium expands the possibilities of sculpture beyond the traditional monument as a fixed and enduring object, embracing contemporary approaches in which artworks can engage with place, memory, environment, and the public realm. Rather than simply representing or commemorating the past, sculpture may create spaces for encounter, reflection, and renewed relationships with it. Works may alter a path, draw attention to overlooked qualities of a site, or create new connections between people and place.
In this way, Where Roots Run Deep becomes an exploration of how what is deeply rooted can generate what is yet to come, how memory can become material, place can become experience, and the traces of the past can open new possibilities for artists to explore our shared future.

Jobs and Opportunities
We are committed to creating a community that encourages people of all ages, abilities and areas of interest to engage with contemporary art. 
We are currently recruiting for a new Director. Please find more details below.
Camden Art Centre does not offer internships or placements, however young people aged 15-25 years old may be interested in learning more about our youth collective, Transformative Futures.
To find out about new opportunities please sign up to our mailing list and follow us on Instagram.
 Read more
Director
Camden Art Centre has been a place for art and the people who make it since 1965. Rooted in its community in north London and respected by artists around the world, it has given early support to artists including Phyllida Barlow, Kerry James Marshall, Kara Walker and Mohammed Sami, and staged the first UK exhibitions of artists such as Hilma af Klint and Martin Wong. Learning sits at the heart of our mission, and exhibitions and education carry equal weight.
After nearly a decade as Director, Martin Clark leaves Camden Art Centre in January 2027 to lead Towner in Eastbourne. The Board of Trustees now seeks his successor.
This is a moment of real change. Camden Art Centre recently acquired its building from Camden Council, securing its long-term home. An upcoming capital project developed with Tony Fretton and David Owen Architect will improve facilities, grow earned income and reduce the building’s environmental footprint. Leading the campaign to fund it will be central to the role.
The position is hands-on, with a team of around 25. The Director sets the artistic vision, leads exhibitions and learning programmes, and is responsible for all fundraising, working with a Deputy Director who oversees finance, operations, and commercial activity. We are looking for a leader with a track record of programming contemporary visual art and working closely with artists. You will bring proven success in fundraising and income generation, sound financial and business judgement, an understanding of capital projects, and a genuine commitment to access, diversity and learning.
We particularly welcome applications from people from backgrounds under-represented in the museums and galleries sector. Saxton Bampfylde Ltd is acting as an employment agency advisor to Camden Art Centre on this appointment. For further information about the role, including details about how to apply, please follow the link below.
Application deadline: Noon, Sunday 8 November 2026.

Upė Foundation and Gasworks are looking for a Curatorial Fellow!
The Upė Foundation Curatorial Fellowship is an 12-18 month full-time paid position embedded within Gasworks’ curatorial team. Conceived as a professional development opportunity for an early-career curator with a connection to the Baltic region, the Fellowship offers sustained experience across Gasworks’ exhibitions, residencies, public programmes and wider artistic activity.
Working closely with Gasworks’ Curator and Assistant Curator, the Fellow will contribute to the coordination and delivery of Gasworks’ artistic programme and collaborate across the organisation with artists, partners, external contributors and freelancers. The role requires care, curiosity, strong organisational ability and administrative skills in an artist-focused, fast-paced environment. A particular focus of the Fellowship will be supporting the artist selected through the parallel Upė Foundation open call. The Fellow will work closely with the selected artist during their 2027 residency and contribute to the research, development, production and logistics of their subsequent solo exhibition at Gasworks in 2028.
This new role is part of a multi-year partnership between Gasworks and Upė Foundation supporting emerging artists and curators connected to the Baltic region (Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia) and their diasporas. The partnership also includes a fully funded artist residency in London, followed by a solo exhibition at Gasworks in 2028. Throughout the Fellowship, regular meetings with Upė will be held, and it is expected that the Fellow engages with research, travel and networking supported through Upė’s programme and with their wider fellow cohort. 
Through the Fellowship, the successful candidate will benefit from:
Structured professional development within Gasworks’ Programmes team
Experience contributing to exhibitions, commissions, residencies, public programmes and events
Opportunities to contribute Baltic and broader Central Eastern European research perspectives to Gasworks’ curatorial discussions
Opportunities to build professional networks in London, the UK and internationally
A dynamic working environment within a leading international contemporary arts organisation
Please review the job description found in the resources section below before starting your application. Then download the application form, complete and submit below. If you have any questions about the opportunity please email rosaharvest@gasworks.org.uk
This fellowship is supported by Upė Foundation, a London-based platform that draws currents between global and Baltic (Lithuanian, Latvian, Estonian) art communities, setting new artistic, curatorial and research possibilities in motion. Upė focuses on horizontal, long-term exchange through a range of partnerships, fellowships and initiatives, amplifying new ideas, risk-taking work and underexplored perspectives. Upė is drawn to a field that is living, cross-disciplinary and imaginative, open to encounters between practices, contexts and communities.

Grant Opportunities
APPLICATIONS ARE NOW OPEN!
2027 ACC Fellowships and Grants 
The Asian Cultural Council (ACC) is pleased to announce the open call for the 2027 Grant Cycle. Applications will be accepted from October 1 through November 10, 2026, with letters of recommendation due November 16.
Prospective applicants are encouraged to review the guidelines below before beginning an application. These guidelines cover ACC’s mission and grantmaking priorities, as well as detailed information on available grant types, eligibility requirements, application procedures, and frequently asked questions. 
Overview of ACC's Grantmaking
ACC’s Mission 
ACC advances international dialogue, understanding, and respect through cultural exchange activities in Asia and the United States to create a more harmonious and peaceful world.  
What We Support 
ACC supports artists, scholars, arts professionals, and organizations through fellowships and grants that advance cultural exchange between the U.S. and Asia, and within Asia. Through these immersive experiences, participants step outside their daily life, engage deeply with new cultural contexts, expand their perspectives and creative practice, and develop relationships with peers across borders. After their fellowship or grant, participants join ACC’s global alumni network, continuing to build connections and contribute to cross-cultural understanding through their work. 
Since 1963, ACC has awarded more than $100 million USD to support nearly 6,000 exchanges across 16 disciplines, involving grantees from 26 countries and regions. 
ACC offers four types of grants to support its mission: 
New York Fellowship: Over a six-month period, a diverse cohort of artists, scholars, and arts professionals from Asia live in the United States and engage with a new cultural landscape, using this immersive experience to broaden their perspectives and inform the development of their artistic practices. This rare and extended pause from daily work—shared with peers across disciplines—offers space for reflection, exploration, and meaningful exchange, free from the pressure to produce or present work. 
Individual Fellowship: With a flexible, often shorter timeframe of one to six months, artists, scholars, and arts professionals from Asia and the U.S. pursue research, self-directed exploration and cultural exchange experiences in a new or less familiar environment, fostering peer-to-peer dialogue, collaboration, and knowledge-sharing. The individual fellowship can be a joint fellowship of up to three participants.
Graduate Fellowship: Supports graduate students from Asia pursuing U.S.-based degree programs that are unavailable or underrepresented in their home region. While this fellowship is academic by nature, studying in a less familiar environment, fellows are exposed to new ideas beyond the classroom. 
Organization Grant: Enables arts and culture organizations in Asia and the U.S. to pursue activities that advance their understanding of a topic or area practice, foster meaningful cultural exchange for their staff, communities, and collaborators. 
Application and Selection Timeline 
The 2027 Grants Cycle will follow the schedule outlined below. 
Call for Applications Opens: October 1, 2026, at 9:59 AM U.S. Eastern Time (ET) 
Applications Due: November 10, at 9:59 AM U.S. Eastern Time (ET) 
Letters of Recommendation Due: November 16, at 9:59 AM U.S. Eastern Time (ET) 
Review and Selection Process: November 2026 - April 2027 
Notifications to Applicants: Mid-May 2027 
Grant Period (When ACC-funded travel and activities must take place): August 1, 2027 – December 31, 2028
Overview of General Eligibility Requirements, Selection Criteria, and Selection Process 
All applicants must meet the general eligibility criteria below. Each fellowship or grant program also has additional requirements, which are outlined in the program-specific guidelines under “Fellowship and Grant Opportunities.”
Learn more about our eligibility criteria and program requirements. 
Eligibility 
ACC welcomes applications from artists, scholars, arts professionals, and organizations proposing immersive cultural experiences aligned with our mission. 
Eligible applications must meet the following requirements: 
Eligible Activities: ACC fellowship and grant funding is strictly limited to supporting activities related to cultural exchange and immersive experiences. ACC does not fund production or promotional activities, including activities intended to directly or indirectly produce, exhibit, or perform a specific, predetermined work product. Examples of ineligible “production grants” include, but are not limited to: filming a documentary, conducting research for a planned work product (e.g. books, films, plays, etc.), organizing an exhibition, or conducting a concert series. 
Timing of Fellowship and Grant Activities: All ACC-funded activities must take place within the grant period: August 1, 2027 – December 31, 2028. 
Eligible Destinations: ACC fellowships and grant activities must take place in the eligible countries, territories, and regions listed below. The New York and Graduate Fellowships may only take place in the U.S. For details on eligible destinations and restrictions, refer to the specific program guidelines. 
 Eligible Countries, Territories, and Regions: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Brunei, Cambodia, China (Mainland), East Timor, Hong Kong SAR, India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Laos, Macau SAR, Malaysia, Mongolia, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Philippines, Singapore, Sri Lanka, Taiwan, Thailand, U.S., and Vietnam. 
Citizenship, Permanent Resident Status, and Organization Registration: Applicants must be citizens or legal permanent residents of at least one of the countries, territories, or regions listed above, or be an organization registered in one of those locations. Permanent resident status refers to a government-issued legal status that allows you to live in a country, territory, or region indefinitely. It does not include temporary, renewable work visas or student/scholar visas.
Experience and Eligible Disciplines: Applicants must be an arts or cultural organization, or an artist, scholar, or arts professional. Applicants must have at least five years of experience in one of the eligible disciplines at the time of application and must propose activities within an eligible discipline. 
 Note: Graduate Fellowship applicants are not required to have five years of professional experience. 
 Eligible Disciplines: Architecture (Design, History, and Theory), Archaeology, Art History, Arts Administration, Arts Criticism, Conservation, Crafts, Curation, Dance, Ethnomusicology, Film,* Literature, Museum Studies, Music, Theater, and Visual Art. 
 * Note: Applicants who primarily work in or study video art or photography may apply under visual art. 
ACC Alumni: ACC welcomes applications from alumni; however: 
Alumni who have received an ACC grant in the last two calendar years are not eligible.
Alumni of the ACC New York Fellowship program cannot apply for another New York Fellowship. 
Alumni who previously received a six-month fellowship or similarly large grant are unlikely to receive another grant of comparable size. 
Budget: Eligible expenses may include travel, accommodation, daily expenses, museum and event tickets, interpreters, and other costs that enable these exchanges. Funding cannot be used to: 
Produce or promote specific, pre-planned projects, including performances, films, exhibitions, or publications. For example, grants cannot cover research for a book, filming for a documentary, or training for a future performance. 
Conduct promotional activities, including public relations, marketing or promotional travel (e.g. a book tour). 
Funding cannot be used exclusively to travel to an event. 
Purchase production capital or equipment. However, funding can include reasonable rental fees for necessary equipment or meeting/workshop spaces used during the grant activities. 
Participate in full-time residency program. 
Selection Criteria 
Applications are assessed using the following criteria: 
Alignment with ACC’s mission: Demonstrates strong alignment with ACC’s mission to advance mutual understanding through cultural exchange. Clearly explains how the fellowship experience will broaden the applicant’s horizons, support creative growth, and foster valuable international connections. 
Time in the applicant’s career: Provides a clear rationale for why the proposed cultural exchange experience is important at this time.  
Quality of proposal: Presents clear and feasible activities and objectives with the potential to impact the applicant, their work, and/or relevant communities. 
Artistic or professional merit: Demonstrates high-level qualifications, excellence and originality in past work, and proposes meaningful contributions to the applicant’s field or artistic discipline.  
Ability to communicate in the destination: Shows sufficient language proficiency or plans to address language barriers (e.g. budgeting for interpreters) to carry out the project. Demonstrates confidence in navigating cultural differences during the fellowship. Fellows traveling to the U.S. on an ACC-sponsored J-1 visa must demonstrate the ability to communicate in English as required by U.S. government regulations (see New York Fellowship and Individual Fellowship Guidelines). 
Selection Process 
ACC staff first review applications to confirm eligibility. Applications that do not meet the criteria, including those considered production grants, will not move forward. Eligible applications are then reviewed by experts across disciplines—including ACC alumni—who serve as panelists/jurors. Short-listed candidates are invited for a virtual interview. Final selections are approved by ACC’s Global Board of Trustees. 
Fellowship and Grant Opportunities
ACC offers four fellowship and grant programs to support immersive cultural exchange. Review the guidelines below for details and use the "How to Apply" section to begin. Applicants may apply to only one program per cycle.
New York Fellowship 
Over a six-month period, a diverse cohort of artists, scholars, and arts professionals from Asia live in the United States and engage with a new cultural landscape, using this immersive experience to broaden their perspectives and inform the development of their artistic practices. This rare pause from daily life and work—shared with peers across disciplines—offers space for reflection, exploration, and meaningful exchange, free from the pressure to produce or present work. 
Learn more about the New York Fellowship. 
What does the New York Fellowship offer? 
Freedom to Explore: Fellows immerse themselves in New York City and U.S. cultural life—attending performances, exhibitions, workshops, and discussions—to inform their practice and broaden their perspectives. 
Peer-Learning and Exchange: Fellows join a diverse cohort from across Asia, sharing artistic perspectives, learning from one another, and building lasting connections. 
ACC Activities and Events: ACC organizes group activities that may include visits to arts and cultural institutions and attending performances and gatherings with local ACC alumni and artists in New York City. 
Individualized Programmatic and Logistical Support: ACC staff provide guidance on living in New York, achieving grant objectives, and connecting fellows with alumni and resources to support their fellowship activities. 
Subject to availability, New York Fellows may live at the International House (I-House), with fees deducted from the ACC grant (see “Grant Amounts and Payments” section). Fellows may also arrange their own housing, however, ACC cannot assist or assume responsibility for independent arrangements.

Exhibition Venue: Mana Wynwood, Miami, FL
Exhibition Dates: December 2–6, 2026 (Concurrent with Miami Art Week & Art Basel)
Submission Deadline: November 10, 2026
RED DOT MIAMI 2026: View Sizzle Reel
Opportunity Overview:
The Black & White Gallery is now accepting entries for our international juried contemporary artist search for Red Dot Miami 2026, taking place December 2–6, 2026, concurrent with Miami Art Week and Art Basel. Our pavilion features a curated presentation of investment-grade monochrome photography and freestanding contemporary sculpture. We are awarding physical exhibition spots on the main fair floor and ongoing global gallery representation to top-tier portfolios.
The Grand Prize Tiers (100% Subsidized Physical Exhibition):
1st Place Photography Winner: Full space procurement fee completely waived. Receives a dedicated vertical wall panel layout on the Red Dot fair floor under a 50/50 fair sales split. Includes full on-site curatorial management and premium global digital distribution. (Note: Past gallery partner entries are ineligible).
1st Place Sculpture Winner: Full space procurement fee completely waived. Receives a dedicated, centralized showcase footprint on the fair floor to exhibit their work under a 50/50 fair sales split.
The Representation & Runner-Up Prizes:
The Roster Integration: Both 1st Place Grand Prize Winners will receive official, ongoing artist representation on the main gallery website and our official Artsy Partner platform profile, launching with a concurrent 1-month online exhibition synced directly with Miami Art Week traffic, and remaining as regular roster artists thereafter.
Digital-Only Finalist Tier: Select high-scoring finalists who pass our curatorial review but do not claim the physical booth slots will be awarded official placement as Digital-Only Exhibition Finalists. You receive the exact same digital prize as the winners: an official representation profile on our website and Artsy, a featured spot in our 1-month concurrent online fair exhibition, and continuous inclusion on our regular digital roster thereafter. The digital sales split operates at a favorable 60% Artist / 40% Galleryduring the active fair week, reverting to a standard 50/50 split thereafter.
Inventory, Sizing, & Space Constraints:
Photographers (Strictly Black & White Only): All subject matters, formats, and styles are welcome. To maintain a premium, large-format gallery standard across our 12-foot high walls, the absolute minimum dimension allowed for any physical print is 24 x 36 inches. The winner’s showcase layout is a dedicated 2 linear feet x 12 feet vertical panel mapped for exactly two (2) 24×36″ works curated in a vertical column stack.
Sculptors: Open to all styles, conceptual themes, and materials. Works must be freestanding and engineered to fit a standard 12″x12″ footprint safely. Tall, freestanding vertical structures are highly welcome, provided their width remains tight to the 12″x12″ base dimension to protect booth traffic paths and client sightlines.
Logistics, Printing, & Shipping Protocols:
Production & Printing: Photographers maintain absolute control over physical presentation standards and are responsible for all printing, mounting, and framing execution and associated costs. For convenience and to minimize transit wear, the gallery can provide a list of recommended premier professional printing labs in Miami that can print, frame, and deliver works directly to our fair coordinator.
Incoming Shipping: The Artist assumes full financial responsibility and logistical arrangement for all inbound freight, shipping, and insurance costs required to deliver the artwork securely to the gallery’s designated Miami receiving location.
Outbound Return Shipping: The Artist is 100% responsible for arranging and paying for the post-fair return logistics of any unsold inventory. The gallery will not physically transport, carry, or deliver artwork to commercial shipping offices (UPS, FedEx, DHL, etc.) post-fair. To ensure a smooth breakdown, the Artist must provide a pre-paid, fully insured electronic return shipping label, alongside a scheduled, direct-from-booth carrier pickup appointment at Mana Wynwood for the official fair breakdown window. Works without pre-arranged return carrier pickups will not be released.
Submission Fee Configuration:
Application fees fund our juried image processing and secure website entry infrastructure:
Standard Entry: $45.00 USD for up to 3-5 unique artwork images.
Extended Portfolio Entry: $55.00 USD for 6-10 unique artwork images.
How to Apply
1. Apply directly through our secure website payment form portal below at SUBMIT / APPLY.
2. Upload high-resolution images of your black and white photography or sculpture. Your image upload link will be available after your submission purchase. Please include your website, instagram or social media.
Final winners and digital runners-up will be announced directly via our administration following the close of the jury window.

VisArts Emerging Curator Program 2027 
Application Deadline:  December 18, 2026, Midnight 
VisArts invites applications from emerging curators to work with an experienced mentoring curator to develop and present an exhibition at VisArts in the Kaplan Gallery in the fall of 2027. 
The VisArts Emerging Curator Program offers a unique opportunity for an emerging curator or artist with an interest in exhibition-making or curating to work with an experienced mentoring curator to develop and present an exhibition and to assist in the presentation of the mentor’s exhibition. To develop expanded education programming and enhanced visitor experiences, the 2027 Emerging Curator and the 2027 Mentoring Curator will also focus on developing tools to support public programming that promotes social interaction, creative exchange, and audience engagement. 
VisArts will provide the Emerging Curator with a $10,000 budget to cover exhibition costs and curatorial fees. Additional staff support for printing, promotions, and execution of exhibition programming is available. The program is one year and will begin in January 2027.
International applicants must be eligible to work in the United States. VisArts is unable to provide or assist with visas.
The selection panel includes the VisArts Galleries Director & Curator, Artist Advisory Council, and the 2027 Mentoring Curator.
VisArts is a nonprofit arts center in Rockville, Maryland. We’re the largest visual arts organization in the area and an active, significant presence in the greater metropolitan arts community. Our contemporary art galleries, artist studios, and 355 POD Space Gallery are located in Rockville Town Square, a thriving gathering place for the local community. VisArts presents exhibitions of contemporary art in our five galleries, along with related programs and events. We also offer Emerging Curator and Studio Artist Programs along with art classes and VisAbility Art Lab, our supported studio for adult emerging artists with disabilities.
2027 Mentoring Curator: Fabiola R. Delgado 
Fabiola R. Delgado (b. Cabimas, Venezuela) is an interdependent curator and creative producer based in Washington DC. Formerly a Human Rights lawyer and political asylum seeker from Venezuela, her practice is shaped by a commitment to justice, engaging questions of power, memory, objecthood, and social responsibility, with a main focus on migrant and diasporic narratives. Her work spans exhibitions, scholarship, editorial projects, and public programming for all ages.
She’s collaborated with institutions such as the Hirshhorn Museum, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Smart Museum of Art, National Museum of American History, Anacostia Community Museum, Brooklyn Museum, Washington Project for the Arts, Transformer, Cervantes Institute NY, and Times Square Arts. Her projects have been featured in The New York Times, The Washington Post, Hyperallergic, and BmoreArt Magazine, among other publications.
Curatorial Collaboration 
During the yearlong program, the curatorial team (mentoring curator and emerging curator) will: 
Conduct curatorial research
Develop a cohesive and compelling exhibition proposal
Develop writing skills for catalogs and other printed and online materials
Develop budgets for executing exhibitions and exhibition programming
Communicate with artists and lending institutions, developing contracts and loan information
Design and implement educational exhibition programming and outreach activities that engage artists, curators, and public audience of all ages
Develop sponsorship/fundraising initiatives to support the exhibition programming (if needed)
Oversee exhibition design and installation
Develop marketing and public relations materials in support of the exhibition, such as press releases, website + social media content, and print media
The VisArts Emerging Curator Program provides emerging curators with practical, hands-on experience at a community arts organization. It’s designed to support diverse exhibitions presenting a broad spectrum of ideas and curatorial approaches. In addition, it enhances the VisArts exhibition experience by developing educational opportunities, public programming, and opportunities for community engagement through expanded use of interactive interpretive media. 
Application 
Applicants don’t need to have a fully realized curatorial proposal, but we’re interested in getting a sense of your interests, tastes, and sensibilities. The formal proposal will be developed with the support and guidance of the 2027 Mentoring Curator and the Galleries Department.
To apply online, create a Submittable account and complete the form. 
Submission Requirements 
1. Application form 
2. CV 
3. Evidence of past curatorial projects: 
Up to 10 still images
Up to five minutes of video and audio tracks
List of images with artist name, title, year, medium, and descriptive information
Supporting PDF documents
4. A statement that addresses the following: 
What makes presenting an exhibition in a nonprofit community arts center with the guidance of a mentor an ideal opportunity?
What do you hope to achieve with this exhibition and mentoring program?
What do you consider your curatorial intentions or interests in regard to exhibition-making?
How do you envision enriching the audience experience?
How would you engage the community?
What sorts of programming and content delivery would you like to see paired with exhibitions?
Timeline 
Application deadline: December 18, 2026
Finalists notified: January 8, 2027
Finalist interviews: January 13-15, 2027
Emerging Curator notified: January 20, 2027
Program: January 2027 – January 2028 (detailed schedule TBD)
Emerging Curator exhibition:  October 15, 2027 – January 9, 2028
Mentoring Curator exhibition:  August 27 – October 10, 2027 
About VisArts
VisArts is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit. Our mission is to transform individuals and communities through the visual arts.
A hub for artistic exploration and social impact since 1987, VisArts brings people together through shared creative experiences, including:
Critically acclaimed contemporary art exhibitions, programs + events
Studio Artist and Emerging Curator programs
Award-winning art classes and camps
VisAbility Art Lab and Accessible Arts classes for artists with disabilities
Community art workshops
Art and wellness programs
Volunteer and internship opportunities
The annual Rockville Arts Festival
These inspire new ideas, encourage self-expression, embrace diverse perspectives, and celebrate the visual arts as fundamental to a connected community.

VisArts invites artists working in all media to apply for solo exhibitions in 2027. Selected artists will present work in one of three exhibition spaces at VisArts: the Gibbs Street Gallery, Common Ground Gallery, or Concourse Gallery. Gibbs Street Gallery 
Approximately 1,100 square feet with 16-foot ceilings. Located at street level, the gallery features floor-to-ceiling windows along one wall and can accommodate large-scale, immersive, and installation-based work.
Common Ground Gallery 
Approximately 300 square feet and located on Floor 2. This intimate gallery is well suited to focused solo presentations, installations, and smaller bodies of work.
Concourse Gallery 
Approximately 500 square feet and located on Floor 2. The gallery includes a curved wall of windows and supports a range of two- and three-dimensional work, installation, and time-based media.

The commission will transform basketball courts, hoardings, shipping containers and other architectural features, celebrating the site's identity as a vibrant, inclusive space for sport, play and community life.

The commission is open to emerging and established artists and designers, particularly those working in public art, large-scale graphics, illustration, mural painting and surface design.

The selected artist will receive a £10,000 artist fee to develop and deliver a major public art commission at Marlborough Sports Garden in central London.

The commission offers opportunities to collaborate with Cullinan Studio architects, Bankside Open Spaces Trust and local communities through participatory co-design workshops.

KANE ART PRIZE 2026
Regular Submission Deadline: November 15, 2026, 23:59 (GMT)
KANE International Contemporary Art Prize 2026 is the second edition of the international contemporary art award established by K:art Studio, dedicated to discovering, supporting, and promoting emerging and experimental artists from around the world.
As an important part of K:art Studio’s artist development programme, the KANE Prize goes beyond recognising outstanding contemporary artworks. It is designed to create long-term pathways for artists to develop their practice, expand their international visibility, and connect with curators, collectors, and wider art audiences across different cultural contexts.
Continuing its focus on motion, resonance, and transformation, the 2026 edition invites artists working across diverse media, disciplines, and conceptual approaches to explore how contemporary art can move, resonate, and connect across cultures. Selected and awarded works will be presented through K:art Studio’s curated physical and online exhibitions, bringing together contemporary voices that reflect the dynamic and evolving landscape of art today.
As part of the post-award support, K:art Studio will continue to provide winning artists with opportunities through its international exhibition and art fair programmes. Following K:art Studio’s participation in major international art fairs in 2026, including EXPO CHICAGO and KunstRAI, the gallery will continue to expand its global presence through multiple art fair presentations in 2027. These platforms will offer selected artists the opportunity to reach broader international audiences and gain exposure within global collecting networks. The programme will also support artists through private collector exhibitions and tailored presentations, with a particular focus on creating meaningful connections with collectors in Asia.
Through the KANE International Contemporary Art Prize 2026, K:art Studio aims to build a bridge between emerging artistic voices, international exhibition platforms, and global collecting communities, helping experimental and culturally resonant contemporary art practices gain visibility, recognition, and long-term development opportunities.
 Awards
Award benefits are designed to support artists with both immediate visibility and longer-term development opportunities through K:art Studio’s artist development programme. All submitted works will be presented in the online showcase!

Submission Guidelines
Open to artists worldwide.
Open to emerging, mid-career, and experimental artists working across all contemporary art practices.
All mediums are accepted, including painting, photography, moving image, installation, sound, digital art, sculpture, performance, text-based work, and interdisciplinary practices.
Submitted works must be original and completed by the artist.
Artists may submit either a single work or a coherent body of work, depending on the application requirements.
All submissions must be made through the official KANE International Contemporary Art Prize 2026 application platform or designated submission channel.
Artists are responsible for ensuring that all submitted materials, images, videos, texts, and documentation are accurate and properly presented.
Incomplete, late, or incorrectly submitted applications may not be considered.
Terms
Entry fees are non-refundable once submitted.
Artists retain full copyright and ownership of their submitted works.
By entering, artists grant K:art Studio the right to use submitted images, videos, texts, and documentation for purposes related to the KANE International Contemporary Art Prize 2026, including exhibitions, catalogues, press, social media, website features, art fair presentations, collector previews, and promotional materials.
This usage right is granted for one year from the date of submission, unless otherwise agreed with the artist.
Selected and awarded artists may be invited to participate in K:art Studio’s exhibitions, online presentations, art fair programmes, private collector exhibitions, and artist development initiatives.
Participation in the Prize does not guarantee gallery representation, sales, acquisition, art fair presentation, or placement in any private or institutional collection.
K:art Studio reserves the right to select, shortlist, award, exhibit, or promote submitted works at its curatorial discretion.
Judging criteria and jury discussions remain confidential.
Winners and selected artists will be contacted by email before any public announcement.
Artists are responsible for securing any necessary permissions for third-party materials, collaborators, music, images, or copyrighted elements included in their submitted work.
K:art Studio reserves the right to disqualify any submission that contains false information, infringes copyright, violates ethical standards, or does not comply with the Prize guidelines.
K:art Studio reserves the right to make reasonable changes to deadlines, exhibition formats, prize structure, or programme arrangements.

Grants for Artists
 The Hopper Prize is a grant-making institution and digital archiving platform offering a series of individual artist grants on a bi-annual basis totaling $26,000.00 USD. 
Now offering $4,500 grants.
We provide unrestricted cash grants in the amount of $4,500 and $1,000 to artists around the globe.

Visibility
The Hopper Prize was established to provide grants, visibility, and career enhancing validation to artists who demonstrate a serious commitment to their work.
We accept submissions for grants through a bi-annual open call. For each grant cycle, a new cohort of artists is selected to receive financial support and widespread exposure. Grant winners and finalists are chosen solely on the basis of artistic excellence and the promise of future potential.
We view the field of visual art in its broadest and most inclusive sense and therefore make our awards available to artists working in any media.

the-don-bachardy-fellowship-in-london-86.text:
The Don Bachardy Fellowship enables an emerging international postgraduate artist to develop their practice at the Royal Drawing School during the Summer Term (April–July). 
Named after Californian portrait painter Don Bachardy, the fellowship supports drawing as a foundation for artistic practice. Bachardy studied at the Slade in 1961 and has since drawn and painted over 10,000 portraits from life.
Who can apply: Applicants must have studied at MA level and demonstrate a commitment to observational drawing. Artists from the UK, those who have studied and lived in the UK, and previous Royal Drawing School students are not eligible. 
What you get: The Fellow receives a $7,500 stipend towards travel and accommodation and spends three days a week for ten weeks drawing alongside students on The Drawing Year postgraduate programme and Public Programme courses. They can curate a programme from over 60 drawing courses, taught by practising artists, and attend lectures featuring leading contemporary artists and art historians.
Deadline 19 November 2026

Residencies
The School runs a variety of residency programmes in the UK and internationally, offering artists time and space to develop their practice in unique settings. 
 Alumni
As a champion of drawing in contemporary art and education, the School sees residencies as a vital opportunity for artists to expand both their creative practice and professional development.
Residencies are primarily open to alumni of The Drawing Year and faculty members of the School. However, there are also opportunities open to artists from around the world.
On this page, you’ll find a range of residencies to explore — each with its own focus, location, and eligibility criteria. Full details are listed under the relevant headings.
Residencies
Scotland | Wales | France | Switzerland | Italy | India | Antigua 
London:
Don Bachardy Fellowship | Manetti Shrem Scholarship | CW+ London
Dumfries House, Scotland 
Artists’ residencies at Dumfries House are open to alumni and faculty of the Royal Drawing School, Scottish artists and to applicants through our partner organisations, for whom drawing is part of their practice. 
The Dumfries House residency is delivered by the Royal Drawing School, Glasgow School of Art and Dumfries House in conjunction with the Royal Drawing School's international partners. 
Funded residency places are available throughout the year. They provide a private studio and self-catering accommodation on the Dumfries House Estate for up to four artists at any one time. 
The Dumfries House residency has an emphasis on working from observation and the development of new work. The residency is s a unique opportunity for painters, textile and furniture designers, illustrators, practice-based researchers, printmakers, and artists who use drawing in their practice. Please note: printmaking residencies are only open to artists proficient in printmaking.  
The Dumfries House residency is kindly support by Thomas and Jeannie Rutherfoord and The King's Foundation. 
Back to top
 About the location
Dumfries House is set in 2,000 acres of land in East Ayrshire, Scotland. It was built between 1754 and 1759 for the 5th Earl of Dumfries. Dumfries House principal rooms and their contents have remained virtually unchanged for 250 years, leading the house to be described by some as an 18th century time capsule. 
Artists in residence have access to a significant collection of 18th century Chippendale furniture, tapestries, and textiles. They also have access to a large collection of Flemish and Scottish paintings from the 15th to 20th centuries, on loan from the National Gallery of Scotland. 
Artists in residence have the freedom to roam, enjoy and draw inspiration from the entire estate and gardens. Artists can work in the house during opening hours and can arrange to meet the Collections Manager for more information about the house and its collection.  
Dumfries House Estate is home to several sustainability and education projects such as the traditional building skills, animal husbandry, cookery school, textiles centre, and horticultural programmes.  
 Studios & Accommodation
Residency studios are housed in a traditional stone building that was once a laundry, situated in a secluded area surrounded by farmland and established trees, close to the main house. 
Thanks to a generous donation from Dimplex in 2012, the laundry was renovated to construct four spacious studios, filled with natural light. A river, walled garden, woods, main house and café are all within short walking distance. Each studio is equipped with professional daylight lights, ground source heating, and a kitchen unit. Shared toilets are on each floor. 
Each studio measures 5 by 5 metres and are suitable for most types of work. Wall space is limited, therefore may not be suitable for working with very large pieces. Two of the studios are situated on the ground floor and two on the first floor; the ground floor studios have doors leading directly outside so for this reason may be more suitable for sculptors. There is 24-hour access to the studios.  
Accommodation provides a private bedroom and a shared kitchen and bathroom. For more information about the house and estate visit www.dumfries-house.org.uk

The Hafod residency in Wales offers two Royal Drawing School, Drawing Year alumni a dedicated self-directed two-week residency. 
The Hafod Estate is situated 12 miles south-east of Aberystwyth. The estate is widely regarded as a supreme example of the picturesque landscape in the British Isles. It has been depicted by artists such as Warwick Smith in the 18th Century and John Piper in the 20th Century.

This residency has been made possible with the support of the National Trust.

Artists must be able to drive with access to a car in order to partake in the residency as there is no public transport.

The residency is only open to alumni of the Royal Drawing School’s postgraduate programme, The Drawing Year.

Applications for the 2026 Hafod residency are now closed.

Monet’s Garden residency is underwritten by The Versailles-Giverny Foundation at the Home and Gardens of the painter Claude Monet. 
The gardens of iconic impressionist painter, Monet, gave him his greatest artistic inspiration and made the small villages beside the Seine so well known today. 
The garden is well known for its waterlily pond, exuberant, vivid gardens and iconic Japanese footbridge that were the inspiration for many of Monet’s greatest masterpieces.  
Each year Monet’s Garden, Giverny hosts two artists from the Royal Drawing School on a three-month residency: one alumni from The Drawing Year and one faculty member. 
This is a unique and special opportunity. The emphasis of this residency is to work from observation. Artists in residence are encouraged to work on paper, in sketchbooks or on canvas. Monet’s Garden, Giverny residence is best suited to artists who are interested in working from nature. 
This residency is generously supported by The Versailles-Giverny Foundation.

The residency provides each visiting artist with self-catering studio accommodation, access to a large, shared atelier and workshop space, out-of-hours access to the Giverny gardens, return travel costs and a $10,000 fellowship bursary. 
During Monet’s Garden, Giverny opening hours, the gardens are closed to artists due to large foot fall of visitors to the gardens.

The Royal Drawing School's Drawing Year alumni and faculty are welcome to apply. 
 Application dates 
Applications for the 2026 Giverny Residency are now closed.

The window is a commemoration of three first world war poets who all died as young soldiers on the battle fields of the Somme. 
The panel will be made in Reims from a scaled artist’s drawing by the Atelier Simon Marq, the stained-glass studios responsible for fabricating many of Marc Chagall’s stained-glass windows and Claire Tabouret’s winning design for Paris’ Notre Dame Cathedral new window.

However, you need no previous experience of stained-glass to apply.

The residency is only open to alumni under the age of thirty-five (stipulated to fit the ages of the poets who died), of the Royal Drawing School’s postgraduate programme, The Drawing Year.

Applications are now closed.

A one-month artistic residency in Ascona, on the hill of the mythical Monte Verità
The residency offers one Royal Drawing School Drawing Year Alumni or one Royal Drawing School faculty member a one month residency each year at the Hotel Ascona, home of the Archivio Luigi Pericle.
