The Pastel Society
Drawn To Colour
Artists working in pastel and contemporary dry media are invited to submit their work for the Pastel Society Annual Exhibition 2027
A celebration of colour as subject, expression and connection...
From pastel and pencil to charcoal, crayon, chalk and beyond, our 128th Annual Exhibition will celebrate one of the five essential components of contemporary painting and drawing: colour.
We invite artists to explore how colour can unite us through a shared language of expression, celebrating the possibilities of pastel, dry, and mixed media. 
We welcome works in pastel and other dry media, from black and white to every shade in between. Whether bold or subtle, light or dark, playful or contemplative, we encourage you to be confident in your mark-making. Draw, paint and discover your own language of colour!
Successful applicants can expect:
• To have their work included in the exhibition at Mall Galleries and online
• The opportunity to win prizes and awards worth over £5,000
• An invitation to the Private View
• The chance to sell their work to new collectors
• To be part of a network of exhibiting artists dating back to 1898, when the Pastel Society was founded
• The possibility of election to membership
Submissions are ONLINE ONLY and open from 17 August to 20 November 2026
 Submit Now
Prizes & Awards
Cash Prizes:
Caran d'Ache Prize
£1,000 for the best work in the exhibition as selected by Caran d’Ache
Pastel Society Prize
£1,000 for the best work by a member, selected by the Pastel Society Council
The Yoshimoto Prize
£1,000 for an outstanding work in any dry medium by a non-member, in memory of Eiko Yoshimoto PS (1937-2026)
The President's Prize
£500 for the best work by an artist aged 35 or under
The Bob Last Prize
£400 for a work that celebrates the spirit of Bob Last (1932-2020), a member of the Pastel Society who was known for his imaginative use of dry media, excellent drawing skills, and passion to present work that was different and innovative. With thanks to his daughters, Joanne Last and Jackie Jones, who will select the prize winner.
Product Prizes:
Caran d'Ache Product Prize
Daler-Rowney Prize
£1,000 in art materials from Daler-Rowney: £500 to a member, £500 to a non-member
Frank Herring Award
Henri Roche Award
Mamut Award
Pith Sketchbook Award
UART Award
Unison Member Award
Unison Non-member Award
Unison Young Artist Award
Visitors' Choice Award
A set of Caran d'Ache pastel pencils to the artist whose work receives the most votes from visitors to the exhibition
West Design Award
Publication Prizes:
Painters Online Award
An interview to be published in The Artist section of Leisure Painter & The Artist
Pastel Society Catalogue Awards | First and Second Prize
The winning works illustrated in the exhibition catalogue
Plus:
NEW Mall Galleries / FBA Award
Ten free submissions to exhibitions by the Federation of British Artists at Mall Galleries (worth up to £220) for a non-member exhibitor
Talented artists are vital to the growth and longevity of the Society. This talent can be from any background; what we want to see is enthusiasm, technical skill, originality and innovation in submissions.
 The Pastel Society
Key Dates
Submissions open: Monday 17 August 2026, 12 noon
Submissions close: Friday 20 November, 12 noon
Notification of selection: Friday 4 December, 12 noon
Receiving Day (if selected): Saturday 16 January 2027, 10am to 5pm
Exhibition opens: Wednesday 27 January, 11am to 5pm, then 10am to 5pm daily
Private View (invite only): Wednesday 27 January, 5pm to 8pm, official opening at 6:30pm
Exhibition closes: Saturday 13 February, 5pm
Collection of unsold work: Thursday 18 February, 10am to 5pm
How to Submit
A single-stage online judging of all submitted works will take place, after which selected works should be delivered to Mall Galleries, London, for inclusion in the exhibition:
• Register or log in to our Open Exhibition Submission System (OESS) to submit between 12 noon on Monday 17 August and Friday 20 November 2026
Upload your image/s in JPEG or PNG format and under 5MB. One image per submission must be submitted, showing the complete work. An optional two additional images per work may be submitted, showing details.
The judges will make their decision based on these images, so please ensure that photographs are accurate and show work at its best.
Also required is the title, medium, size (cm), year of completion, and price per work, plus there is the option to add an artwork description.
• Log in to the OESS from 12 noon on Friday 4 December to see if your work has been selected
• If selected, deliver your work on Saturday 16 January 2027, 10am to 5pm, to Mall Galleries, 17 Carlton House Terrace, London SW1Y 5BD
Works should be delivered unwrapped with the relevant form and labels, which are downloadable upon notification of selection.
 Submit Now
Our recent exhibitions have shown that with ‘Fresh Eyes’ and a ‘Direct Touch’, using ‘Pastel Without Boundaries’ is truly ‘Remarkable’ - this year, we want to set an exciting new ‘Benchmark’...
 Simon B. Hodges
 -
 President
Important Information for Artists
Eligibility 
Who may enter?
Any artist aged 18 or over may enter, from anywhere in the world. 
How many works may I enter?
Artists may enter a maximum of six works each, from which up to four works per artist may be selected. 
What type of work is eligible? 
All works submitted must be original creations by the artist. They must demonstrate originality and technical skill.
Work produced under instruction, such as in structured workshops, or work deemed to be derivative of or copied from another artist, will be ineligible for selection.
Works must have been completed within two years prior to the exhibition and must not have been previously exhibited at Mall Galleries.
Works should not exceed 2.4m along their longest dimension. 
Acceptable media: 
All types of pastel including soft pastel, hard pastel, oil pastel, ink pastel, water-based pastel, conté crayons or sticks, sanguine, and other dry mediums that are similar in their application including charcoal, chalk, and pencil. Mixed media and three-dimensional works are welcome where pastel or another dry media is the primary medium.
However, all work that is submitted must have a full description of the media used and any process which has been employed in the finished work beyond drawing and painting, e.g. printing, photography. Please note that failure to do this may result in unnecessary rejection on the grounds that work deserves to be judged on a like for like basis and because any buyer should be made aware of what they are buying.
Submission Fee
How much does it cost to enter?
There is a non-refundable submission fee of £22 per work, or £14.50 per work for artists aged 35 or under.
The submission fee includes free admission to the exhibition for all entrants (normally £7).
Submission fees support the not-for-profit programme at Mall Galleries. The gallery is home to visual arts charity, the Federation of British Artists (Registered Charity Number 200048).
We have partnered with the Visual Artists Association to offer a Free Artist Resource Pack to all entrants. This includes 'The Artist's Guide to Selling Art on Instagram’ (PDF) and 'Instagram for Art Careers’ (Video Masterclass). Entrants will receive instructions to download the Artist Resource Pack upon notification of selection.
Presentation 
How should I present my work?
Works must be framed with picture glass (except in special circumstances as below, or by prior arrangement with the Society). Both the Mall Galleries and the Pastel Society reserve the right to not hang work that is considered ‘not fit for purpose.’
Glazing in Perspex and other similar transparent acrylic materials may be accepted, but only on works arriving from abroad or large works in frames exceeding 100 cm on the longest side.
We advise that all work should be framed with picture glass, however we acknowledge that alternative solutions are being presented for exhibition elsewhere. All works submitted to the exhibition should be framed unless there is a genuine aesthetic or technical reason for the work to remain unframed. If entering unframed work, please indicate it will be unframed in the artwork description. Artists entering unframed work do so at their own risk.
Frames should be sufficiently substantial to withstand mirror plating with 12mm (size 6) screws.
Artists are advised to use plain, simple framing.
Metal frames, unprotected glass edges and clip frames are inadmissible. 
Please remove all fittings and fixings from the back of frames, for example D-rings and picture wire. This is to prevent damage to other works, and because we will mirror-plate works for hanging. 
Delivery & Collection
Works should be delivered and collected on the specified receiving and collection days via the gallery's rear entrance at Mall Galleries, 17 Carlton House Terrace, London SW1Y 5BD. 
If you are unable to deliver or collect your work, you may send another person on your behalf – this may include an art courier (see below).
Artists are responsible for the costs of delivery and collection.
Delivery
Works should be delivered unwrapped with the relevant form and labels, which are downloadable upon notification of selection.
All packaging must be taken away at the point of delivery. 
Collection
We are unable to wrap works or provide wrapping for works being returned. 
Any uncollected works will be removed from the gallery after the collection day and stored by an independent courier company at the artist's expense. 
If works are not collected within 12 months of the collection day, the gallery will be entitled to destroy, sell, or otherwise dispose of the works without consent, prior notification, or compensation to the artist.

Open Call Theme
Open Call Theme
01
A Place Where Disappearance and Emergence Intersect
Brackish estuaries, where rivers meet the sea, support diverse forms of life and are among the environments most vulnerable to climate change. Their waterways, landforms, vegetation and living beings are in constant flux, while the landscapes we see today face the possibility of disappearance.
02
Fleeting Time and Deep Time
The theme begins with the contrast between the brevity of human time—which nevertheless leaves profound and lasting marks on the land—and the land’s deep ecological time, which has sustained life from the distant past to the present. “The Earth Endures” expresses a shared hope that the habitats we must protect, and the relationships they sustain, will endure intact for generations to come.
03
Site-Specific Land-Ecological Art
We invite site-specific works of land and ecological art that move beyond anthropocentric perspectives, reconsider human roles and responsibilities through ecological perspectives and timescales, and explore, through the language of art, the planetary interconnections between humans and non-human beings, nature and cities, and past and future.

About
Background & Aims
Eulsukdo lies in a brackish estuary where fresh water meets the sea. One of Korea’s major migratory bird habitats, it supports diverse forms of life. Although industrialisation, urban development and the Nakdong River Estuary Barrage significantly altered its environment, wetland and habitat restoration has helped revive its ecological vitality.
Now facing sea-level rise and biodiversity loss, Eulsukdo prompts renewed reflection on coexistence between humans and nature. Building on its ecological and historical context, this project uses art to foster environmental awareness and action, and to establish Eulsukdo as a hub for environmental art.
 Today View of Eulsukdo
Aim 01
Reinterpreting Coexistence between Humans and Nature
Moving beyond anthropocentric perspectives, the project considers ecosystems from more-than-human viewpoints and reinterprets the value of coexistence through land and ecological art.
Aim 02
Site-Specific Environmental Art
Reflecting Eulsukdo’s geographical and historical context, the project seeks creative, ecologically responsible works that explore sustainability in an age of climate crisis.
Aim 03
Art that Responds to Nature
Through installation projects that evolve and circulate with nature over time, the project proposes new possibilities for environmental art.
Aim 04
Establishing an Environmental Art Platform
The project strengthens the case for the Nakdong River Estuary’s designation as a National Urban Park and develops Eulsukdo as an international public cultural platform, promoting its ecological identity in Korea and beyond.
Aim 05
Revitalising Culture and Tourism in Western Busan
By creating a distinctive cultural destination that brings together the ecology and art of the Nakdong River Estuary, the project aims to foster local pride and broaden access to cultural experiences.
Eulsukdo
Nakdong estuary · Saha-gu, Busan
1966S
Eulsuldo, An Ecological Haven
Eulsukdo first appeared as an island on a cadastral map in 1916. Recognised for its international importance as a migratory bird habitat, it was designated Natural Monument No. 179 in 1966.
1970s — 1997
Ecological Degradation
From the 1970s onwards, the island’s ecosystem was degraded by the introduction of night-soil treatment, waste disposal and sewage treatment facilities. In particular, large-scale landfilling took place between 1993 and 1997.
1999 — 현재
Restoring the habitat
Eulsukdo was designated a Wetland Protection Area in 1999 and included in the Busan Coastal Special Management Area in 2000. As ecological restoration progressed, parks, visitor trails and cultural facilities were established, including the Nakdong Estuary Eco Center and the Museum of Contemporary Art Busan.
Ongoing
Pursuing Designation as a National Urban Park
Designation of the Nakdong River Estuary as Korea’s first National Urban Park is now being pursued to support its systematic conservation and restoration. Building on sustained efforts by Busan’s civil society since 1999, the National Urban Park system was established in 2016.

Water
Inaugurated in 2013 in the former bottling plant of the Wattwiller springs, the François Schneider Foundation’s Art Centre is a unique venue entirely dedicated to the theme of water. Every year, through temporary exhibitions and cultural projects, this vital element is explored across all its facets: artistic, poetic, aesthetic, geographic, political, and scientific.
Since its launch in 2011, the Talents Contemporains competition dedicated to the theme of water has honored numerous international artists, thereby building a singular and highly original institutional collection of contemporary art.
View the collection
Guidelines and eligibility
The competition is open to visual artists of all nationalities who are of legal age.
Profile: Applicants must demonstrate a solid professional artistic background and/or hold a degree from an art school. To be eligible, candidates must provide evidence of a recent and continuous track record over the past five years through several exhibitions (solo and/or group), publications (monographs, catalogues), or artist residencies.
Eligible Disciplines: Painting, drawing, sculpture, installation, photography, video, textile art, or any other form of fine and visual arts. Note: Performing arts and music are not accepted.
Artwork Specifications: The submitted artwork (whether it consists of a single piece or a body of work) must focus exclusively on the theme of water. Each candidate may submit only one artwork or project per year.
Existing Artwork / Project to be Produced:
Existing Artworks (All disciplines): For painting, drawing, photography, video, textile art, as well as completed sculptures and installations (unique pieces), only the existing artwork can be submitted. No additional production budget will be allocated for these proposals.
Creative Projects (Sculpture and Installation only): Artists working in sculpture or installation have the specific option to apply either with an existing artwork or with a project proposal to be produced. In this second case only, a detailed production budget may be allocated, up to a maximum of €50,000.
Multiple Artworks (Editions): The submitted artwork may be part of a limited edition series for video and photography. If the proposed artwork includes multiple editions, the final grant structure differs and is reduced to €8,000.
Competition Process
Artists are invited to submit their proposals based on the theme of water—whether realistic or utopian, figurative or abstract—by bringing a unique and sensitive perspective to this subject.
Selection of Artworks and Projects
Four Expert Committees and an International Grand Jury will convene successively:
The Expert Committees
Four expert committees, composed of gallerists, art critics, curators, and past competition winners, form pairs to review 200 applications each and shortlist the finalists. The roughly thirty finalist applications are then presented to the Grand Jury.
The International Grand Jury
Chaired by Jean-Noël Jeanneney, this Jury will select 4 to 7 Talents Contemporains laureates from among the thirty finalists. Their artworks will be acquired by the Foundation.
Jean-Noël Jeanneney, Former President of Radio France, former Secretary of State, and former President of the Bibliothèque nationale de France – Paris (France)
Constance de Monbrison, Head of the Insulinde Collections, Musée du Quai Branly – Jacques Chirac – Paris (France)
Alfred Pacquement, Honorary General Curator of Heritage – Paris (France)
Ernest Pignon-Ernest, Artist – Paris (France)
Roland Wetzel, Director of the Museum Tinguely – Basel (Switzerland)
Rosa Maria Malet, Director of the Fundació Joan Miró from 1980 to 2017, Member of the Board of Directors of the Fundació Miró – Barcelona (Spain)
Chiara Parisi, Director of Centre Pompidou-Metz (France)
NB: The composition of the expert committees and the Grand Jury is subject to change based on member availability.
Timeline
September to November: Online call for applications period.
December to February: Review of applications and shortlisting of approximately thirty finalists by the Expert Committees.
March: Official announcement of the finalist artists.
May/June: Deliberations of the International Grand Jury and announcement of the winners.
Autumn (Year N+1): Major group exhibition of the winners at the Wattwiller Art Centre, featuring video portraits of the laureates.
The Prize Grant
For each edition, the International Grand Jury designates a maximum of 7 laureates.
Each winner receives a grant of €15,000 as a merit-based prize and for the official acquisition of their artwork, which then joins the collection of the François Schneider Foundation. (In the case of photographic or video works involving multiple editions, the grant is fixed at €8,000).
The Foundation covers all costs related to the production of the winners’ exhibition at the Wattwiller Art Centre (see rules and regulations).
How to Apply?
Participation in the competition can only be done electronically after registering on the François Schneider Foundation website by clicking the Individual registration or Collective registration buttons at the top of this page.
Applications must be written in French for French-speaking candidates and in English for all other candidates.
Applications must strictly include:
Administrative Section
Registration form and signed, approved Rules and Regulations (PDF format).
A copy of your valid ID (recto/verso ID card or passport) (PDF format).
Artistic Section (Completed artwork or project to be produced, sculpture or installation)
Your CV and/or a presentation of the artists’ collective, demonstrating a professional artistic background (work recently exhibited in institutions, galleries, festivals, etc., or participation in artist residencies) (PDF format, maximum 2 pages).
Your portfolio/artistic dossier presenting an overview of your work (PDF format, maximum 20 A4 pages, maximum 30 MB).
A statement of intent presenting the artwork or project and the artist’s conceptual and creative approach for the competition (PDF format, maximum 2 pages).
A detailed technical specification sheet of the existing artwork or project (sculptures, installations), indicating title, materials, technique, dimensions, weight, constraints, and technical means required for exhibition, installation, or transport (PDF format, maximum 1 page).
A detailed production budget up to a maximum of €50,000 for artworks submitted as project proposals for sculptures and installations (PDF format).
3 to 5 color visuals (photo, drawing, diagram, 3D modeling, floor plan, etc.) (JPG format, maximum 5 MB per visual).
A video excerpt for video works. Video footage may also be attached for other types of artwork (painting, sculpture, etc.) to contextualize them (MOV/MP4 format, maximum 4 GB).
NB: The jury will particularly appreciate clear, concise applications and proposals that align cohesively with the collection of the François Schneider Foundation.
Incomplete applications or those failing to comply with the above instructions will not be submitted to the Expert Committees or the International Grand Jury.
In the event of technical difficulties related to the internet connection, candidates should contact the Organizer as soon as possible. We strongly encourage you to submit your application well in advance to avoid server slowdowns that could prevent your submission from reaching us on time.
IMPORTANT: Under no circumstances should the submitted artworks be designed with the intention of being permanently installed at the Foundation.

Home / News / Art in Manufacturing Open Call: Crown Paints & Fox’s Burton’s Companies UK
26 October 2026 | ← All News
The National Festival of Making invites applications for two paid artist residencies with manufacturers in Lancashire as part of Art in Manufacturing, its headline commissioning programme. Each residency offers the opportunity to develop new work through research and collaboration within a distinctive manufacturing setting.
The residencies will take place between January and June 2027, with completed work presented at the National Festival of Making in Blackburn on 25-27 June 2027, marking ten years since the festival’s founding.
Each residency has a commission budget of £8,000 covering artist fees and the making of the work, plus VAT where applicable, with an additional allowance of up to £600 towards travel and accommodation. Applications are welcome from UK and Ireland based artists and makers working in any art form, as individuals or collectives.
For further information, please download the full application pack here:
Application Pack
Application Pack (Plain Text Version)
Lancashire Residency Partners
Crown Paints, Darwen
Fox’s Burton’s Companies UK, Blackpool, in partnership with LeftCoast.
Artistic Invitation
Art in Manufacturing invites artists to develop ambitious, contemporary work through encounters with manufacturers and spaces of making. Working alongside skilled workforces, artists can explore materials, processes and lived experiences, opening up unexpected connections and revealing perspectives that are often unseen. With curatorial and producing support, we encourage artists to experiment, take creative risks and extend their practice. We welcome outcomes that may be playful, beautiful, humorous and complex, and which create meaningful opportunities for diverse audiences to encounter contemporary work.
The commissioned artist is invited to spend time in the factory, getting to know the workforce and gaining an understanding of material, process and expertise.
As part of the residency, you will have the possibility of access to materials and/or production hours provided by the manufacturer – the scope of this support is to be agreed between the manufacturer, producing team and artist during the residency period.
Exhibition and Presentation
Resulting artworks are presented as part of the National Festival of Making’s programme in venues from Blackburn’s grandest, historic spaces to repurposed town centre shops and public realm spaces. In-situ talks with commissioned artists take the shape of informal In-Conversation discussions and provide insight into the residency experience, along with workshops inspired by and complementing new works.
The festival weekend is a joyful and exploratory gathering where families try a skill for the first time, established makers work with artisan crafters, music and performance is enjoyed across the town centre, thousands of people make things with their hands, and audiences experience new and contemporary work in spaces previously unknown to them.
Art in Manufacturing residencies often cultivate unexpected and diverse outcomes and you can explore all previous artistic outcomes from across the residency programme here.
How to Apply: Please submit your expression of interest to applications@festivalofmaking.co.uk
Deadline: 23 November 2026 at 12 noon.
Interviews will take place on 9 – 14 December 2026. You will be notified if you have been selected for an interview no later than 2 December 2026.
Important Information
If you would like the application information in a different format or to discuss alternative ways to submit an application, please email info@festivalofmaking.co.uk. We are open to many alternative ways to submit including video/audio recordings of commission proposals.
Festival of Making CIC’s aim is that our workforce, contributors and partners are representative of the diverse society we live in and that each individual feels respected, supported and able to give their best. We encourage applications from all backgrounds and communities and welcome discussions about specific individual requirements. Please contact us by emailing info@festivalofmaking.co.uk
Sam Williams Studio + Cardboard Box Company, 2024. Photo by Robin Zahler.
Abigail Hampsey + Bronzecast, JJ Sandham LTD and Artisan Food Producers, 2026. Photo by Robin Zahler.
About Art in Manufacturing
Art in Manufacturing is the National Festival of Making’s headline commissioning programme providing artists with an incomparable platform to make new work in and alongside some of the UK’s major manufacturers and making industries. 
Each season of Art in Manufacturing sees artists paired with leading manufacturers and unique spaces of making, from artisan producers to industry giants. The residency programme creates collaborations with highly skilled workforces, facilitates access to cutting edge technologies and unearths hidden heritages – all resulting in remarkable contemporary artworks that form an integral part of the National Festival of Making programme. 
Art in Manufacturing and the National Festival of Making are curated and produced by Festival of Making CIC.
We invite you to explore the breadth of Art in Manufacturing residencies to date here.

Call for Proposals
Shoeburyness Commission
Budget: £10,000
Deadline: 24 November 2026 (11.59pm – closes at midnight)
Timeline: January to September 2027
Interview: w/c 7 Monday December 2026
Essex Cultural Diversity Project invites proposals for a new project to creatively respond to the history of Shoeburyness near Southend. 
For over a century the ‘Proof and Experimental Establishment’ was a military site for testing ordnance, artillery and ammunition. We have teamed up with the Cart & Wagon Shed, the community and heritage space managed by Shoebury Coastal CIC, to host a commission that aims to engage local communities and underrepresented voices.
We are looking for a project that will creatively collect and bring to life historical and contemporary stories of the people and places across Shoeburyness, which can illustrate the unique heritage of the area and reflect on its history of military, war and defence, as a way to bring into focus themes of community, heritage and care. We want to celebrate the area, enable local people to tell their own stories in their own words, and help shape a strong and collaborative future for Shoeburyness.
To read the full brief and find out how to respond to this opportunity, visit https://essexcdp.com/commission/shoeburynesscallforproposals/
Informal 1-2-1s are available for those wanting to talk through the brief and their proposal, and how to articulate their ideas for the project.
Full Creative Brief 
The project brief with suggested creative starting points is below, and can also be downloaded as a PDF here: Commission Brief – Shoeburyness
How to Respond to this Opportunity
We accept written, verbal and video proposals for this commission. Video proposals should be no longer than 10 minutes in length. To apply, please email your proposal to jo@essexcdp.com by midnight on Tuesday 24 November and include the following:
An outline of the artistic concept, your project title, intended participants and any groups you may like to work with (if known), and your community engagement process (no more than 600 words).
How your practice and project explores or promotes diversity (no more than 200 words).
Some info about you and your work. This could be a short biography/artist statement with examples of previous work / a PDF portfolio / a CV / links to your website and social media.
A short, estimated and basic budget outline, showing how you would utilise the £10,000 (we suggest 4-6 lines)
A short approximate timeline for the work (we suggest 4-6 lines with key milestones)
A completed Commissioning Monitoring Form (please note that, as a MS Word document, on some computers this document goes direct to your downloads folder once clicked – contact jo@essexcdp.com if you have any problems downloading this form)
Further Support & Accessibility
It is highly recommended that you visit the ECDP Commissions Frequently Asked Questions page at which has supporting information and practical advice to support you in putting a proposal together.
We are committed to making our application process accessible, and can be adaptable to your needs. We welcome proposals in various formats, such as a written, video or audio proposals, or via a recorded Zoom call.
If you would like to talk this brief through or need further information about the commission, we’d be very happy to offer a 1-2-1 to support you and answer your questions. Please email Jo on jo@essexcdp.com to arrange a meeting.
To request a text / audio / large print version of this brief, contact Jo at jo@essexcdp.com
FULL CREATIVE BRIEF
Essex Cultural Diversity Project invites proposals for a new project that will creatively respond to the history of Shoeburyness, located to the east of the City of Southend, and help articulate the future aspirations of its community. For over a century, the ‘Proof and Experimental Establishment’ at Shoeburyness was a military site for testing ordnance, artillery and ammunition. We are seeking a project that can reflect on and echo the language of military, war and defence, focussing on community, heritage and care.
We have teamed up with the Cart & Wagon Shed, the community and heritage space managed by Shoebury Coastal CIC, to host a commission that aims to engage local communities and underrepresented voices. We want to celebrate the area, enable local people to tell their own stories in their own words, and play a role in shaping a strong and collaborative future for Shoeburyness.
Through the commission we are looking for a project that will creatively collect and bring to life historical and contemporary stories of the people and places across Shoeburyness, which can illustrate the unique heritage of the area, and provide a platform for less heard and marginalised voices.
Shoebury Coastal CIC have recently secured funding from the National Lottery Heritage Fund to put in place an updated and interactive museum focusing on the area’s military history, social and economic development, as well as its important natural habitats. A new exhibition will draw on some of the 1000s of documents and artefacts that make up the Shoeburyness Archives, which are housed at the Cart & Wagon Shed. It is hoped that some of the commission outcomes could contribute to this larger project and tie in with future exhibitions.
A suggested creative starting point: 
“Proof and Experimental Establishment”
Reflecting military words connected with the site
The military and testing heritage of Shoeburyness is present across the whole area, most prominently at the Garrison and Gunners Park, but also through place names, stories and personal histories, as well as the environment and natural space. The area retains its military testing role through the operations overseen by QinetiQ at the New Ranges and Foulness Island.
In 1905, the Experimental Branch of the School of Gunnery at Shoeburyness became an independent unit and in 1920 was renamed as the Experimental Establishment, commonly referred to as XP. In 1948, XP was re-organised as the Proof and Experimental Establishment (P&EE). For a brief history of Shoeburyness (including military) see www.cartandwagonshed.org/history.
We are interested in gathering stories that can help illustrate the human side of this military heritage, as well as celebrating a site which is currently in transition and transformation. One way forward could be to draw links between the language of military testing with that of community, heritage and care.
For example, ‘Proof’ could be evidence gathered of lives lived – testimony, oral history and the power of community voices – the things we offer as proof of belonging, or as a measure of our care towards each other and the environment. ‘Experimentation’ may be our willingness to try something new for the area, to take risks in a safe environment, and explore creativity as a tool to improve our mental and physical health, or just to play and be curious.
We would also be interested in seeing proposals that explore and celebrate the role of women at the P&EE and QinetiQ, and throw a spotlight on a less well-known part of the history of the operation at Shoeburyness. Women have played key roles over the years, including collecting fired out shells on the perilous mudflats during the Victorian era, and later utilising plotting equipment to collect essential scientific data for proofing and testing trials.
We would like to see project proposals that reflect elements of the above as a starting point, either directly or indirectly, for community engagement, collaboration and co-creation.
Project Approach, Delivery and Final Artwork
Through our commissions, we support participatory practice; the voice of the community is at the heart of all our commissioned projects. We would expect the appointed creative practitioner to act as a bridge between the community, us and our local partners, and be proactive in finding, recruiting and liaising with new audiences and participants. We would like the project to engage no less than 150 individuals; connect with at least three community groups in the area; and deliver at least six workshops for residents and communities.
The creative vision, participatory process and final artwork will be shaped by the creative practitioner, their proposed project and practice, as well as the participants they work alongside.
Regarding the final artwork, we tend not to support large-scale site-specific work or public art, due to limitations of the budget, timescales and ongoing maintenance costs (although this can be considered with a clear and strong proposal with technical evidence and insight). Past commissions have proposed and delivered artworks in various forms, including picnic blanket designs, community films, collective zines, collaborative tapestries, nature habitats designed by school children, shared writing, performances and processions, podcasts, tarot card packs, interactive websites and maps (please refer to the ECDP website for examples of past commissions).
We are happy to be led by the appointed creative practitioner but would expect to see a brief outline of approach and ideas of what the final piece may be in the proposal. The final artwork is to be presented or exhibited at the Cart & Wagon Shed in Summer 2027.
About the Cart & Wagon Shed
Our partner for this commission is the Cart & Wagon Shed, run by the Shoebury Coastal CIC. The building is an early example of a prefabricated iron-frame military building. Built around 1860, it is Grade II listed for its special architectural or historic interest. Sitting at the heart of the redeveloped Shoeburyness Garrison site, it has the historic Garrison buildings to one side and the newly formed Gunners Park to the other. To the front, it sits on the edge of the Thames Estuary with its beautiful and interesting views. Shoebury Coastal CIC is taking inspiration from both the ancient and more modern history of Shoeburyness and the Garrison site, the Shoebury Archives and artefacts, the natural heritage of Gunners Park and the wider nature reserve and Thames Estuary to create a heritage and visitor centre for all to enjoy.
The Cart & Wagon Shed comprises four main internal areas which could be used for project activity (subject to prior agreement and availability): a heritage display hall; archives storage rooms (with space for research); community rooms for workshops, meetings and activities; and a café area. There is also outside garden space. It will be possible for some creative inspiration to be taken from the archives located at the Cart & Wagon Shed.
About ECDP and our Commissions
Our commission call outs are open to creative practitioners working across any media, at any levels of career, as individuals or as part of a collective or a company. This includes, but is not limited to, visual artists, digital artists, writers, poets, performers, theatre practitioners, musicians, dancers and multimedia artists. We are keen to support diverse practitioners and those working in diversity, to develop their socially engaged and participant-led projects and practices.
Successful projects have put communities at the heart of the creative process, while also being central to the artists’ practice and own lines of enquiry. Commissions can capture the spirit of place, give people a voice, connect communities and let people tell their own story in their own words.

• ECDP Commissions: https://essexcdp.com/commissions
• Cart & Wagon Shed: https://www.cartandwagonshed.org/about

APPEL À CANDIDATURE BOURSE "FRANÇOIS DAULTE"
Le musée Fabre conserve depuis 2017 un fonds « François Daulte » constitué du fonds d’archives de l’historien d’art, auteur notamment du premier catalogue raisonné de Frédéric Bazille (1841-1870). À ce fonds s’ajoute un ensemble exceptionnel de 76 lettres autographes de Frédéric Bazille, 8 lettres de son père Gaston Bazille et 22 lettres de ses amis artistes : Claude Monet, Auguste Renoir et Edmond Maître notamment.
Afin de valoriser ce fonds ainsi que plus largement les recherches de François Daulte, il a été décidé l’instauration d’une bourse annuelle « François Daulte » d’un montant de 10 000 €, destinée aux chercheurs post-doctorants.
La bourse de recherche « François Daulte » soutiendra des recherches en histoire et en histoire de l’art dans la lignée des champs d’étude de François Daulte, tout particulièrement sur les thématiques suivantes :
La vie et l’œuvre de Frédéric Bazille, d’Alfred Sisley et d’Auguste Renoir
Les débuts de l’impressionnisme
L’impressionnisme et les arts graphiques
Exposer et collectionner l’impressionnisme
L’histoire de la critique d’art durant la seconde moitié du XIXe siècle
La vie culturelle et artistique à Montpellier durant la seconde moitié du XIXe siècle

[KORRALDAJA LEHT]
ANNONCE DES PROJETS LAURÉATS FIN FÉVRIER 2027
La bourse de recherche curatoriale des Rencontres d'Arles, d’un montant de 20 000 euros, est ouverte à toutes et tous commissaires d’exposition.
Le projet retenu se déroulera en deux phases :
→ temps de recherche autour d'un projet d'exposition.
→ production du projet - soumis à validation.
La bourse d’un maximum de 20 000 euros se compose :
→ d’un premier montant acquis pour le/la lauréat·e de 5 000 euros de droit d'auteur.
→ d’un second montant de 15 000 euros soumis à la validation, pour la production du projet.
RÈGLEMENT DE PARTICIPATION
1 — OBJET
La bourse de recherche curatoriale des Rencontres d’Arles s’adresse aux commissaires d’exposition souhaitant réaliser un projet inédit en lien avec l’image/la photographie. La bourse de recherche et de production reçoit le soutien de Jean-François Dubos.
2 — DOSSIER
LE DOSSIER DE CANDIDATURE EST A REMPLIR EN LIGNE EN CLIQUANT ICI JUSQU'AU 30 NOVEMBRE 2026 :
→ rencontresarles.typeform.com 
LE DOSSIER DOIT SE CONSTITUER DES ELEMENTS SUIVANTS, SELON L’ORDRE INDIQUE CI-DESSOUS, EN UN SEUL PDF (10 MO MAXIMUM) : 
→ un texte de présentation du projet d’exposition proposé pour la bourse de recherche (maximum 5000 signes), corpus des œuvres et des artistes envisagés pour le projet (il est vivement recommandé de présenter des visuels), budget prévisionnel de recherche (5 000 euros), échéancier de recherche et budget prévisionnel de production de l’exposition (15 000 euros) dans les enveloppes imparties.
→ biographie du/de la commissaire (ou des co-commissaires/du collectif le cas échéant) avec formation, coordonnées complètes et liste des projets et expositions du (des) commissaire(s), reprenant les présentations et vues (dans le cas d'expositions) des différents projets réalisés par la/le ou les commissaire(s).
Les textes doivent être en français ou en anglais, idéalement les deux.
3 — RECHERCHE & PRODUCTION
PHASE 1 — RECHERCHE
→ À partir de la sélection du projet, le/la commissaire recevra une bourse de 5 000 euros pour ses frais et droits d'auteur.
→ Le budget et le planning seront soumis à la direction des Rencontres d’Arles pour validation.
→ La/le commissaire aura six mois de temps de recherche à l’issue desquels il/elle devra proposer une note à la direction artistique des Rencontres d’Arles. Après un arbitrage artistique, les Rencontres d’Arles valideront ou non la faisabilité du projet et son format de restitution (phase 2).
PHASE 2 — PRODUCTION & RÉALISATION DU PROJET
Après accord, si le projet est validé par les Rencontres d’Arles à l’issue des 6 mois de recherche, le projet passera en phase de réalisation et de production et sera accompagné par les Rencontres d’Arles.
→ Le budget de 15 000 euros piloté par les Rencontres d'Arles comprend :
- prêts des œuvres
- transports des œuvres jusqu’à Arles (aller-retour)
- productions des œuvres : tirages/encadrements, wallpapers, vidéos, etc.
- invitation du commissaire et éventuellement prise en charge des artistes à Arles pendant la semaine d'ouverture (et/ou le montage de l'exposition).
- assurance
- etc.
→ Le/la commissaire s’engage à :
- sélectionner les œuvres constituant le corpus de l’exposition et en déterminer les droits de présentation et de reproduction.
- concevoir et rédiger un texte de présentation de la sélection des photographies.
- être présent·e lors de la semaine d’ouverture du festival et participer à la visite guidée de l’exposition.
En plus de ce budget, seront pris en charge par les Rencontres d’Arles : la scénographie, la communication, le montage et le démontage des œuvres, le gardiennage.
4 – CALENDRIER
→ 16 septembre 2026
ouverture des candidatures
→ 30 novembre 2026
date limite de l’envoi des candidatures
→ fin février 2027
annonce des projets lauréats
→ jusqu’à l’été 2027
phase 1 de recherche
→ de septembre à mi-octobre 2027
restitution de l’étude, puis si validation, phase 2 de production du projet.
5 — TERMES ET CONDITIONS 
5.1 — Phases du projet 
PHASE 1
Le/la commissaire bénéficie de six mois de recherche dans lesquels il/elle s’engage à déployer ses meilleurs efforts dans le cadre des travaux préparatoires d’une Exposition. 
À partir de septembre jusqu’à mi-octobre au plus tard (date à convenir ultérieurement), à l’issue des travaux préparatoires, le/la commissaire envoi un dossier au jury comprenant : 
Une note artistique sous forme d’un texte original de présentation de la sélection des photographies (2000 signes, espaces compris). 
Une sélection d’œuvres constituant le corpus de l’Exposition projetée 
L’identification des droits de représentation et de reproduction afférant aux œuvres sélectionnées, qui pourraient avoir vocation à être présentées et/ou reproduites dans le cadre de l’Exposition projetée 
Un budget prévisionnel détaillant les postes énumérés ci-dessus 
Un rétroplanning 
Le/la commissaire d’exposition présentera ce dossier au jury à l’occasion d’un rendez-vous planifié ultérieurement entre septembre et mi-octobre 2027. À l’issue de ce rendez-vous, Les Rencontres d’Arles valideront ou non le projet et en feront part par mail au commissaire, dans un délai de 6 mois au plus tard après la remise de la dernière version du projet.
PHASE 2
Les Rencontres d’Arles disposent d’une pleine et entière liberté éditoriale et de direction artistique quant à la programmation de l’Exposition dans une de ses éditions et restent donc libres de valider ou pas le projet d’Exposition remis à la fin de la phase 1. 
→ En cas de non-validation des Travaux préparatoires 
Le/la commissaire sera libre de produire l’Exposition à ses frais avec tout tiers de son choix. 
Les Rencontres d’Arles ayant soutenu les travaux préparatoires, le/la commissaire s’engage, en cas de présentation du projet dans un autre cadre d’exposition, que soit mentionné sur tous support, « travaux de recherche soutenus par la bourse de recherche curatoriale 2027 des Rencontres d’Arles ».
→En cas de validation des Travaux préparatoires 
Dans le cas où l’exposition serait programmée dans le cadre d’une des éditions des Rencontres d’Arles, un nouveau contrat sera signé entre le/la commissaire et les Rencontres d’Arles.
5.2 — Cession des droits d’auteurs 
Le/la commissaire cède aux Rencontres d’Arles ses droits de représentation et le droit de reproduction sur les travaux préparatoire, ce compris, la rédaction du texte de présentation des photographies sélectionnées, en France et à l’étranger, sur tous supports habituellement utilisés par les Rencontres d’Arles. 
En cas de validation des travaux préparatoires et de la tenue de l’exposition, cette cession autorise les Rencontres d’Arles à produire, faire promotion de, et organiser l’exposition. 
Le/la commissaire garantit aux Rencontres d’Arles la jouissance des droits cédés contre tout trouble, revendication ou éviction quelconque. 
5.3 — Paiement des droits d’auteur 
En contrepartie de la réalisation des travaux préparatoires réalisés par le/la commissaire et la cession afférente des droits d’auteur, le Rencontres d’Arles s’engagent à verser au/ à la commissaire la somme de 5 000€ bruts. 
Il est entendu que cette rémunération restera acquise au/à la commissaire, même dans l’hypothèse où les travaux de recherche n’auraient pas été validées à l’issue de la phase 1, où que l’exposition projetée n’aurait pas lieu, et que l’organisation de l’Exposition, si celle-ci est validée (phase 2), ne donnera pas lieu au paiement d’une rémunération complémentaire. 
La bourse de recherche et de production reçoit le soutien de Jean-François Dubos.

Beam Camp Seeks Ambitious Project Proposals for 2027 season
Beam Center seeks design proposals for an ambitious public artwork that will be brought to life through collaborations between youth, Beam Camp staff and the selected proposer. Projects will be realized by a community of more than 100 young people at Beam Camp in July 2026.
Beam Camp is a specialized summer camp for building and collaboration located in Strafford, NH. Our award-winning program offers youth (ages 9-17) the opportunity to cultivate hands-on skills while exploring innovative thinking, design, problem solving and the creative process.
Every year, Beam Camp solicits proposals for unique and spectacular large-scale projects that serve as the centerpiece for the four week session of camp. Our Project Team works with the winning designers to translate their vision into a real construction reflecting a high level of craftsmanship and skill by 100 campers and 20+ staff. Projects are always ambitious and technically challenging, and in many cases our Big Project becomes the world we live in during our time at camp. The themes and questions introduced by our project circulate to all parts of camp and make each Summer at Beam distinctly exciting from the next.. Please take some time to familiarize yourself with our past projects.
Winning proposals will be selected by a committee composed of Beam Center staff, youth, past project designers, and community members. We welcome proposals from all over the world and from people of any age, and while we recognize the usefulness of AI, we ask that you use it sparingly. We would rather see and hear about an idea from its human designer(s) because they are the ones who can tell the story best. 
We will be holding two Zoom info sessions for prospective project proposers. Please register:
Thursday, October 22nd at 2:00 PM
Saturday, November 21st at 2:00PM
Beam Camp is looking for the following:
Proposals from creative individuals with big ideas, including but not limited to Artists, Engineers, Architects, Builders, Filmmakers, Musicians, Designers, Technologists, etc.
Big ideas that result in a unique, ambitious, and spectacular product
Proposals that communicate a clear vision (sketches, diagrams, and other visuals are always helpful) and represent your/your team’s expertise
Projects that are ambitious enough to occupy and challenge 100 campers and 20+ staff members for approximately 50 hours
Projects that take advantage of Beam’s facilities, community, landscape and rural setting
Projects that use a range of materials, processes and techniques
Projects that incorporate entry points for camper and staff worldbuilding.
Projects that allow us to create the majority of the components onsite and from scratch
Beam Camp Disciplines and Facilities include:
Full wood and metal shops, equipped with a range of hand and power tools
Welding facilities
Textile, dye and sewing stations
Ceramic studio
Molding and casting facilities
Technology lab
Audio equipment and instrument selection
Commercial Kitchen
Project Site: Beam Project NH
Location: Beam Camp in Strafford, NH
Completion: Summer 2027
Past projects: Theater of Giants (2025), Welcome Beacon(2023), As Above, So Below (2022), and A Universe (2021), Trip To The Sun (2010)
Maps and Images of Beam Camp
Award, Project Budget and Selected Artist Expectations:
Selected project proposers receive a $5,000 award
Selected projects have approximately a $15,000 fabrication budget
Selected proposers should have a general understanding of the processes, techniques, and materials involved in their proposal

The opportunity is open to artists from Devon or Cornwall to apply in collaboration with another artist based in the UK. Continuing Freelands Foundation’s commitment to supporting the relationship between making and learning, the residency offers artists an opportunity to invite a new person into their practice through a shared residency supporting experimentation and exchange through making.

Artists currently enrolled in formal education (e.g., BA/MA/PhD programmes) are not eligible.

About the Porthmeor Residencies
The 2027 Two Together: Porthmeor Studios Residencies offer the opportunity for three pairs of visual artists to undertake a shared residency at the historic Porthmeor Studios in St Ives, Cornwall, to enable exchange and learning. 
Artists from Devon or Cornwall are invited to apply with another UK-based artist. 
Applicants are encouraged to consider how you will benefit from working together, how your practices connect, and why this residency is timely for you both, as well as how a shared studio space will benefit each of you. The residency necessitates process-led experimentation. We are interested to see practices, ideas and projects developed through an engagement with materials and materiality.
Continuing Freelands Foundation's commitment to supporting the relationship between making and learning, this residency offers artists an opportunity to invite a new person into their practice. Selected pairs will work alongside one another in Porthmeor’s Studio 5 across a month-long residency.
Two Together: Porthmeor Studios Residencies is held in partnership with the Borlase Smart John Wells Trust.

About the opportunity
The Two Together residencies emphasise exploration, experimentation and shared learning, allowing artists to focus on creative growth and exchange through making.
We are seeking joint applications from two visual artists—one of whom must be based in Devon or Cornwall–who do not already work together in an existing partnership. 
Each pair will have access to a large, shared studio, shared accommodation, travel support and a stipend to cover living costs for one month. Artists will be encouraged to document their experience, though there is no expectation of final work(s) or resolved outcomes. 
Residents will receive:
Use of Studio 5 at Porthmeor Studios (shared with your collaborator). 
Accommodation in St. Ives, Cornwall (shared with your collaborator). 
Travel expenses covered to and from St. Ives, Cornwall. 
£2,000 stipend per artist to participate and cover living costs during the residency. 
Support from Porthmeor Studios and Freelands Foundation. 
A unique opportunity to learn from and experiment with another artist in a supportive, process-driven environment. 
It's a rare privilege to be working so closely alongside another artist with a sustained insight into each other's workflows and obsessions... Returning to our studio practices after this month of experiments, we are derailed in the best way. 
Hugh Frost & Leomi Sadler, Two Together 2026 residency pair. 
Who can apply
Artists must be based in the UK, with a studio-based visual arts practice. 
Applicants must have at least 5 years of professional practice (five years after graduating from BA, or equivalent experience). 
Each application must include a collaborator. 
One artist must be based in Devon or Cornwall. 
Artists who are in an existing creative, professional or personal partnership are not eligible to apply together to this opportunity. This includes artist collectives or duos. 
Artists currently enrolled in formal education (e.g., BA/MA/PhD programmes) are not eligible. 
Artists who are employees, trustees or funders of BSJWT or Freelands Foundation are not eligible for this opportunity. 
Both artists must be available for at least one of three proposed residency months: March, May, and September 2027. The residency dates will be agreed with successful applicants.

About the Porthmeor Residencies
Porthmeor Studios in St Ives, Cornwall, has been a nurturing and generative space for artists’ practice for decades – providing studios for local artists and artist residency opportunities. Recent residency artists include Sadia Pineda Hameed, Rebecca Moss, Rae-Yen Song, Rana Begum, Nicholas Deshayes, Lubaina Himid, Richard Long, Katy Moran, Veronica Ryan, Daniel Sinsel, Noorain Inam, and Hannah Quinlan & Rosie Hastings. Working in partnership with the Borlase Smart John Wells Trust (BSJWT), who manage Porthmeor Studios, Freelands Foundation has created a residency opportunity for artists in this unique space.
Freelands Foundation champions art education, believing in the intrinsic value of art and that making is fundamental. At Freelands Foundation we create programmes based on testing approaches that support the different ways that artists learn. Both Freelands Foundation and BSJWT recognise the vital role that the studio can play as a space for learning, making and experimentation, and how developing networks and opportunities for artists to collaborate with their peers around the country can support artist development over the short and longer term.

2027 Vital Impacts Fellowships and Mentorships open in August. Learn more and apply here.
View the 2026 winners here.
Vital Impacts is dedicated to supporting visual storytellers who capture compelling, solutions-focused environmental stories at the local level. We are excited to offer one (1) $20,000 fellowship and six (6) $5,000 fellowships to help bring these vital stories to life.
Fellowship recipients will have twelve months to develop their projects, with support from Vital Impacts to publish and showcase their work.
Additionally, ten (10) emerging photographers will be chosen to participate in an intensive mentorship program, designed to nurture their growth and enhance their craft.
All applicants are also welcome to join our online speaker series, which provides valuable insights and guidance to all who are interested.
FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
The Fellowships
Vital Impacts is thrilled to introduce our fellowships, named in honor of legendary environmental advocates whose groundbreaking work has inspired global change. 
The Dr. Jane Goodall Environmental Photography Fellowship ($20,000)
We are deeply honored to announce that one of our Vital Impacts Environmental Photography Fellowships will carry the name of Dr. Jane Goodall.
Dr. Goodall’s extraordinary journey has not only transformed our understanding of primates but has also profoundly deepened our bond with the natural world. Her groundbreaking research opened our eyes to the rich emotional lives of chimpanzees, while her relentless advocacy through the Jane Goodall Institute has galvanized a global movement to protect endangered species and their precious habitats.
The Vital Impacts Jane Goodall Fellowship, honoring the iconic ethologist and conservationist, will support a photographer dedicated to telling powerful, solutions-focused environmental stories. It is with immense pride and gratitude that we celebrate Dr. Goodall’s lasting legacy and unwavering dedication to both humanity and the planet. Her spirit of hope and resilience continues to inspire us all to make a difference.
The Dr. Sylvia Earle Environmental Photography Fellowship ($5,000)
The Dr. Sylvia Earle Environmental Photography Fellowship honors Dr. Sylvia Earle, an oceanographer and tireless advocate for marine conservation. Recognized as TIME magazine’s "Hero for the Planet" and a “Living Legend” by the Library of Congress, Dr. Earle has shattered records and set new standards with over 7,500 hours underwater. Her achievements include leading the first all-female team of “Aquanauts” in 1970, setting a world untethered diving record in 1979, and serving as Chief Scientist for NOAA, the first woman in that role.
In 2008, Dr. Earle founded Mission Blue to create a global network of marine protected areas, known as Hope Spots, aiming to protect 30% of the world’s oceans by 2030. The Dr. Sylvia Earle Emerging Photographer Fellowship honors her legacy by supporting photographers who capture the beauty and critical state of our oceans, inspiring action and awareness through powerful visual storytelling.
The Hindou Oumarou Ibrahim Environmental Photography Fellowship ($5,000)
The Hindou Oumarou Ibrahim Environmental Photography Fellowship honors Hindou Oumarou Ibrahim, an Indigenous environmental activist and member of Chad’s pastoralist Mbororo people. This fellowship recognizes her lifelong dedication to advocating for Indigenous rights and protecting the environment.
Since founding the Association for Indigenous Women and Peoples of Chad (AFPAT) at the age of 12, Ibrahim has tirelessly worked to elevate Indigenous voices and safeguard their lands from degradation. She has held leadership roles in global climate negotiations, including serving as co-chair of the International Indigenous Peoples Forum on Climate Change at COP21, and continues to positively influence international policy.
We hope this fellowship inspires and supports storytelling works that promote Indigenous experiences and knowledge in the fight to save our planet.
The Ian Lemaiyan Environmental Photography Fellowship ($5,000)
We are honored to name The Ian Lemaiyan Environmental Photography Fellowship in memory of Ian Lemaiyan, whose vibrant spirit left an indelible mark on everyone who knew him. Ian’s journey began with a passion for studying rhino behavior and blossomed into a distinguished career as a conservation pilot. His vital work, which included critical aerial surveys and anti-poaching patrols across Kenya, demonstrated his deep commitment to wildlife protection and his love for flying.
Ian also had a deep love for photography and film, and his work was featured in Wildlife Warriors and The Flying Maasai. 
We also wish to acknowledge the continuing inspiration of Ian’s family, especially his son, Louis. Our aim with this fellowship is to support young dreamers who, like Ian, aspire to make a meaningful difference in the world and honor the remarkable legacy that continues to inspire us all.
The Chico Mendes Environmental Photography Fellowship ($5,000)
The Chico Mendes Environmental Photography Fellowship commemorates the remarkable life of Chico Mendes, a laborer turned environmentalist who championed the preservation of the Amazon rainforest and the rights of local and Indigenous communities.
As a Brazilian rubber tapper and land rights leader, Mendes created the world’s first tropical forest conservation initiative led by the forest peoples themselves. His work led to the establishment of Brazil's extractive reserves—protected forest areas managed by local communities. Chico Mendes dedicated his life to safeguarding the Amazon, inspiring the next wave of environmental activism and leaving a lasting legacy of environmental and social justice.
We hope that this fellowship will inspire unrelenting bravery and fierce determination to protect and preserve the natural world.
The Madonna Thunder Hawk Environmental Photography Fellowship ($5,000)
The Madonna Thunder Hawk Environmental Photography Fellowship will honor Madonna Thunder Hawk, an activist and a guiding force for generations of Native American leaders. 
Ms. Thunder Hawk's tireless advocacy for justice and environmental protection has left an indelible mark on the world. From her pivotal role in the Red Power Movement and the occupation of Alcatraz, to her leadership in the American Indian Movement and the Black Hills Alliance, her dedication to protecting both people and the environment is unparalleled. 
She was the tribal liaison for the Lakota People's Law Project, and today, serves as an advisor to the Warrior Women Project and the Director of Grassroots Organizing for the Red Road Institute, where she remains a fierce advocate for Indigenous rights and environmental justice. 
This fellowship will reflect her legacy by supporting a photographer whose work highlights impactful, solutions-based environmental stories. We are honored to celebrate her enduring influence and commitment through this recognition.
The E.O. Wilson Environmental Photography Fellowship ($5,000)
The E.O. Wilson Environmental Photography Fellowship celebrates the memory and legacy of Dr. E.O. Wilson, a renowned biologist whose work has shaped modern conservation science. His innovative concept of "Half-Earth" advocates for dedicating half of the Earth's surface to nature, aiming to halt the global extinction crisis. 
Through his influential writings and the establishment of the E.O. Wilson Biodiversity Foundation's Half-Earth Project, Wilson's legacy continues to inspire efforts to protect and restore the world's ecosystems for future generations. Through this fellowship, we hope to counter the onward march of the Anthropocene and help foster a reconciliation between humanity and the natural world.
The Requirements
Vital Impacts is seeking local photographers and visual storytellers who are deeply embedded in their communities and uniquely positioned to document environmental and conservation issues within their own surroundings. We aim to support work that explores both the complexity of these challenges and the solutions emerging in response, highlighting innovative conservation efforts, strengthening connections between communicators and practitioners, and inspiring action and hope through stories of resilience and possibility.
It is imperative that fellowship recipients focus on documenting a story within their own community. Our goal is to bolster local journalism, so we're specifically targeting photographers rooted in the communities they aim to spotlight. We won't be considering applications from photographers residing outside of the respective community or country. 
Applicants are encouraged to apply in their native language or in English. For proposals submitted in foreign languages, we'll arrange for translation services to ensure fair evaluation and consideration. 
All applicants must follow the Vital Impacts Code of Ethics and be able to agree to and sign our Environmental Fellowship Agreement. 
Grantees cannot be the target of sanctions or located or resident in a country, territory or region that is the target of comprehensive territorial sanctions. 
Prior publication experience is not a requirement. Vital Impacts is particularly interested in uplifting photographers who have been working on long term projects and who have existing relationships with the stakeholders in this issue. 
Previous Recipients
Prior applicants as well as previous fellowship and mentorship recipients are welcome to reapply. View the recipients of the 2024, 2025, and 2026 Vital Impacts Environmental Fellowship and Mentorships. 
The Timeline
APPLICATIONS OPEN: 31 AUGUST 2026
SUBMISSION DEADLINE: 30 NOVEMBER 2026
GRANT WINNERS AND MENTORSHIP RECIPIENTS ANNOUNCED: JANUARY 2027 
Entrance Fee
$25. Fee may be waived for economic hardship. The fee is waived for all applicants from developing countries. Please reach out to hello@vitalimpacts.org for fee waiver codes. 
Photos by Musuk Nolte, CBS/Landov, Rip Evans, @AmiVitale, Courtesy of Stephanie Hauser, Miranda Smith, Courtesy of Madonna Thunder Hawk and Jay Vavra, with permission from the E.O. Wilson Biodiversity Foundation.
Meet the Judges
Kathy Moran
Kathy Moran, former Deputy Director of Photography for National Geographic magazine, has been producing projects about terrestrial and underwater ecosystems since 1990 and has edited more than 350 stories for the publication. Her collaboration with photographer Nick Nichols and Dr. Michael Fay played a pivotal role in establishing Gabon’s national park system. Additionally, she is a founding member of the International League of Conservation Photographers and has served on its Executive Committee.
Gail Fletcher
Gail Fletcher is the Lead Photo Editor at The Guardian, where she develops and produces award-winning visual stories. She is also on the faculty at the International Center of Photography and was previously an Associate Photo Editor at National Geographic.
She has served as a juror for the Alexia Grant, Review Santa Fe, American Photography, and World Report Award, among others. She regularly reviews portfolios to help photographers and artists refine their work.
Laura Covelli
Laura Covelli is the curator of the Festival della Fotografia Etica in Lodi, Italy. She has worked at the festival for 10 years, coordinating and supervising educational programs for students and teachers, the World Report Award, and the nonprofit Open Call. She also carries out educational activities with a particular focus on social photography and reportage.
Alessia Glaviano
Alessia Glaviano is the Head of Global PhotoVogue and Director of the PhotoVogue Festival, where she works to champion emerging and established talent and influence visual literacy to help shape a more just, ethical, and inclusive visual world. Since PhotoVogue launched in 2011, Glaviano has helped grow the platform into a globally recognized community with over 300,000 photographers.

Season Theme
Belonging
This theme invites young artists to explore what it means to belong -
to a place, a culture, a community, or to themselves.
Belonging can be inherited, constructed, questioned, or lost.
It can exist between worlds, across borders, or entirely within.
A reflection on identity, memory, and connection in a constantly shifting world.
 Unlock the Theme 
Explore the memories, traditions, and histories that shape your sense of belonging.
ROOTS
& MEMORY
BETWEEN WORLDS
What does it mean to exist between cultures, identities, or places?
HOME
Is home a place, a feeling, or a moment in time?
What does belonging feel like within yourself?
Can you feel at home in your own mind and emotions?
INNER WORLD
Where do you imagine your place in the future?
FUTURE BELONGING
IDENTITY
How do you define yourself beyond labels and expectations?
OUTSIDER
How does the digital world shape identity, presence, and belonging?
DIGITAL BELONGING
COMMUNITY
Who do you feel connected to, and what defines that connection?
What does it mean to not belong — and how does that shape you?

Natalia Kapchuk
Natalia Kapchuk is an internationally recognised contemporary artist and environmentalist based between Dubai and London. Her multidisciplinary practice explores the relationship between ecological systems, human intervention and the natural world through painting and mixed-media sculpture. Working with natural, reclaimed and industrial materials, she develops research-driven projects addressing biodiversity loss, industrialisation, sustainability and the long-term impact of human activity on natural ecosystems. She further developed her artistic education at Central Saint Martins and Chelsea College of Arts, both part of University of the Arts London.
Kapchuk has exhibited internationally across Europe, the Middle East and Asia, with her work presented at major cultural platforms and institutions including Expo 2020 Dubai, CICA Museum in South Korea, ME Dubai Hotel, as well as public art venues in London and New York. Her works have also been presented at international auctions, including Phillips and Christie’s, and are held in private collections in the United Kingdom, France, the United Arab Emirates and India. Her artistic and environmental work has received international recognition, including distinctions from the Parliamentary Society of Arts, Fashion and Sports and the Michelangelo International Art Prize.
Alongside her artistic practice, Kapchuk is actively engaged in international environmental advocacy. She serves as an Ambassador of the Parliamentary Society of Arts, Fashion and Sports (UK) and a Goodwill Ambassador for the Better World Fund (BWF). She has collaborated with environmental organisations including The Ocean Cleanup, Born Free Foundation, Earthwatch Europe and Plastic Oceans Europe, using art and public engagement to raise awareness of environmental challenges and encourage greater responsibility towards the natural world.
Contemporary Artist and Environmentalist
Ashraf Abuissa
Entrepreneur, philanthropist, and patron of the arts, Ashraf Abu Issa is the Chairman of Abuissa Holding, one of the Middle East’s leading family-owned conglomerates with diversified operations in retail, distribution, real estate, and investments.
A passionate art collector and cultural advocate, Mr. Abu Issa is also the Founder and CEO of AlBahie Auction House, Qatar’s first fine art and antiques auction house, and Owner of Bissan Gallery, a contemporary art gallery that supports regional and international artists. Through these ventures, he has played a key role in enriching Qatar’s cultural landscape, fostering artistic dialogue, and supporting the creative economy in the region.
His dedication to the arts extends beyond business — Mr. Abu Issa actively supports emerging artists, art education, and heritage preservation, believing in art’s power to connect people and tell stories across generations.
In recognition of his entrepreneurial leadership and commitment to community development, he was named Ernst & Young Entrepreneur of the Year in 2011. He also co-founded INJAZ Qatar, a non-profit organization empowering youth through education, entrepreneurship, and innovation.
Through his vision, philanthropy, and cultural engagement, Ashraf Abu Issa continues to bridge commerce and creativity, championing initiatives that inspire dialogue, innovation, and cultural appreciation across Qatar and beyond.
Chairman, Abuissa Holding | Founder, AlBahie Auction House & Bissan Gallery | Art Collector
Azza Al Qubaisi
Azza Al Qubaisi is a pioneering Emirati multidisciplinary artist, sculptor and designer, recognised as the UAE’s first Emirati jewellery artist. Born and based in Abu Dhabi, her practice explores Emirati identity, heritage and the natural landscape through sculpture, jewellery and public art.
Working across metals and natural materials, including palm fronds, Al Qubaisi combines traditional craftsmanship with contemporary forms. Her work draws on the landscapes, materials and visual culture of the UAE, exploring the relationship between cultural memory, identity and place.
Her work has been presented internationally, including at Forever Is Now at the Giza Pyramids, the Smithsonian Folklife Festival in Washington, D.C., Sotheby’s London, Expo Milano and exhibitions in Berlin. More recently, she participated in the Abu Dhabi Public Art Biennial 2024–2025 and exhibited with Leila Heller Gallery in New York in 2025.
Beyond her artistic practice, Al Qubaisi is committed to supporting emerging creative talent. She is the founder of the Ebda’a Awards, a long-running platform dedicated to discovering and developing emerging jewellery designers, and has contributed extensively to cultural initiatives, education and creative development in the UAE.
Al Qubaisi holds a BA in Jewellery Design, Silversmithing and Allied Crafts from London Guildhall University and an MA in Cultural and Creative Industries from the Higher Colleges of Technology. She is a recipient of the British Council Young Creative Entrepreneur Award and the Emirates Woman of the Year Award.

2-minutes-for-peace-international-open-c.text:
2 Minutes for Peace is an international open call inviting people worldwide to share a short video expressing what peace means to them. Through storytelling, images, words, music, or everyday moments, create a video of up to two minutes reflecting on peace, dialogue, coexistence, solidarity, and hope. The project brings together diverse voices and stories to show how peace can be imagined, experienced, and communicated. Filmmakers, artists, storytellers, students, activists, and anyone with a story to share are welcome.
Who can apply: Anyone worldwide can apply. The call is open to filmmakers, artists, storytellers, students, activists, and anyone with a story, idea, or personal perspective on peace to share. 
What you get: Participants have the opportunity to share their voice internationally, contribute to a collective storytelling project for peace, and connect with diverse perspectives from around the world. Selected videos may be featured through Storytellers for Peace and its communication channels. 
Deadline 01 December 2026
