2 MINUTES FOR PEACE
International Open Call 2026
One story. Two minutes. A world of peace.
Storytellers for Peace invites storytellers, filmmakers, performers, writers, artists and anyone with a story to tell to take part in an international open call dedicated to peace.
We are looking for short original videos, no longer than two minutes, telling a story about peace.
It can be a true story or a fictional one.
It can be intimate or universal, poetic or humorous, dramatic or unexpected.
It can be about a person, a relationship, a community, a choice, a memory, a place or an idea.
Because peace is not only the absence of war.
Peace can be dialogue.
Reconciliation.
Dignity.
Understanding.
Coexistence.
Forgiveness.
Solidarity.
The courage to choose another way.
Tell us your story.
THE CHALLENGE
Create or choose a video of no more than two minutes telling a story about peace.
There is no required genre or production style.
We welcome:
fiction; 
documentary; 
personal stories; 
theatre and performance; 
animation; 
poetry and spoken word; 
visual storytelling; 
experimental video; 
stories inspired by real events; 
stories created with a smartphone; 
any other form of storytelling. 
Professional production is not required.
A powerful story is more important than an expensive production.
WHO CAN PARTICIPATE?
The call is international and open to anyone aged 18 or over.
There are no restrictions based on nationality or country of residence.
Participation is free.
You may participate individually or as part of a creative team, provided that the person submitting the video is at least 18 years old and has the necessary rights and permissions concerning the submitted work.
YOU DON'T HAVE TO SEND US YOUR VIDEO
This is the simple part.
Publish your video on your own YouTube channel and send us the link.
No video file needs to be uploaded to Storytellers for Peace.
We recommend that the video be set to Public, so that people can discover both your story and your work as a storyteller.
You keep your video.
You keep your channel.
You keep your audience.
Storytellers for Peace will help discover, select and promote stories and storytellers from around the world.
CAN I SUBMIT A VIDEO I HAVE ALREADY MADE?
Yes.
The video does not have to have been created specifically for this open call.
You may submit a new video or a previously published video, provided that it meets the requirements of this call and that you have the necessary rights and permissions to submit it.
Maybe you already have a story worth sharing.
LANGUAGE
Videos may be made in any language.
If the video is not in English, it must include English subtitles.
HOW TO PARTICIPATE
It's simple:
1. Create or choose your video.
2. Upload it to your YouTube channel.
3. Make sure it is public.
4. Complete the Storytellers for Peace submission form.
5. Paste the YouTube link.
That's it.
The submission form is intentionally short.
DEADLINE
1 DECEMBER 2026
The open call launches on:
21 SEPTEMBER 2026
International Day of Peace
The 2026 United Nations theme is:
“Invest in Peace – For Everyone, Everywhere, Every Day.”
The initiative will then lead towards:
1 JANUARY 2027
World Day of Peace
The theme for the 2027 World Day of Peace is:
“Disarming Technology, Serving Peace. Politics as Preventive Responsibility.”
These two dates frame our journey.
But the invitation is simple:
Tell us your story about peace.
WHAT HAPPENS TO THE SELECTED STORIES?
Storytellers for Peace will select a number of stories to be featured through its international network.
Selected videos may be:
embedded on the Storytellers for Peace website;
featured on the Storytellers for Peace YouTube channel; 
included in articles, playlists, presentations and communications related to the initiative; 
promoted with appropriate attribution to the original creator and, where possible, a link to the original YouTube video. 
The original video remains on the creator's YouTube channel.
STORYTELLERS FOR PEACE AWARD
A selection of outstanding stories may receive the:
STORYTELLERS FOR PEACE AWARD
The selection will consider:
the strength of the story; 
originality; 
storytelling ability; 
emotional or human impact; 
relevance to the idea of peace; 
the ability to communicate something meaningful within two minutes. 
Technical production quality will not be the only or principal criterion.
A powerful story is more important than an expensive production.
There is no cash prize attached to the award.
The greatest opportunity is to have your story discovered and promoted through an international storytelling network.
JOIN THE NETWORK
Selected storytellers may also be invited to become part of the international:
STORYTELLERS FOR PEACE NETWORK
and to participate in future collaborations, projects and initiatives.
The purpose of this open call is not simply to collect videos.
It is to discover people who believe that stories can contribute to a more peaceful world.
ONE STORY.
TWO MINUTES.
A WORLD OF PEACE.
18+ | FREE | WORLDWIDE
MAXIMUM 2 MINUTES
ANY LANGUAGE
ENGLISH SUBTITLES IF NEEDED

LA SFIDA
Realizza o scegli un video di massimo due minuti che racconti una storia sulla pace.

Sono benvenuti:

CHI PUÒ PARTECIPARE?
La call è internazionale ed è aperta a tutte le persone che abbiano compiuto 18 anni.

NON DEVI INVIARCI IL VIDEO

Raccomandiamo di impostare il video come Pubblico, così che possano essere scoperti sia la tua storia sia il tuo lavoro di storyteller.
Il video rimane sul tuo canale.
Il canale rimane tuo.
Il pubblico rimane tuo.
Storytellers for Peace contribuirà a scoprire, selezionare e promuovere storie e storyteller provenienti da tutto il mondo.
POSSO PRESENTARE UN VIDEO CHE HO GIÀ REALIZZATO?
Sì.
Il video non deve necessariamente essere stato realizzato appositamente per questa open call.
Puoi presentare un video nuovo oppure un video già pubblicato, purché rispetti i requisiti della call e tu disponga dei diritti e delle autorizzazioni necessari per partecipare.
Forse hai già una storia che merita di essere raccontata.
LINGUA
I video possono essere realizzati in qualsiasi lingua.
Se il video non è in inglese, deve contenere sottotitoli in inglese.
COME PARTECIPARE
È semplice:

2. Pubblicalo sul tuo canale YouTube.

4. Compila il modulo di partecipazione di Storytellers for Peace.

Tutto qui.

Queste due date rappresentano i due estremi del nostro viaggio.

COSA ACCADRÀ AI VIDEO SELEZIONATI?
Storytellers for Peace selezionerà alcune delle storie ricevute per presentarle attraverso il proprio network internazionale.

Una storia potente è più importante di una produzione costosa.
Non è previsto un premio in denaro.
La principale opportunità consiste nel vedere la propria storia scoperta e promossa attraverso un network internazionale di storyteller.
ENTRA NEL NETWORK

The Material Works Art Award supports artists through a one-time $2500.00 award in exchange for an original artwork that will join our growing contemporary art collection. This award recognizes artistic excellence and aims to promote career advancement through increasing visibility and exposure.
Who can apply:
We are currently accepting applications from artists with contemporary art practices. Visual artists working worldwide in painting, photography, installation, sculpture, drawing, printmaking, mixed-media, experimental, and conceptual art are eligible to apply.
What you get:
The award grants the selected artist $2500.00 based on the merit of their submitted portfolio. The award is exchanged for an original artwork (one of similar monetary value to the award).
This artwork will be negotiated and determined with the selected artist. The artwork joins our collection and is considered for future exhibition opportunities MW will cover shipping costs and details will be discussed with the selected artist.
The selected artist is interviewed about their work and practice with an archived online profile and featured on the social media platforms.

 Spotlight · Open
The Room Next Door
The space just beyond what we see
There is always a room next door: a door left ajar, a window lit across the courtyard, a hallway that turns out of sight, a voice through the wall. We know it is there. We don't know what it holds.
For THE ROOM NEXT DOOR we are looking for photographs that bring the viewer to the edge of a space they cannot fully enter. These are images where something is felt more than shown, where the frame stops just short of an answer, and where what lies beyond is left for the viewer to imagine. The mystery should come from what the photograph withholds, not from what it hides.
We welcome thresholds, doorways, windows, and reflections; interiors seen from outside and exteriors seen from within; neighboring lives glimpsed at a distance; sounds, light, and shadows that arrive from somewhere else; and constructed or staged work that invents what waits on the other side. Documentary, conceptual, and experimental approaches are all welcome. People may appear, but the subject is the space between here and there.
Awards - $1,000 Cash Awards
First Place$500
Second Place$250
Third Place$150
Two Honorable Mentions$50
Human Presence AwardFree entry to a future exhibition of their choice
Cash awards are limited to one per photographer. Should a photographer's submissions be selected for multiple awards, the photographer will receive the award of greatest value only.
Selected Artists Receive
Online exhibition by Decagon Gallery
Publication in a professionally designed exhibition catalog
Digital badges and certificates for exhibiting artists
How to Submit
Open to photographers worldwide. All photographic processes and styles welcome.
Submit JPGs sized to 2100 pixels on the long side, without text, watermarks, or borders. Preferably under 4 MB.
Name files: First Name-Last Name_Title.jpg
You grant Decagon Gallery the right to publish your photograph in the online exhibition, in the exhibition catalog, and to promote the exhibition on social media and in newsletters. Photographers retain all rights, including copyright, to their photographs.
Meet the Juror
Dr. Susan Bright
Dr. Susan Bright (Aus/UK) is a curator, art historian, writer and lecturer with over two decades of experience curating exhibitions featuring both major international and emerging contemporary artists. While maintaining a broad curatorial practice, she specializes in lens-based art and has developed a reputation for strong scholarship combined with imaginative, intuitive and rigorous collaboration.
Read full bioShow less
She has been invited to curate exhibitions at prestigious institutions worldwide, including Tate Britain, The National Portrait Gallery (UK), Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna (Italy), Princeton University Art Museum (USA), Lismore Castle Arts (Ireland), Serlachius Museum (Finland), and Fremantle Arts Centre (Australia), among others.
As guest curator and artistic director for festivals across France, Spain and Germany, she has demonstrated versatility and leadership in cultural programming.
She writes extensively on contemporary art, photography and culture. She has authored seven books and regularly contributes to exhibition catalogues, journals, magazines, and broadsheets, including The Financial Times, The Guardian and Vogue. She has written and broadcast for BBC Radio 4.
She has taught at leading institutions including Parsons School of Design in New York and University of the Arts London (UAL). She is frequently invited to deliver keynote addresses at museums and universities internationally and has participated on numerous juries and panels worldwide. Additionally, she consults for brands and organizations on cultural strategies and initiatives.

VisArts Emerging Curator Program 2027 
Application Deadline:  December 18, 2026, Midnight 
VisArts invites applications from emerging curators to work with an experienced mentoring curator to develop and present an exhibition at VisArts in the Kaplan Gallery in the fall of 2027. 
The VisArts Emerging Curator Program offers a unique opportunity for an emerging curator or artist with an interest in exhibition-making or curating to work with an experienced mentoring curator to develop and present an exhibition and to assist in the presentation of the mentor’s exhibition. To develop expanded education programming and enhanced visitor experiences, the 2027 Emerging Curator and the 2027 Mentoring Curator will also focus on developing tools to support public programming that promotes social interaction, creative exchange, and audience engagement. 
VisArts will provide the Emerging Curator with a $10,000 budget to cover exhibition costs and curatorial fees. Additional staff support for printing, promotions, and execution of exhibition programming is available. The program is one year and will begin in January 2027.
International applicants must be eligible to work in the United States. VisArts is unable to provide or assist with visas.
The selection panel includes the VisArts Galleries Director & Curator, Artist Advisory Council, and the 2027 Mentoring Curator.
VisArts is a nonprofit arts center in Rockville, Maryland. We’re the largest visual arts organization in the area and an active, significant presence in the greater metropolitan arts community. Our contemporary art galleries, artist studios, and 355 POD Space Gallery are located in Rockville Town Square, a thriving gathering place for the local community. VisArts presents exhibitions of contemporary art in our five galleries, along with related programs and events. We also offer Emerging Curator and Studio Artist Programs along with art classes and VisAbility Art Lab, our supported studio for adult emerging artists with disabilities.
2027 Mentoring Curator: Fabiola R. Delgado 
Fabiola R. Delgado (b. Cabimas, Venezuela) is an interdependent curator and creative producer based in Washington DC. Formerly a Human Rights lawyer and political asylum seeker from Venezuela, her practice is shaped by a commitment to justice, engaging questions of power, memory, objecthood, and social responsibility, with a main focus on migrant and diasporic narratives. Her work spans exhibitions, scholarship, editorial projects, and public programming for all ages.
She’s collaborated with institutions such as the Hirshhorn Museum, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Smart Museum of Art, National Museum of American History, Anacostia Community Museum, Brooklyn Museum, Washington Project for the Arts, Transformer, Cervantes Institute NY, and Times Square Arts. Her projects have been featured in The New York Times, The Washington Post, Hyperallergic, and BmoreArt Magazine, among other publications.
Curatorial Collaboration 
During the yearlong program, the curatorial team (mentoring curator and emerging curator) will: 
Conduct curatorial research
Develop a cohesive and compelling exhibition proposal
Develop writing skills for catalogs and other printed and online materials
Develop budgets for executing exhibitions and exhibition programming
Communicate with artists and lending institutions, developing contracts and loan information
Design and implement educational exhibition programming and outreach activities that engage artists, curators, and public audience of all ages
Develop sponsorship/fundraising initiatives to support the exhibition programming (if needed)
Oversee exhibition design and installation
Develop marketing and public relations materials in support of the exhibition, such as press releases, website + social media content, and print media
The VisArts Emerging Curator Program provides emerging curators with practical, hands-on experience at a community arts organization. It’s designed to support diverse exhibitions presenting a broad spectrum of ideas and curatorial approaches. In addition, it enhances the VisArts exhibition experience by developing educational opportunities, public programming, and opportunities for community engagement through expanded use of interactive interpretive media. 
Application 
Applicants don’t need to have a fully realized curatorial proposal, but we’re interested in getting a sense of your interests, tastes, and sensibilities. The formal proposal will be developed with the support and guidance of the 2027 Mentoring Curator and the Galleries Department.
To apply online, create a Submittable account and complete the form. 
Submission Requirements 
1. Application form 
2. CV 
3. Evidence of past curatorial projects: 
Up to 10 still images
Up to five minutes of video and audio tracks
List of images with artist name, title, year, medium, and descriptive information
Supporting PDF documents
4. A statement that addresses the following: 
What makes presenting an exhibition in a nonprofit community arts center with the guidance of a mentor an ideal opportunity?
What do you hope to achieve with this exhibition and mentoring program?
What do you consider your curatorial intentions or interests in regard to exhibition-making?
How do you envision enriching the audience experience?
How would you engage the community?
What sorts of programming and content delivery would you like to see paired with exhibitions?

VisArts is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit. Our mission is to transform individuals and communities through the visual arts.
A hub for artistic exploration and social impact since 1987, VisArts brings people together through shared creative experiences, including:
Critically acclaimed contemporary art exhibitions, programs + events
Studio Artist and Emerging Curator programs

International Residency Program
The New York Art Residency & Studios (NARS) Foundation International Artist Residency Program supports emerging and mid-career artists working across all disciplines through three and six-month residencies. The program is open to both International and US-based artists, creating a shared space for artistic dialogue and international cultural exchange for an extended period of time.
For International ArtistsFor US-based Artists
About: International Artist Residency 
Our core program, the NARS International Residency Program offers 24/7 access to furnished, private or semi-private studio spaces (250 – 300 sq ft) in our diverse artist community in Sunset Park, Brooklyn. As a studio based residency, the focus is on the artistic process and experimentation that results from working alongside other artists, within New York’s cultural and sociopolitical context.
Residency sessions are offered in one-season, two-season, and four-season terms, lasting approximately three months, six months, and one year, respectively. Actual start and end dates vary slightly based on the residency calendar. Artists meet with 2-3 Studio Visitors each month, gaining invaluable feedback and expanding their network of artists and professionals in New York City and internationally. Residents are provided with administrative, curatorial, and professional support to explore and expand the scope of their artistic practice through research, dialogue, and production of new projects. Presentation opportunities include a curated exhibition in the NARS gallery, bi-annual Open Studios, through which artists can introduce and share research and work through artist talks, discussions, screenings, workshops, and performances.
Residency artists benefit from a community driven program and ongoing dialogue with fellow residency artists through weekly informal gatherings, inter-studio visits and activities, as well as field trips and meals together. Residents also have the advantage of working alongside emerging and established NYC based artists in our studio facilities, who retain space year round. The program and facilities are designed to form a community, foster the expansion & exchange of artistic and cultural practices, and provide artists with exposure to New York and its art scene.
Please note: The studio is a work space only — housing is NOT provided.
‍
‍
ASAP
ASAP is our weekly community gathering, hosted by two paired artists each week. Artists lead the group in inquiry-based activities such as art-making, reflection, or conversation. ASAP gives the majority international cohort an opportunity to foster cross-cultural exchange and share different traditions, perspectives and creative practices. 
Each season, the NARS Curatorial Fellow leads an ASAP session, thoughtfully crafting an experience that reflects their engagement with the artists in residence. The Curator is also an active participant in ASAP, attending weekly and contributing to the ongoing exchange.
Past ASAPs have included mind mapping, drawing sessions, a pickleball tournament, discussions at Sunset Park, screenings, craft making, artist-led conversations ranging from aspects of creative life to reflecting on personal growth, and more. These gatherings may relate to an artist’s practice or not at all. They are a dedicated space to explore, question, dissect, and share, all while strengthening the cohort’s sense of community.
‍
ASAP stands for many things:
Artists Sitting and Pondering 
As Slow as Possible 
Artists Sharing Artists Practices
A Space for Art and Play 
Artists, Space, Action, Process
‍
‍
‍
‍
‍
‍
‍
‍
‍
NARS Artists Present: An Offering for the Public
To create connection between our community and artists-in-residence, we organize the NARS Artists Present: An Offering for the Public event each season. In close collaboration with our Curatorial Fellow, the artists conceive and produce a vibrant series of activities, meant to invite participants to engage with their creative process and offer a unique window into their work. We encourage the artists to stretch beyond their studios and consider how their work may be activated and shared.
‍
Artist Salon
Our Artist Salon is designed as an informal gathering where artists and curators may share their work and cultivate meaningful relationships. The Salon offers the opportunity for our artists-in-residence and Curatorial Fellow to engage with the artists and curators showing work in our exhibitions program and, more broadly, across our larger network. While we prioritize currently exhibiting artists and curators to foster closer engagement with and crossover between their work and our residents, the Salon also welcomes NARS alumni, artists-in-residence from fellow programs in New York City, and independent artists.
‍
Studio Visitor Salon
Throughout each residency season, NARS facilitates one-on-one studio visits between our artists-in-residence and curators, fellow artists, writers, educators, and other professionals from across the art world. These studio visits are part of our ongoing commitment to network our residents into the New York art scene by fostering dialogue and connection. Our Studio Visitor Salon offers a unique opportunity for deeper engagement between our residents and these art professionals. 
For the Studio Visitor Salon, we invite one professional to return after their studio visits to connect with the full artist-in-residence cohort, as well as our Curatorial Fellow, in an informal, salon-style setting. The Salon begins with a walkthrough of the residency exhibition guided by our Curatorial Fellow, who works closely with our artists-in-residence to showcase their work in this exhibition. After the walkthrough, everyone gathers for a conversation to reflect on the exhibition and the many facets of being an artist in the twenty-first century.
‍
Makerspace NYC | NARS Residency Program
In partnership with our friends at MakerSpace NYC, NARS is thrilled to offer select artists-in-residence free 11-week Pro memberships each season.
What residents will receive: Participants will enjoy all the benefits of a Pro Membership including full access to the metalshop, woodshop, machine shop, sewing room, laser cutters, 3D printing and electronics room for an 11-week period and discounted access to our pottery studio. All members must show proficiency on any machine in the shop before use. As part of the membership, some specialty (non-BUS) classes are available to residents at 50% off the member ticket prices on a case by case basis. Some equipment requires an additional fees.
‍
For additional information or questions, please contact residency@narsfoundation.org 
‍
NARS residency programs are, in part, supported by public funds from the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs and City Council Member Alexa Avilés.

Selected artists will have their work exhibited in a public cultural venue in central Paris during QIANKUN 2027. They will be invited to the opening reception and may participate in artist meetings, guided tours and cultural discussions. Artists will receive a participation certificate and exhibition documentation, including photographs. 
Selected works may also be offered for sale during the exhibition. Artists may benefit from editorial and media promotion in France and internationally, as well as potential future collaborations with artists, curators and cultural partners.

Accueil
QIANKUN 2027 OPEN CALL
QIANKUN 2027 OPEN CALL
 QIANKUN 2027 — Lancement officiel de l’appel international à projets artistiques
Nous invitons chaleureusement les artistes et créateurs du monde entier, issus de différentes cultures, disciplines et parcours artistiques, à participer à un dialogue artistique international autour des questions de genre, d’identité, de corps, de pouvoir, de culture et de diversité du vivant.
À travers la peinture, la photographie, la vidéo, l’installation, l’art numérique, l’art performatif, le son, la performance et les pratiques interdisciplinaires, les artistes sont invités à proposer des œuvres explorant les multiples façons dont les individus se construisent, évoluent et interagissent avec le monde qui les entoure.
L’exposition aura lieu en février 2027 à Paris, en France. Elle est organisée par l’Association Esthétique de l’Est (EDE) et sera ouverte gratuitement au public.
À propos de QIANKUN
Créé en 2022, QIANKUN（乾坤） est une plateforme internationale d’art contemporain basée en France. Le projet explore les liens entre la philosophie orientale, la création artistique contemporaine et les grandes questions sociales, culturelles et humaines de notre époque.
Le terme « QIANKUN » (乾坤) trouve son origine dans le Yi Jing (易经), ou Livre des Transformations, un classique majeur de la pensée chinoise traditionnelle.
Dans cette philosophie, Qian (乾) et Kun (坤) ne représentent pas deux entités fixes et opposées, mais symbolisent une relation dynamique entre le Yin et le Yang : une interaction permanente, une transformation continue et une recherche d’équilibre.
Selon cette vision, la différence n’est pas nécessairement source de conflit. Elle peut devenir un espace de dialogue, d’évolution mutuelle et de création d’un nouvel équilibre à travers les échanges et les relations.
À travers le langage de l’art contemporain, QIANKUN souhaite réinterpréter cette pensée philosophique millénaire et la mettre en dialogue avec les questions actuelles liées à l’identité, aux expériences individuelles, aux différences culturelles et aux formes de coexistence humaine.
Depuis sa création, chaque édition de QIANKUN développe une thématique spécifique, prenant la philosophie orientale comme point de départ pour explorer les relations entre l’être humain, la nature, le corps, la société et le vivant.
Des premières réflexions autour de :
la relation entre les paysages naturels, le ciel et la terre ;
les cycles de la vie, l’existence et le passage du temps ;
le mouvement, le corps et les expressions artistiques interculturelles ;
QIANKUN poursuit son exploration des grandes expériences communes de l’humanité.
Le projet rassemble des artistes issus de différents pays et disciplines, en créant un espace de dialogue entre philosophie orientale, art contemporain international et problématiques sociales actuelles à travers les arts visuels, les installations, la vidéo, la performance, le son et les pratiques interdisciplinaires.
Thème de l’exposition
Genre : Yin, Yang et les diversités du vivant
QIANKUN 2027 s’inspire de la pensée du Yin et du Yang issue du Yi Jing, afin d’explorer de manière artistique les questions contemporaines liées au genre, à l’identité et aux relations de pouvoir dans nos sociétés.
Dans cette édition, le concept de Yin-Yang ne sera pas réduit à une simple opposition entre « masculin » et « féminin », ni considéré comme une classification fixe et immuable.
Au contraire, l’exposition propose de partir des principes fondamentaux du Yin et du Yang — interdépendance, transformation permanente et coexistence dynamique — afin de repenser les différentes formes d’équilibre et de déséquilibre dans le monde contemporain.
Elle invite à réfléchir aux relations en constante évolution :
entre les individus ;
entre les êtres humains et la société ;
entre les corps, les identités et le monde qui nous entoure.
Axes de réflexion proposés
L’exposition souhaite notamment explorer, sans limitation :
L’évolution du féminisme et des rôles sociaux attribués aux femmes ;
La diversité des identités de genre et des expressions de genre ;
Les expériences vécues et les expressions culturelles des personnes LGBTQIA+ ;
La reconstruction des identités masculines et l’évolution des rôles sociaux des hommes dans les sociétés contemporaines ;
Les relations entre corps, pouvoir, famille, travail, traditions culturelles et normes sociales ;
Les questions d’identité, de migration et d’appartenance dans des contextes interculturels ;
Les liens entre expériences individuelles et structures sociales ;
Les différences, les relations, la coexistence et les nouvelles formes d’équilibre.
QIANKUN 2027 ne cherche pas à opposer les différents groupes sociaux ni à défendre une vision unique du genre.
Nous considérons que les différences ne constituent pas nécessairement une source de conflit. Elles peuvent au contraire devenir une force permettant aux différentes expériences humaines de dialoguer, d’évoluer ensemble et de s’enrichir mutuellement.
L’art offre un espace où ces expériences diverses peuvent être visibles, exprimées et questionnées.
Appel à participation — Artistes recherchés
Nous recherchons des œuvres qui témoignent d’un regard personnel, d’une observation sociale et d’une démarche artistique indépendante.
Les artistes peuvent répondre directement aux notions de « Yin-Yang », « genre » ou « identité », mais peuvent également partir de leur propre expérience de vie, de leurs relations familiales, de leur rapport au corps, de leur héritage culturel, de leurs observations sociales ou de leurs recherches artistiques personnelles afin de proposer une interprétation singulière du thème.
Les œuvres n’ont pas besoin d’apporter une réponse définitive.
Elles peuvent être :
un souvenir personnel ;
une expérience corporelle ;
une observation de la société ;
une réflexion sur les traditions et les normes culturelles ;
une nouvelle imagination des espaces publics, des structures identitaires ou des relations humaines futures.
Nous accordons une attention particulière aux éléments suivants :
le lien réel et pertinent entre l’œuvre et le thème de l’exposition ;
l’originalité du langage artistique développé par l’artiste ;
la diversité des expériences issues de différents contextes culturels et sociaux ;
la capacité à comprendre la complexité des questions liées au genre ;
une réflexion approfondie sur le corps, l’identité et les relations sociales ;
les pratiques expérimentales et interdisciplinaires ;
les nouvelles créations et projets de recherche développés par de jeunes artistes.
Cette édition prévoit d’inviter plusieurs dizaines d’artistes internationaux issus de différents pays et cultures. À travers une grande diversité de médiums artistiques, leurs œuvres dialogueront dans un même espace d’exposition afin de créer des rencontres et des échanges.
Public concerné
Cet appel à projets est ouvert à l’international.
Les candidats doivent être âgés de 18 ans ou plus.
Aucune restriction de nationalité, de lieu de résidence, de formation artistique ou de niveau d’expérience n’est appliquée.
(Les artistes de moins de 18 ans sont invités à suivre l’appel à participation du programme QIANKUN YOUNG.)
Sont invités à participer :
artistes professionnels ;
jeunes artistes et créateurs indépendants ;
étudiants en écoles d’art et jeunes diplômés ;
chercheurs et praticiens interdisciplinaires ;
designers, photographes et créateurs vidéo ;
artistes du mouvement, de la danse, du son et de la performance ;
acteurs culturels travaillant sur les questions de genre, d’identité, de corps et de société ;
artistes individuels et collectifs artistiques.
Types d’œuvres acceptées
Toutes les pratiques artistiques sont acceptées, notamment :
peinture à l’huile, acrylique, aquarelle, peinture à l’encre ;
dessin, bande dessinée, gravure et techniques mixtes ;
photographie ;
sculpture et installation artistique ;
vidéo, cinéma expérimental et œuvres audiovisuelles ;
art numérique et nouveaux médias ;
créations artistiques utilisant l’intelligence artificielle comme outil de création ;
art performatif et performances en direct ;
art sonore, musique et créations interdisciplinaires ;
danse, théâtre et créations scéniques ;
artisanat traditionnel et réinterprétation contemporaine des savoir-faire culturels ;
projets participatifs, interactifs ou immersifs.
Les œuvres déjà réalisées ainsi que les projets en cours de création sont acceptés.
Chaque candidat peut soumettre jusqu’à trois œuvres.
Informations générales de l’exposition
Nom de l’exposition
QIANKUN 2027 — Exposition d’art contemporain
Thème
« Genre : Yin, Yang et les diversités du vivant »
Le genre : Yin, Yang et les diversités du vivant
Dates de l’exposition
Du 15 au 27 février 2027
Lieu
Centre Paris Anim’ Jacques Bravo
14-18 Rue de la Tour des Dames
75009 Paris, France
Situé dans le 9ᵉ arrondissement de Paris, à proximité de l’Opéra Garnier et des Galeries Lafayette, le lieu est un espace culturel public parisien dédié aux activités artistiques, culturelles et citoyennes.
Accès au public

Before you apply.
 Everything you need to know before submitting your work for review.
 Who can apply to the London open call?
Emerging, independent and mid-career artists working in painting, photography, sculpture, textile, digital art, illustration, mixed media, installation, printmaking, video art and related visual practices can apply.
 Do you accept photography submissions?
Yes. Arrival Gallery accepts fine art photography, documentary photography, portrait photography, conceptual photography, street photography and experimental photographic work.
 Do you accept digital art and video art?
Yes. Digital artists, video artists, motion artists, illustrators, graphic artists and screen-based artists can submit. Digital works may be considered for screen display, digital showcase or selected exhibition formats.
 Do you accept oil painting and traditional artwork?
Yes. Artists working with oil painting, acrylic painting, watercolour, drawing, pastel, charcoal, printmaking and works on paper are welcome to submit.
 Is every artist accepted?
No. Submissions are reviewed before selected artists receive the full exhibition details and confirmation steps. This helps keep the programme considered and avoids overcrowding the showcase.
 Is there a participation fee?
You can submit your work first. If selected, you’ll receive the full details, including the format, fee and preparation requirements, before confirming your place.
 Can I apply for more than one city?
Yes. Artists can be considered for the wider Arrival Gallery international programme, including London, Athens, Brighton, Lisbon, Madrid, Manila, Osaka, Milan and other city opportunities.
 What happens after I submit?
Our team reviews your submission. If your work is selected, you’ll receive the next steps, available routes and confirmation details for the London showcase.

Royal Society of British Artists
Artists are invited to submit work for exhibition alongside members of the Royal Society of British Artists at the RBA Annual Exhibition 2027
The Royal Society of British Artists invites artists of all backgrounds to submit works in various media, including painting, sculpture, printmaking, and drawing, for the RBA Annual Exhibition 2027.
The Royal Society of British Artists (RBA) is a prestigious art society founded in 1823 as an alternative to the Royal Academy; it champions skill, draughtsmanship and traditional techniques, featuring both members and emerging artists in its annual exhibition at Mall Galleries.
The RBA Annual Exhibition offers major cash awards, art materials and framing prizes, media features, and more, to recognise and reward talented artists from anywhere in the world. This includes The Huaicun Zhang Award for Excellence, an award of £10,000 for a work (or works) of exceptional quality. 
Successful applicants can expect:
• To have their selected work included in the RBA Annual Exhibition at Mall Galleries, in the gallery, and online
• Eligibility to win prizes and awards, worth over £15,000
• An invitation to the Private View
• The chance to sell their work
• To be part of a network of exhibiting artists dating back to 1823 when the Society was founded
‘With such a wealth of talent and support, the future looks exceptionally bright for the Royal Society of British Artists. Join us in celebrating the power of art and creativity!’ - Michael Harrison, RBA President 
Submissions are ONLINE ONLY and open from 7 September 2026 to 8 January 2027
 Submit Now
Prizes & Awards
The RBA offers significant prizes and awards:
The Huaicun Zhang Award for Excellence 2027
An award of £10,000 will be offered for a work (or works) of exceptional quality. The selection committee reserves the right to split the award as is deemed appropriate for works in the exhibition.
The de Laszlo Foundation Award
£2,000 awarded to an artist aged 35 or under for the best work from life, plus four Highly Commended awards of £300 each
The Michael Harding Awards
Two prizes of £500 worth of art materials
The Daler-Rowney Award
£500 of art materials from Daler-Rowney for an outstanding work
The John Lynn Commemorative Award for a Young Artist £500
Ronald Benham Memorial Award
An annual memorial prize of £500 in the name of Ronald Benham RBA NEAC, to be awarded to an artist for work painted in a traditional manner in celebration of the natural world
The Winsor & Newton Award
Art materials to the value of £500 for an outstanding painting
Frinton Frames Award
£300 of picture framing at Frinton Frames
The MONTOOLI Award
A prize of £300 for an outstanding portrait painting in the exhibition. The name of the award is derived from a Bengali word which means, "A paintbrush from the creative heart”.
The Peter Kelly Commemorative Prize £300
The Gordon Hulson Memorial Prize
£250 for draughtsmanship, variety and exploration
The Ronald Morgan Memorial Award £250
The Stuart Southall Print Prize £250
The President's Award
Ten free submissions to exhibitions by the Federation of British Artists at Mall Galleries for a non-member exhibitor
Nathan David Award for Sculpture £150
Painters Online Award
The winner will be featured in The Artist magazine. Sponsored by Painters Online, the home of Leisure Painter and The Artist.
The Dry Red Press Award
The winning work will be published as a greetings card
Key Dates
Submissions open: Monday 7 September 2026, 12 noon
Submissions close: Friday 8 January 2027, 12 noon
Notification of selection: Friday 15 January, 12 noon
Receiving Day (if selected): Saturday 13 February, 10am to 5pm
Exhibition opens: Thursday 25 February, 10am to 5pm daily
Private View (invite only): Thursday 25 February, 5pm to 9pm, official opening at 6pm
Exhibition closes: Saturday 6 March, 5pm
Collection of unsold work: Thursday 11 March, 10am to 5pm
How to Submit
A single-stage online judging of all submitted works will take place, after which selected works should be delivered to Mall Galleries, London, for inclusion in the exhibition:
• Register or log in to our Open Exhibition Submission System (OESS) to submit between Monday 7 September 2026 and Friday 8 January 2027
Upload your image/s in JPEG or PNG format and under 5MB. One image per submission must be submitted, showing the complete work. An optional two additional images per work may be submitted, showing details, multiple angles, or framing, etc., however this is not compulsory.
The judges will make their decision based on these images, so please ensure that photographs are accurate and show work at its best.
Also required is the title, medium, size (cm), year of completion, and price per work, plus there is the option to add an artwork description.
• Log in to the OESS from 12 noon on Friday 15 January to see if your work has been selected
• If selected, deliver your work on Saturday 13 February, 10am to 5pm, to Mall Galleries, 17 Carlton House Terrace, London SW1Y 5BD
Works should be delivered unwrapped with the relevant form and labels, which are downloadable upon notification of selection.
 Submit Now
Important Information for Artists
Eligibility 
Who may enter?
Any artist aged 18 or over may enter, from anywhere in the world. 
How many works may I enter?
Artists may enter a maximum of six works each, from which up to four works per artist may be selected. 
What type of work is eligible? 
Work must not have been exhibited previously in London.
Works should not be larger than 2.4m along the longest dimension. 
All works must be an original creation by the artist.
Acceptable media: 
Painting, sculpture, drawing and original prints (excluding photography).
Submission Fee
How much does it cost to enter?
There is a non-refundable submission fee of £22 per work, or £14.50 per work for artists aged 35 or under.
The submission fee includes free admission to the exhibition for all entrants (normally £7).
Submission fees support the not-for-profit programme at Mall Galleries. The gallery is home to visual arts charity, the Federation of British Artists (Registered Charity Number 200048).
We have partnered with the Visual Artists Association to offer a Free Artist Resource Pack to all entrants. This includes 'The Artist's Guide to Selling Art on Instagram’ (PDF) and 'Instagram for Art Careers’ (Video Masterclass). Entrants will receive instructions to download the Artist Resource Pack upon notification of selection.
Presentation 
How should I present my work?
Frames or stretchers should be sufficiently substantial to withstand mirror plating with 12mm (size 6) screws.
Artists are advised to use plain, simple framing. 
Metal frames, unprotected glass edges and clip frames are inadmissible. 
Please remove all fittings and fixings from the back of works, for example D-rings and picture wire. This is to prevent damage to other works, and because we will mirror-plate works for hanging. 
Delivery & Collection
Works should be delivered and collected on the specified receiving and collection days via the gallery's rear entrance at Mall Galleries, 17 Carlton House Terrace, London SW1Y 5BD. 
If you are unable to deliver or collect your work, you may send another person on your behalf – this may include an art courier (see below).
Artists are responsible for the costs of delivery and collection.
Delivery
Works should be delivered unwrapped with the relevant form and labels, which are downloadable upon notification of selection.
All packaging must be taken away at the point of delivery. 
Collection
We are unable to wrap works or provide wrapping for works being returned. 
Any uncollected works will be removed from the gallery after the collection day and stored by an independent courier company at the artist's expense. 
If works are not collected within 12 months of the collection day, the gallery will be entitled to destroy, sell, or otherwise dispose of the works without consent, prior notification, or compensation to the artist.

Selection
How are works selected for exhibition? 
The works for exhibition are selected by a committee formed of members of the Society. 
If selected works arrive damaged, with unacceptable framing, size discrepancies from the original submission, or not as shown online, these will be withdrawn and will need to be collected from Mall Galleries by the artist at their expense.
May I ask for feedback?
The decision of the Selection Committee is final and we are unable to offer feedback.
Sales
Does my work have to be for sale?
All work must be for sale.
Once work has been submitted, any sale made by the gallery before or during the course of the exhibition up to and including the collection day shall take precedence and supersede one made privately. Any private sale made in this period will incur the normal commission. 
How should I price my work?
There is a minimum price per work of £300, except for prints – framed £180, unframed £120. (Buyers will not be charged for postage and packaging of unframed prints, so please ensure the price of unframed prints allows for this).
Unless otherwise advised, the gallery will charge a commission on the total price paid for works, including commissioned works, before, during, or as a result of the exhibition. 
The price submitted should be the selling price, which should include commission, and is the price at which the work will be sold.
The price of works must include commission of 45% +VAT (please note that where foundry fees apply, foundry costs will be deducted before commission is calculated). If an artist is registered for VAT, then the VAT due on the selling price of works should be included in the price submitted. 
Mall Galleries reserves the right to query the price of works. 
May I change the price of my work once submitted?
The price of works may only be changed by written agreement between the artist and Mall Galleries. 
How will I know if my work has sold?
You will be notified by Mall Galleries if your work sells. 
I am an international artist, do I need to register for a UK VAT number?
Artists who are not resident in the UK but are resident in the EU or elsewhere are welcome to submit work.
Artists without a UK residence are classified as NETPs (Non-Established Taxable Persons) and must register with HMRC (HM Revenue & Customs) for a UK VAT number in order for their work to be included in the exhibition. If selected for the exhibition, you must supply us with your UK VAT number (or proof of application) before the Receiving Day, otherwise your work may be withdrawn. First Plinth: Public Art Award 2025 Shortlist
The five artists shortlisted for First Plinth: Public Art Award 2025 were Bea Haines MRSS (Winner), Emily Motto, Gabriele Risso MRSS, Olana Light MRSS and Regan Boyce GBA.
The five shortlisted artists made maquettes as part of the final phase of the competition. The maquettes were on show at Dora House as part of the International Sculpture Day on Saturday 26 April 2025 and following the Sculpture Symposium, Bea Haines MRSS was announced as the winner (click here to view).

Recent winners
The winner of the First Plinth: Public Art Award 2025, Bea Haines MRSS was announced on 26 April 2025, at Dora House as part of the Society's marking of International Sculpture Day with a Sculpture Symposium. Bea's winning entry will now start the process of fabrication and will be unveiled at Dora House in 2027.
The winner of the First Plinth: Public Art Award 2023, Madi Acharya-Baskerville MRSS, was announced during the Public Art Symposium, that took place at Dora House on on Saturday 29 April marking International Sculpture Day. Madi's commission was unveiled on 1 June 2024 at Dora House and is at The Art House, Wakefield until July 2025.
The winner of the First Plinth: Public Art Award 2021 was Polly Morgan MRSS and her work Open! Channel! Flow! was on the sculpture terrace at Dora House in 2023 and is now at the Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park until July 2025.
The making of 'The Double Act'
What how 'The Double Act' by Madi Acharya-Baskerville MRSS winner of the First Plinth: Public Art Award 2023 was made.
The making of 'OPEN! CHANNEL! FLOW!'
First Plinth: Public Art Award 2021 winner Polly Morgan MRSS talks about the making of 'Open! Channel! Flow!'
Testimonial
Hear from artist Fabio Lattanzi Antinori MRSS who won the First Plinth Award in 2019 about his experience and why he recommends artists apply.
 Current Winner
 Bea Haines MRSS
Bea Haines MRSS' work often appropriates and manipulates unorthodox materials including dust, human ash, lime scale, snail slime, chewing gum and blood. Transient, taboo or everyday detritus becomes the focus of intense scrutiny or worship. Mundane objects are raised to the status of relics or changed beyond recognition. In this way banal or discarded items are granted a second life. Bea aims to shine a light on the small traces of life that are deeply poignant or represent momentous life events such as birth, love, sickness and death. 
Bea's second child was born unexpectedly on the way to hospital in the passenger seat of her old Honda Jazz surrounded by toys, half eaten snacks and other detritus. In recent years she has been using the everyday materials of family life to reflect on her experience of motherhood.
Bea’s First Plinth sculpture will use reclaimed air bags and her own car to produce an impactful artwork that both celebrates and challenges cars as protective vessels of opportunity, and components of global warming.
Inspired by encounters between forensic science and the domestic environment, my practice explores the human trace, our relationship with everyday objects and the insight these give into human desire, fear and mortality.

What the Streets Hold
What becomes visible when no one is performing
 Photograph: Leroy Skalstad
A person can enter a photograph without ever knowing it. They may be going home, avoiding someone, carrying good news, or thinking about a life that is invisible to everyone around them. The photograph cannot tell us the whole story. But sometimes it catches the moment when something private appears in public.
WHAT THE STREETS HOLD is an open call for street photography. We are interested in what people reveal without intending to: how they wait, protect themselves, occupy space, move toward one another, or remain separate while standing side by side.
The photographs may be made on streets, in stations, markets, public transport, neighborhoods, or anywhere strangers temporarily share the same place. A person may be central to the image, barely visible, or present only through what they have left behind.
We are not looking only for dramatic events, visual coincidences, or perfectly timed gestures. We are looking for photographs that make us pause because something in them feels known — even when we cannot fully explain what happened.

Royal Institute of Painters in Water Colours
Artists are invited to submit work for exhibition alongside members of the Royal Institute of Painters in Water Colours at the RI Exhibition 2027
The Royal Institute of Painters in Water Colours (RI) seeks the best in contemporary watercolour and water-based media painting for the RI 215th Exhibition.
The exhibition is the largest of its kind, featuring over 400 works from around the world. Alongside the work of its elected members, leading figures in contemporary watercolour and water-based media, the RI welcomes both emerging and established artists who push the boundaries of the medium through traditional and experimental approaches.
'Founded in 1831 on principles of inclusivity, the RI has long provided a platform where artists at different stages of their careers can exhibit side by side. That ethos remains central to the Institute’s work today.' - Juliette Losq PRI, President
Successful applicants can expect:
• To have their selected work included in the RI 215th Exhibition at Mall Galleries, in the gallery, and online
• Eligibility to win prizes and awards worth over £15,000
• An invitation to the Private View
• The chance to sell their work
• To be part of a network of exhibiting artists dating back to 1831 when the RI was founded
Submissions are ONLINE ONLY and open from 12 October 2026 to 22 January 2027
 Submit Now
Prizes & Awards 
There are many prizes and awards available to win:
NEW The Winsor & Newton Award £3,000 cash award, £1,500 of materials, plus a two-day residency valued at £1,000
NEW The Winsor & Newton Materials Prize £1,500 worth of materials
NEW The Winsor & Newton Emerging Artist Award £500 of materials, plus a one-day immersion at the sponsor's London Head Office (valued at £500) to include an archive tour, the opportunity to explore materials research, and a paint-making experience with a specialist chemist
NEW The YUPO Co-creator Prize £500 awarded at the judges’ discretion to an outstanding work incorporating a YUPO product. The prize is open to RI members and non-members.
The Baohong Artists' Watercolour Paper Prizes Two prizes of £250 worth of watercolour paper, awarded to a member and non-member for excellence
The Cass Art Colour Award £200 of art supplies from Cass Art, awarded to a work demonstrating innovative use of colour
The Chaoshan Watercolour Award £250 for the best classically inspired watercolour
The David Barker Award Two prizes of £1,000 each – one for an RI member and one for a non-member. The prizes will be awarded to works created from observed experience, with the condition that recipients commit to using the award to further their artistic development and education by undertaking residencies or courses of their choice.
The Debra Manifold RI Memorial Award Presented by the Linda Blackstone Gallery, an award for the most innovative work in the exhibition
The Dry Red Press Award The winning work will be published as a greeting card in the Dry Red Press 'Prize Winners' range, with royalties from the sale of the cards going to the artist
The Escoda Barcelona Award A set of Escoda's finest brushes for an outstanding landscape painting
The Frank Herring Easel Award An easel presented by Frank Herring & Sons for an outstanding work
The James Fletcher-Watson RI Award £500 for the best use of watercolour in the exhibition
The John Purcell Paper Prize Paper to the value of £100, awarded by John Purcell Paper
The Michael Harding Award A varied selection of Michael Harding watercolour sets
The President’s Choice Award An award of £750
The RI Young Artist Award sponsored by Daler-Rowney £1,000 and art materials to the value of £1,000 RRP to be awarded to an artist aged between 18 and 25
The Richard Plincke RI Prize for Colour An award of £250 for creative use of colour
Subject to final confirmation
Our exhibitions invite you to experience the creativity and diversity of watercolour in all its forms
 Juliette Losq

 President
Key Dates
Submissions open: Monday 12 October 2026, 12 noon
Submissions close: Friday 22 January 2027, 2pm
Notification of selection: Friday 5 February, 12 noon
Receiving Day (if selected): Saturday 13 March, 10am to 5pm
Private View (invite only): Tuesday 23 March, 5pm to 8:30pm, official opening at 6:30pm
Exhibition opens: Wednesday 24 March, 10am to 5pm*
*Closed on Easter Sunday 28 March and Easter Monday 29 March
Exhibition closes: Saturday 10 April, 5pm
Collection of unsold work: Thursday 15 April, 10am to 5pm
How to Submit
A single-stage online judging of all submitted works will take place, after which selected works should be delivered to Mall Galleries, London, for inclusion in the exhibition:
• Register or log in to our Open Exhibition Submission System (OESS) to submit between Monday 12 October 2026 and Friday 22 January 2027
Upload your image/s in JPEG or PNG format and under 5MB. One image per submission must be submitted, showing the complete work. An optional two additional images per work may be submitted, showing details (including framing if applicable).
The judges will make their decision based on these images, so please ensure that photographs are accurate and show work at its best.
Also required is the title, medium, size (cm), year of completion, and price per work, plus there is the option to add an artwork description.
• Log in to the OESS from 12 noon on Friday 5 February to see if your work has been selected
• If selected, deliver your work on Saturday 13 March, 10am to 5pm, to Mall Galleries, 17 Carlton House Terrace, London SW1Y 5BD
Works should be delivered unwrapped with the relevant form and labels, which are downloadable upon notification of selection.
 Submit Now
Important Information for Artists
Eligibility 
Who may enter?
Any artist aged 18 or over may enter, from anywhere in the world. 
How many works may I enter?
Artists may enter a maximum of six works each, from which up to four works per artist may be selected. 
What type of work is eligible? 
Works must have been completed within the last three years.
Works should not be larger than 240 cm high and 150 cm wide including the frame. The Selection Committee has the right to exclude paintings that are over this limit.
All works must be an original creation by the artist.
Acceptable media: 
Watercolour or water-soluble mediums including watercolour, watercolour pencil, acrylic, ink or gouache (excluding water-soluble oils) on any appropriate support.
Please specify the type of support (for example paper, board, wood, parchment, etc) as well as the medium.
Submission Fee
How much does it cost to enter?
There is a non-refundable submission fee of £22 per work, or £14.50 per work for artists aged 35 or under.
The submission fee includes free admission to the exhibition for all entrants (normally £7).
Submission fees support the not-for-profit programme at Mall Galleries. The gallery is home to visual arts charity, the Federation of British Artists (Registered Charity Number 200048).
We have partnered with the Visual Artists Association to offer a Free Artist Resource Pack to all entrants. This includes 'The Artist's Guide to Selling Art on Instagram’ (PDF) and 'Instagram for Art Careers’ (Video Masterclass). Entrants will receive instructions to download the Artist Resource Pack upon notification of selection.
Presentation 
How should I present my work?
All paintings must be well presented, and should be suitably framed (no metal or clips frames are permitted) and glazed with picture glass (except in special circumstances as below, or by prior arrangement with the RI).
Glazing in perspex and other similar transparent acrylic materials may be accepted, but only on works arriving from abroad or large works in frames exceeding 100 cm on the longest side.
All works submitted to the exhibition should be framed unless there is a genuine aesthetic or technical reason for the work to remain unframed. If entering unframed work, please indicate it will be unframed in the artwork description. Artists entering unframed work do so at their own risk.
Frames or stretchers should be sufficiently substantial to withstand mirror plating with 12mm (size 6) screws.
Artists are advised to use plain, simple framing in a light or medium colour. 
Please remove all fittings and fixings from the back of frames, for example D-rings and picture wire. This is to prevent damage to other works, and because we will mirror-plate works for hanging. 
Delivery & Collection
Works should be delivered and collected on the specified receiving and collection days via the gallery's rear entrance at Mall Galleries, 17 Carlton House Terrace, London SW1Y 5BD. 
If you are unable to deliver or collect your work, you may send another person on your behalf – this may include an art courier (see below).
Artists are responsible for the costs of delivery and collection.
Delivery
Works should be delivered unwrapped with the relevant form and labels, which are downloadable upon notification of selection.
All packaging must be taken away at the point of delivery. 
Collection
We are unable to wrap works or provide wrapping for works being returned. 
Any uncollected works will be removed from the gallery after the collection day and stored by an independent courier company at the artist's expense. 
If works are not collected within 12 months of the collection day, the gallery will be entitled to destroy, sell, or otherwise dispose of the works without consent, prior notification, or compensation to the artist.

The works for exhibition are selected by a committee formed of members of the Institute.

Royal Society of Portrait Painters
 The RP exhibition is an annual opportunity for artists who paint people to see their paintings hung alongside the work of their peers. As always, emerging and established talent is displayed together.
 Anthony Connolly
 -
 President
Artists are invited to submit work for exhibition alongside members of the Royal Society of Portrait Painters at the RP Annual Exhibition 2027
The Royal Society of Portrait Painters invites artists around the world to submit portraits for its annual exhibition. The Society welcomes paintings, drawings and original prints from artists aged 18 and over, in the UK and internationally.
Selected artists will have their work exhibited in a prestigious showcase at Mall Galleries, London, at which a number of works will sell and a number of commissions will be placed.
The total prize fund is over £35,000, including The William Lock Portrait Prize (£20,000).
Successful applicants can expect:
• To have their work included in the exhibition at Mall Galleries and online
• The opportunity to win prizes and awards
• An invitation to the Private View
• The chance to sell their work and/or receive commissions 
• To be part of a network of exhibiting artists dating back to 1891, when the Society was founded
• The possibility of election to membership
Submissions are open from 2 November 2026 to 2 February 2027
 Submit Now
Prizes & Awards
The exhibition offers prizes and awards worth over £35,000:
The William Lock Portrait Prize
£20,000 for the most timeless portrait with a real feeling for paint and its aesthetic potential. Plus two special mention prizes of £2,500 each.
The Almenara Collection Award
A £5,000 purchase prize will be awarded to a picture which is for sale (at a price not exceeding £5,000) and which, in the opinions of the nominated RP panel and representatives of the Almenara Collection, is agreed to be a worthy addition to the Almenara Collection
The Faringdon Prize
£5,000 for the most distinguished drawing in the annual exhibition
The de Laszlo Foundation Award
£3,000 for the most outstanding portrait by an artist aged 35 years or under, plus four Highly Commended awards of £500 each
The Raw Umber Studios Prize
Raw Umber Studios believes that the most exciting contemporary portraiture lies at the intersection of technical excellence and creative expression. Their annual prize, inaugurated in 2023, encourages and rewards such work. Value £2,000.
The RP Prize for the Best Small Portrait
A prize of £2,000 for the best small portrait in the exhibition, measuring not more than 38 x 30.5 cm (15 x 12 inches) unframed
Daler-Rowney Materials Prize
Daler-Rowney materials to the value of £1,000 will be awarded to the artist who in the opinion of the judging panel has submitted a picture to the annual show which is exceptional, either in terms of its imaginative response to the sitter or its technical achievement
Subject to final confirmation
Key Dates
Submissions open: Monday 2 November 2026, 12 noon
Submissions close: Tuesday 2 February 2027, 12 noon
Notification of pre-selection: Wednesday 10 February, 12 noon
Receiving Day (if pre-selected): Saturday 27 February, 10am to 5pm
Notification of final selection: Tuesday 2 March, 12 noon
Collection of unaccepted work: Thursday 4 March, 10am to 5pm
Private View (invite only): Wednesday 5 May
Exhibition opens: Thursday 6 May, 10am to 5pm
Exhibition closes: Saturday 15 May, 5pm
Collection of unsold work: Thursday 20 May, 10am to 5pm
How to Submit
All work must be submitted online. Pre-selection from online entries will take place, after which pre-selected works should be delivered to Mall Galleries, London, for final selection (with the exception of International Artists*):
• Register or log in to our Open Exhibition Submission System (OESS) to submit between 12 noon on Monday 2 November 2026 and Tuesday 2 February 2027
Upload your image/s in JPEG or PNG format and under 5MB. One image per submission must be submitted, showing the complete work. An optional two additional images per work may be submitted, showing details (including framing if applicable).
Please ensure that photographs are accurate and show work at its best.
Also required is the title, medium, size (cm), year of completion, and price (if for sale) per work, plus there is the option to add an artwork description.
• Log in to the OESS from 12 noon on Wednesday 10 February to see if your work has been pre-selected
• If pre-selected, deliver your work for final selection on Saturday 27 February, 10am to 5pm, to Mall Galleries, 17 Carlton House Terrace, London SW1Y 5BD
Works should be delivered unwrapped with the relevant form and labels, which are downloadable upon notification of pre-selection.
• Log in to the OESS from 12 noon on Tuesday 2 March to see if your work has been selected
• If unaccepted, collect your work on Thursday 4 March, 10am to 5pm
*International Artists: All international submissions will be selected ONLINE ONLY, therefore international artists will need to ship their work to the gallery if selected only, on a date to be announced
 Submit Now
Important Information for Artists
Eligibility
Who may enter?
Any artist aged 18 or over may enter, from anywhere in the world. 
How many works may I enter?
Artists may enter a maximum of four works each, from which up to three works per artist may be selected.
What type of work is eligible? 
The Society welcomes paintings, drawings and original prints (including digital/iPad prints). Sculpture and photography are not admissible.
Works should be based on a sitting or study of the human figure from life. We understand that artists may use photographs for assistance but the primary source should be from life.
Works must have been completed in the last three years and not been exhibited in London previously.
Works should not be larger than 2.4m along the longest dimension. 
All works must be an original creation by the artist.
May I apply for membership of the Society?
Any artist is eligible to apply to become a candidate for membership of the Society, provided their work is selected into the annual exhibition and they have registered their intent to apply.
To find out about the application process and the roles and responsibilities of membership, please read more here.
Submission Fee
How much does it cost to enter?
There is a non-refundable submission fee of £22 per work, or £14.50 per work for artists aged 35 or under.
The submission fee includes free admission to the exhibition for all entrants (normally £7).
Submission fees support the not-for-profit programme at Mall Galleries. The gallery is home to visual arts charity, the Federation of British Artists (Registered Charity Number 200048).
We have partnered with the Visual Artists Association to offer a Free Artist Resource Pack to all entrants. This includes 'The Artist's Guide to Selling Art on Instagram’ (PDF) and 'Instagram for Art Careers’ (Video Masterclass). Entrants will receive instructions to download the Artist Resource Pack upon notification of pre-selection.
Presentation
How should I present my work?
Frames or stretchers should be sufficiently substantial to withstand mirror plating with 12mm (size 6) screws.
Artists are advised to use plain, simple framing. 
Metal frames, unprotected glass edges and clip frames are inadmissible. 
Please remove all fittings and fixings from the back of works, for example D-rings and picture wire. This is to prevent damage to other works, and because we will mirror-plate works for hanging. 
Delivery & Collection
Works should be delivered and collected on the specified receiving and collection days via the gallery's rear entrance at Mall Galleries, 17 Carlton House Terrace, London SW1Y 5BD. 
If you are unable to deliver or collect your work, you may send another person on your behalf – this may include an art courier (see below).
Artists are responsible for the costs of delivery and collection.
Delivery
Works should be delivered unwrapped with the relevant form and labels, which are downloadable upon notification of selection.
All packaging must be taken away at the point of delivery. 
Collection
We are unable to wrap works or provide wrapping for works being returned. 
Any uncollected works will be removed from the gallery after the collection day and stored by an independent courier company at the artist's expense. 
If works are not collected within 12 months of the collection day, the gallery will be entitled to destroy, sell, or otherwise dispose of the works without consent, prior notification, or compensation to the artist.

Selection
How are works selected for exhibition? 
The works for exhibition are selected by a committee formed of members of the Society. 
If works arrive damaged, with unacceptable framing, size discrepancies from the original submission, or not as shown online, these will be withdrawn and will need to be collected from Mall Galleries by the artist at their expense.
May I ask for feedback?
The decision of the Selection Committee is final and we are unable to offer feedback.
How are the prize winners selected?
The prize winning works are selected in time for the awards ceremony during the Private View, prior to the exhibition opening to the public. 
Sales
Does my work have to be for sale?
Although the exhibition is an excellent opportunity to sell work, works may be listed as not for sale.
Once work has been submitted, any sale made by the gallery before or during the course of the exhibition up to and including the collection day shall take precedence and supersede one made privately. Any private sale made in this period will incur the normal commission. 
How should I price my work?
If for sale, work must have a minimum sale price of £300 (framed prints: £180, unframed prints £120 - buyers will not be charged for postage and packaging of unframed prints, so please ensure the price of unframed prints allows for this).
Unless otherwise advised, the gallery will charge a commission on the total price paid for works, including commissioned works, before, during, or as a result of the exhibition. 
The price submitted should be the selling price, which should include commission, and is the price at which the work will be sold.
The price of works must include commission of 45% +VAT. If an artist is registered for VAT, then the VAT due on the selling price of works should be included in the price submitted. 
Mall Galleries reserves the right to query the price of works. 
May I change the price of my work once submitted?
The price of works may only be changed by written agreement between the artist and Mall Galleries.

The Drawing Year
