Overview
The Drawing Year is our full-time, full-scholarship postgraduate-level programme. It is designed for artists and creatives who wish to engage in creative exploration and critical enquiry, and discover how drawing can further enrich their practice. 
30 selected students benefit from 3.5 days of skills-based tuition a week from distinguished teaching and visiting artists, access to their own dedicated studio space, a lecture programme, professional development guidance and the opportunity to exhibit in a series of end-of-year public exhibitions. 
Places are offered on portfolio and interview. The programme has no fees, and living grants are available. Our Alumni programme offers teaching, residency and exhibition opportunities. 
 Introduction from our Founding Artistic Director 
The Royal Drawing School started The Drawing Year, its postgraduate programme dedicated to drawing from life in 2000. It is unique in the spectrum of tertiary level art education in the UK. 
The Drawing Year is a course of study at postgraduate level which provides an opportunity for intensive research and practice in drawing from observation. It sees drawing both as an end in itself and in relation to other areas of practice. 
Drawing can be direct, incisive, intimate, surprising, funny or confrontational. Using the most limited of means, it offers some of the most demanding opportunities for growth to a contemporary artist, both visually and intellectually, allowing a free transition between mediums. It is one of the simplest and yet the most endlessly complex of human activities, encompassing a wide scope of practice and interpretation. 
The Royal Drawing School provides a supportive and lively environment for sustained exploration in drawing, in the belief that practice strengthens hand and eye, and concentration nourishes the imagination. 
Drawing Year students benefit from working amongst peers and from the contact with tutors and visiting lecturers, who represent a wide spectrum of artistic practice. Both students and faculty value the freedom of intellectual exchange and the atmosphere of shared commitment. Drawing is a primary language natural to all human beings. At the Royal Drawing School, it is taught as a way of thinking, seeing and understanding. Fundamental to the course is the assertion of the connection between looking and making images; a belief that conceptual innovation can be generated by an active engagement with the visual world that surrounds us. 
Drawing connects what we see with how we think. It is a crucial meditation between the world and our idea of it. More flexible than language, drawing has the power to express thought in a new way, to communicate with economy and authenticity. 
Catherine Goodman LVO CBE, Founding Artistic Director
 Graduate recognition and impact
Since its inception in 2000, more than 550 people have completed The Drawing Year programme. Past students have won high profile awards, including the John Moores Painting Prize, BP Portrait Award, Jerwood Drawing Prize, and The Ondaatje Prize for Portraiture amongst others, as well as being exhibited in the Bloomberg New Contemporaries, Whitechapel Open, Royal Academy’s Summer Exhibition, Threadneedle Prize, Frieze, the Liverpool Biennial, the Wellcome Collection, the Royal Collection, the National Portrait Gallery, and The British Council.
 Thinking of applying?
 Register here to receive updates about open days, application support, deadlines and more.
Programme details
Structure
The Drawing Year is a full-time, 16-month programme: 
Three 10-week terms (September 2027 – June 2028) 
Summer break (July–August 2028) with the opportunity to attend a Summer Painting Residency 
Final term (September- December 2028) dedicated to studio and professional practice 
Flexible Course Selection 
During the first three terms, students curate their own learning path from over 50 available courses, all led by our expert faculty of practicing artists. Each student participates in a minimum of 3.5 days of courses per week, ensuring a well-rounded and intensive experience. 
Core Programme Day 
Alongside their chosen courses, students take part in the Core Programme day, where all Drawing Year students come together once a week. These sessions explore a broad range of artistic approaches, subjects, and themes, while also fostering collaboration and critical discussion through forums, tutor-led critiques, and peer-to-peer feedback. 
Studio Space & Independent Practice
From Term 2 onwards, students receive a free dedicated studio space, where they can focus on developing their individual practice. Studio access continues throughout the summer break and into the final term, allowing uninterrupted creative development in preparation for the end-of-year exhibitions. 
 Tutorials
Drawing Year students have two one-to-one tutorials each term with members of faculty. Tutors visit students in their studio spaces to look at drawings and other ongoing work. 
In addition to these regular faculty tutorials, students benefit from special sessions with visiting artists. Past guests have included Hurvin Anderson RA, Celia Paul, and Daniel Crews-Chubb, offering students insight into their contemporary practice and creative processes.
 Lectures and forums 
Our lecture and in-conversation series introduce students to leading artists, writers, art historians and creatives. Past speakers have included; Chantal Joffe RA, Lynette Yiadom-Boakye, Hans Ulrich Obrist, Sir Peter Blake CBE RDI RA and Denzil Forrester MBE.
 Professional development 
The professional development programme brings together a wide range of industry experts who offer advice on aspects of professional practice, helping to prepare students for life as practicing creatives after The Drawing Year. 
 Study trips
Special access and trips to museums, galleries and exhibitions are planned throughout the year. 
 Summer painting residency
All Drawing Year students are invited to attend a funded summer painting residency alongside tutors. Most recently students have visited Borgo Pignano in Tuscany, Italy
 Three exhibitions
At the end of the programme, students of The Drawing Year present their work across two selling exhibitions and a Studio Show, introducing their practices to collectors, supporters, and new audiences. The largest is the 'End of Year Exhibition', held in December at the School’s gallery studio, showcasing over 500 works that demonstrate the range and ambition of the cohort.
A curated selection is previewed in November at 'The Best of The Drawing Year' at Christie’s, giving graduates prominent exposure in Mayfair. 
Running alongside the main show in December, the 'Studio Show' invites visitors into the artists’ working environments at SPACE studios, providing direct insight into their developing practices. Together, these exhibitions form an important platform for presenting the varied output produced across the year.
 Akilah Chambers
 I Long For A Reflection
 Keziah Mornin
 Do What You Feel
Curriculum
Courses are divided into three main areas: 
Drawing in the Studio 
The studio is a constant source of inspiration and is transformed into something different with every tutor. Working from the model, students will explore subjects including narrative and storytelling, costume and stage, portraiture and anatomy, memory and imagination. 
Drawing from Art
Students get face to face with some of the world’s most remarkable collections. Through focused study, they gain a deeper understanding of the works and discover how drawing from art can inspire and enrich their own practice. 
Drawing London
Students will be challenged to take work out of the studio and into the dynamic city, which is in continual flux. Drawing by day and night, students will see the architecture, the people, even the flow of traffic, with new eyes. 
Imagination
Woven throughout the curriculum, with dedicated courses emphasising imaginations role in observational drawing. Students are encouraged to explore how imagination enhances perception, drawing, and learning, opening up new creative possibilities. 
Printmaking 
Seen as an extension of drawing, these courses also form part of the curriculum. Students will have the opportunity to explore intaglio techniques with an emphasis on etching.
Facilities
The Royal Drawing School is located in Shoreditch, London. The converted 19th-century warehouse house includes spacious drawing studios, gallery spaces and a fully equipped intaglio print room. Learn more about the facilities.
Students’ individual studios are situated at SPACE studios in Hackney, a short journey from the school. They are purpose-built, with natural light, and accessible 24 hours a day, 7 days a week throughout the year, including holiday periods.
 There are so many classes, opinions and lessons to be learnt that I am quite excited to see in several years what the lasting lessons will be. But I think for now the most important lesson is in the doing, not the thinking and to let the work lead the way and not intervene too much with what I think it should be or what I’ve done before.
Isaac Heard

Alumni opportunities
Our alumni are a valued part of our artistic community. There are many opportunities to stay in touch with and be supported by the School.
Visit our alumni opportunities page.
 Funded residencies
National and international residencies created for Drawing Year alumni take place in countries such as Scotland, Wales, Italy, France, Switzerland, USA, Jamaica, Antigua and India. 
See more details about the residencies here.
 Tutor training
Tutor training with our Young Artists programme is a way to gain financial support and professional development as you continue to cultivate your practice. Many alumni also go on to teach on the School’s Public Programme. 
 Alumni exhibitions
Alumni are invited to exhibit in the School’s annual exhibition programme in the UK and abroad.
 Paid commissions
The School offers alumni commercial opportunities with external partners. Recently, alumni have worked with Hauser & Wirth and the Peninsula Hotel, London. 
 Alumni network
The School has a vibrant network of alumni who frequently collaborate on projects and exhibitions. We keep in touch regularly with news of residencies, competitions, exhibitions and paid opportunities.
 Discounted courses
Alumni receive a discount of 50% on term-time courses at the School, so graduates can continue to develop their practice with us and benefit from the support of our tutors.
Our students come from a variety of backgrounds and disciplines and each has their own unique experience on the year. Watch them describe how the Drawing Year has changed their practice.
Watch more videos
Funding
There are no fees for The Drawing Year; every student offered a place is awarded a full scholarship. 
London Living Grant 
This grant exists to support students who are relocating to London and those in financial need. Selected students may be eligible for a single grant of £3000 awarded before the start the course. 
Bursaries 
Each term students can apply to the School for a limited number of bursaries, which are means-tested. There is also a Financial Support Fund available should students find themselves in financial difficulty during the course.

6okken-residency-2027-at-the-foot-of-mt-.text:
6okken is an artist-run residency in Oishi, a small village on the north shore of Lake Kawaguchi at the foot of Mt. Fuji, about two hours from Tokyo by bus.
Each resident or group has a whole house with its own kitchen and bathroom, in a cluster of six houses where our members also live and work. Terms are 26 nights, eleven times a year. Applications are open year-round, at least 60 days before the start date. Artists of every discipline are welcome, on their own, in pairs or with family.
Who can apply:
Artists, writers, curators and researchers of any nationality and discipline, at any stage of their career. Individuals, pairs, small teams and families with children are welcome. We speak English and Japanese.
What you get:
A whole house for each resident or group (kitchen, bathroom, Wi-Fi), a shared studio, an online meeting before arrival, pick-up from Kawaguchiko Station with a welcome lunch, chat support during the stay, and a car ride up to twice a week for shopping and research. 
We are glad to write invitation letters and letters of support for grant applications. There is no required final presentation.
Entry Fee:
There is no application fee. Applications are open year-round.
280,000 JPY per 26-night term for the first person (320,000 JPY for summer terms 6 to 8), plus 100,000 JPY for each additional person.
This covers the house, utilities and staff support (heating oil in winter is charged at cost).
Travel, food and materials are covered by the artist.
Deadline 31 May 2027
Organiser: 6okken
Locations: East Asia

cove-park-residency-2027-2028-artists-sc.text:
Cove Park: Residency 2027–2028 for Artists in Scotland, UK, Central and South America and Diasporas (UK)
Cove Park’s year-round residency programme welcomes local, national, and international artists, creative practitioners, and researchers. The fully funded Awarded Residencies are due to be programmed between May 2027 and December 2028 and can be for as short a time as two weeks or up to three months in duration. Artists, creative practitioners, writers and researchers working in all art forms and at every career stage are welcome to apply.
The Awarded Residencies will be offered to individuals and collaborators who urgently require the time, care, financial support, and facilities offered to develop their creative practice. A final presentation or participation in a public event is not a requirement, but Cove Park aims to support those who wish to work within and contribute to a community of residents, and to benefit from the experience of working alongside others engaged in a wide range of specialisms.
For 2027 and 2028, these residencies are open to individuals, collectives, and collaborative groups based in Scotland and the UK and in Central and South America. Artists from the Central and Sound American diaspora based in Europe and North America are also welcome to apply. People born in Scotland, but living elsewhere in the world, may also apply.
The appointed residents will receive a fee (775 GBP per week), funding for travel (65–1,250 GBP), and, when required, for materials (up to 150 GBP), access support, and the visa application process.
There is also an Application Access Bursary. This funding is for those who experience barriers to the application process due to disability and neurodivergence. This funding can be used to pay a support worker to help with the process (requests to be made by 30 November 2026).
Deadline: 11 December 2026

Our mission is to support the activities and protect the interests of our members and other creative individuals in the arts, develop the art field and promote awareness of art, and contribute to the sustainable development of Estonian

Vision
The EAA is a modern and developing organisation operating in a balanced and effective way to contribute to the sustainable development of Estonian art and culture. EAA membership card
The EAA issues IAA cards (the International Association of Art acting under the auspices of UNESCO) to its members, which give artists membership in the largest international network of professional artists and entitle them to numerous discounts in museums and galleries around the world.
The membership card is issued upon the admission of a member. The card is valid for five years and can be extended by sending a relevant request to the EAA secretary together with a digital portrait photograph or a printed photograph submitted at the EAA office.
Discounts and exemptions from entrance fees can be checked here.
All EAA members also receive a KuKu club card that entitles the holder to discounts at the G-Galerii art supplies shop, KuKu club and Tuum café.

Table of Contents
CTM Festival Open Call
The CTM Festival open call for In Listening 2027 invites artists working with experimental sound practices and audio art to propose new hybrid works that combine a live presentation with an original radio production. Two selected projects will each receive a €6,000 commission, production support, travel to Berlin, and accommodation during the festival period. The commissioned works will premiere during CTM Festival 2027 in Berlin before being developed into a radio work for Deutschlandfunk Kultur. Applications close September 6, 2026, at 23:59 (UTC+2).

CTM Festival Open Call Snapshot
What: In Listening 2027 is an open call for two newly commissioned hybrid works that combine a live presentation with an original radio production. Projects must be grounded in experimental sound practices and audio art and respond to the CTM Festival 2027 theme, Process…ing.
Who: Artists working with experimental sound practices and audio art. Individual artists, duos, and groups may apply. Applications must be submitted in English.
Where: Berlin, Germany.
Award / Support: Two commission fees of €6,000 each; technical and staging costs for the CTM presentation following discussion with CTM; technical and staging costs for a possible presentation at ORF musikprotokoll im steirischen herbst following discussion with the organizer; possible radio production support from Deutschlandfunk Kultur, including translation, voiceover, and recording studio costs following discussion; travel to Berlin; accommodation during the production and festival period; production support and counseling from CTM Festival and Deutschlandfunk Kultur.
Application Fee: FREE
Deadline: September 6, 2026, 23:59 (UTC+2, Berlin Time)
Official Link:
https://www.ctm-festival.de/festival-2027/open-calls/in-listening-2027
Strategy Coach Notes: https://www.patreon.com/pformart/posts/ctm-festival-000-166036415
Get the Application Strategy
The In Listening 2027 commission asks applicants to develop a project that functions successfully in two distinct formats: a live presentation and an original radio work. Successful applications will demonstrate a clear artistic concept, an understanding of listening as the central medium, and a realistic production plan that aligns with the technical framework described in the call. Practitioner Members receive Strategy Coach Notes that examine the application materials, production requirements, reviewer priorities, and practical strategies for developing a competitive proposal.
Get The Strategy
About the CTM Festival Open Call
The In Listening 2027 commission expands on the long-running collaboration between CTM Festival, Deutschlandfunk Kultur, and ORF to support new work that exists in two distinct forms: a live presentation and an original radio production. Rather than asking artists to adapt an existing project, the call invites proposals conceived from the beginning as hybrid works. Applicants are expected to consider how listening changes across physical and broadcast environments and how each format can become its own artistic experience. The selected works will premiere during CTM Festival 2027 in Berlin before continuing as radio productions for broadcast through Deutschlandfunk Kultur and presentation through ORF platforms.
The 2027 edition is organized around the festival theme, Process…ing, which examines movement, transformation, and systems through sound. The call asks artists to engage directly with this theme while remaining grounded in experimental sound practices and audio art. Sound must function as the primary artistic medium. Live presentations are designed for a shared listening experience within the Kuppelhalle at silent green, where audiences sit around the performers inside a 6.1-channel loudspeaker configuration. The accompanying radio work should not function as documentation of the live presentation. It should instead be developed as an independent work that takes advantage of the possibilities offered by broadcast listening.
What Is Offered
Two commission fees of €6,000 each
World premiere during CTM Festival 2027
Technical and staging costs for the CTM presentation, following discussion with CTM
Technical and staging costs for a possible presentation at ORF musikprotokoll im steirischen herbst, following discussion with the organizer
Possible production support from Deutschlandfunk Kultur, including translation, voiceover, and recording studio costs, following discussion
Travel expenses to Berlin
Accommodation during the production and festival period
Production support, counseling, and assistance from CTM Festival and Deutschlandfunk Kultur
Broadcast through Deutschlandfunk Kultur’s Klangkunst program
Presentation through one or more ORF platforms
Online streaming through Deutschlandfunk and ORF platforms for at least one year
Who Should Apply
This opportunity is intended for artists whose practice is rooted in experimental sound and audio art. Individual artists, duos, and collaborative groups are eligible to apply. Projects should place sound at the center of the artistic experience and demonstrate how the proposal will function as a live event and as an original radio work. Applications must be submitted in English. Artists proposing collaborative projects should identify one primary contact for the application and develop a realistic production plan that reflects the available commission.
CTM Festival Open Call Timeline
Application Deadline: September 6, 2026, 23:59 (UTC+2, Berlin Time)
Applicants Notified: Mid October 2026
Production Period: Late October 2026 through January 2027
CTM Festival 2027: January 22 to January 31, 2027
Deutschlandfunk Kultur Broadcast: Spring 2027
ORF Presentation: Autumn 2027
Why This Opportunity Matters
Few international commissions ask artists to develop a project simultaneously for live presentation and radio broadcast. The structure encourages applicants to think beyond documentation and to consider how listening changes across different contexts. Artists selected for In Listening 2027 receive financial support together with production guidance from three established cultural organizations working across contemporary sound, experimental music, and radio. The opportunity offers time to develop a new work, present it within an international festival, and extend its reach through public broadcast and online distribution.
Apply
Applications must be submitted through the official CTM Festival application portal before September 6, 2026, at 23:59 (UTC+2, Berlin Time).
Official Link: https://www.ctm-festival.de/festival-2027/open-calls/in-listening-2027

Two projects will be selected for presentation in Arraiolos, Portugal, between May and July 2027.

Open Call Portugal Snapshot
What: International Open Call for Performance Projects
Who: Artists and collectives from any disciplinary field, 18+
Where: Arraiolos, Alentejo, Portugal
Award / Support:
– €1,500 Artist Fee
– €500 Production Grant
– Accommodation
– Workspace
– Equipment Access

– Website Inclusion
– Catalogue Inclusion
– Documentary Inclusion

Residency Duration: Public presentations take place May–July 2027.
Deadline: July 3, 2026, 11:59 PM (Mainland Portugal Time)
Official Link: https://www.cortexfrontal.org/performance
Strategy Coach Notes: https://www.patreon.com/posts/strategy-coach-159873170
Get The Application Strategy
This opportunity appears straightforward at first glance, but the regulations reveal a highly focused curatorial and evaluation framework. The jury is selecting only two projects. Applicants are competing for a small number of presentation slots inside a biennial connected to Évora_27 European Capital of Culture. The strongest applications will demonstrate a clear relationship between the existing performance and the thematic framework of topophilia, place, territory, memory, and lived experience.
Strategy Coach Notes break down how the jury is likely to evaluate quality, thematic relevance, adaptation to Arraiolos, work sample selection, project framing, and interview preparation. Members receive access to detailed application analysis designed to help artists build stronger submissions.
Get The Strategy
About the Open Call Portugal
Hypertextile 2027 is the inaugural edition of the Alentejo Contemporary Art Biennial. The event is integrated into the official cultural program of Évora_27 European Capital of Culture and will take place in Arraiolos, a town internationally recognized for its centuries-old textile traditions.
The biennial uses textiles as a curatorial lens through which artists can reconsider relationships to territory, place, memory, labor, identity, and community. This edition is organized around the concept of topophilia, developed by geographer Yi-Fu Tuan, which describes the affective relationship between people and place.
Unlike many open calls focused on development or research, Hypertextile is seeking projects that already exist. Selected works must demonstrate artistic maturity and previous public presentation experience. The organizers emphasize conceptual clarity, artistic consistency, technical feasibility, and adaptability to the local context.
Only two projects will be selected, creating a highly competitive process that favors applications with strong alignment to the biennial’s curatorial framework.
What Is Offered
€1,500 artist fee
€500 production grant
Accommodation during presentation period
Workspace
Access to available equipment
National or international round-trip transportation
Inclusion in Hypertextile website
Inclusion in Hypertextile catalogue
Inclusion in Hypertextile documentary
Inclusion in communication and promotional materials
Who Should Apply
This opportunity is best suited to artists and collectives who already have a completed performance project and are seeking international presentation opportunities.
Projects should have a demonstrated public life and a clear artistic identity. The jury is specifically seeking performances capable of engaging questions of place, territory, memory, identity, and lived relationships to environments. Artists whose work explores social, political, emotional, ecological, or sensory connections to place may find strong alignment with the curatorial framework.
The call is open internationally and welcomes artists from any discipline working through performance.
Timeline
Application Deadline: July 3, 2026, 11:59 PM (Portugal)
Interviews with Pre-Selected Applicants: July 6–10, 2026
Selected Artists Announced: July 13, 2026
Public Presentations: May–June 2027
Why Open Call Portugal Matters
Many performance open calls support research or development phases. Hypertextile 2027 is focused on presentation. The biennial is investing directly in finished work and providing resources to bring artists to Portugal for public engagement with international audiences.
The connection to Évora_27 European Capital of Culture increases visibility for participating artists and places selected projects within a broader international cultural program. For artists already touring completed work, this opportunity offers funding, presentation support, travel assistance, and institutional visibility through a major biennial framework.

call-for-submissions-the-11th-cica-new-m.text:
The 11th CICA New Media Art Conference 2027 and the annual publication “New Media Art 2028.” Accepted presenters will have the opportunity to present and exchange ideas with peers. Presenters and exhibitors who participate on-site will be featured in the book “New Media Art 2028,” scheduled for publication in December 2027. The book will be distributed through major bookstores in Korea and made available internationally via the CICA Press website.
Please note that all presenters are required to register upon acceptance and attend the conference in person. The registration fee ($430 USD) directly contributes to fostering diversity, inclusion, and cross-cultural exchange.
Who can apply: CICA Museum invites writers, scholars, researchers, and artists worldwide to participate in the 11th CICA New Media Art Conference 2027 and the annual publication “New Media Art 2028.” 
What you get: Exhibition, Publication, Conference. 
Deadline 04 November 2026
Organiser: CICA Museum

virtual-open-days-west-dean-college-3cda.text:
Discover studying at West Dean from wherever you are with our programme of Virtual Open Days. 
Explore courses across Arts, Crafts, Conservation and Design, and find out more about the subjects that interest you. Our online sessions offer the opportunity to hear from tutors and students, learn more about the courses and student experience, and ask questions about studying at West Dean. 
Whether you're considering your next step in education, looking to develop your creative practice or exploring a future in conservation, our Virtual Open Days are a chance to discover more about the opportunities available. 
Sessions cover a range of subjects and course levels, with dates and times varying by event.

What you get: Explore courses, hear from tutors and students, and find out about admissions, funding and how to apply. 
Deadline: Dates vary by session. Please check the event listings and register in advance.

art-exhibition-common-things-36bcc2.text:
Common Things explores how familiar objects, materials and everyday experiences shape the way we see, remember and understand the world. It asks how ordinary things can carry memory, identity and social meaning, and how artists can transform the familiar into powerful intellectual and emotional experiences.
Who can apply:
Open to artists and creative practitioners working across all media, including painting, photography, sculpture, ceramics, textiles, installation, sound, moving image, digital media, performance, architecture, design, research and interdisciplinary practices.
What you get:
Curated physical exhibition in central London
Official programme and exhibition website listing
Permanent online artist profile
Individual pre-exhibition artist feature
Opportunities for curatorial critique and critical review
Professional photography and exhibition documentation
Press release and media promotion
Printing, framing, mounting and display support where required
Professional installation and spatial planning
Technical equipment and support for digital and moving-image works
Professionally produced wall texts and labels
Private view and networking opportunities with collectors, curators and industry professionals
Artwork sales and collector network access
Artists retain 90% of artwork sales
Market guidance and long-term online presence
Official invitations and letters of recommendation
Entry Fee: 
Fees start from £30, with the final amount depending on the specific artworks and requirements. For more information, please contact the organiser.
Deadline 13 November 2026
Organiser: spira9art
Locations: United Kingdom

winter-short-courses-at-west-dean-4c2934.text:
Discover a season of creativity with West Dean’s programme of short courses this winter. From painting, printmaking and textiles to jewellery making, ceramics and traditional crafts, there are opportunities to explore a new creative interest, develop existing skills and learn something new under the guidance of expert tutors.
Courses take place at West Dean’s West Sussex campus, nestled in the heart of the South Downs, and its London campus in Bloomsbury. With opportunities for a range of interests and experience levels, there's something for everyone.
For seasonal inspiration, West Dean’s Winter Warmers programme (27–29 November) brings together a selection of hands-on creative courses, including festive jewellery making, pastels, calligraphy, embroidery and willow weaving. Participants can enjoy a creative break, with complimentary entry to the West Dean Christmas Market included.
Who can apply:
Courses are available to adults of all experience levels, unless otherwise specified on individual course listings.
What you get:
A varied programme of in-person creative short courses, with expert tuition. Course fees and availability vary.Courses run throughout the winter season. Individual course dates, availability and booking deadlines can be found online.
Deadline 29 November 2026
Organiser: West Dean 
Locations: United Kingdom

screen-south-showcase-artists-2026-7-ope.text:
Screen South is seeking applications from artists and creatives working with digital, immersive, sound, interactive or technology-based creative practice. We are looking for projects already in development that require support to reach completion and public presentation, exhibition or distribution. Ten selected artists will receive a tailored package of support, with applications invited in two rounds during 2026-27 
Who can apply: Artists and creatives based in South East England (excluding London) who use, or would like to use, digital tools within their creative practice. We welcome proposals across visual, sound-based, immersive and interactive work. Applicants must have already started their project, have a clear route to completion, and be able to deliver exhibition, showcase or distribution outcomes within six months. This opportunity is not intended for early-stage concepts and is unlikely to support linear film projects 
What you get: Ten selected artists will receive tailored support based on project needs. This may include access to Screen South's equipment (including cameras, computers and VR kit), studio facilities, technical and project advice, exhibition opportunities, marketing support and financial bursaries of up to £1,500. Support is designed to help projects overcome barriers to completion and reach exhibition, showcase or distribution. 
Deadline 30 March 2027
Organiser: Screen South
Locations: United Kingdom
